_meta.source: KI-NRT's FlyerTalk 'Japan Luxury Ryokans' thread + TripAdvisor + Japanese booking sites

inns.name: Myoken Ishiharaso

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Based on our otherworldly stay in December of 2021, in my original post I had Myoken Ishiharaso among my personal top 10 favorite ryokans. After our second visit there last week, nothing has changed my sentiment - in fact, we had an even more phenomenal experience last week, and now it is highly unlikely that it will ever be dislodged from my list.

inns.summary: A 19-room inn on the Amori River at the edge of Kirishima National Park, with hot springs gushing from the rocks and mallards paddling past the baths, which two “otherworldly” stays made a permanent fixture of KI-NRT's personal top ten. Seven springs rise beneath the property and reach the baths untouched by air or tap water, which makes it the most technically obsessive onsen in Japan. The kitchen never repeats a dish, and trilingual attendants like Clement can explain each course and the water itself.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Not a single dish was repeated between KI-NRT's two stays, and he says every course qualifies as a signature dish: a clear soup of sea bream and cabbage wrapped in a sheet of mochi, seared buri raised on black vinegar (quite possibly the best he has had) and a handmade monaka wafer unlike any other. One couple call it the best food they have had at any ryokan, a 2025 guest one of the best meals of his life; one dissenter found dinner unmemorable.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Seven springs rise beneath the property and reach every tub without touching air or tap water (heat exchangers cool the 55°C source), so the carbonated 'Bijin no Yu' keeps its bubbles and mineral film; KI-NRT calls it quite possibly Japan's best onsen technically. There is a communal indoor bath, a mixed outdoor bath by the river, a drinking station and two rental baths, of which Mutsumi no Yu is the one to book. The sauna is tiny.

service.label: Service
service.text: Clement, ten years at the inn and fluent in English, French and Japanese, gave KI-NRT an hour-long education on the spring and typed English menus for another couple; KI-NRT thinks he ought to be made part-owner and recommends asking for him in advance. The room attendant handles every meal and the bath bookings, and a 2025 guest called the service impeccable. The one gripe came from a guest whose English-speaking staff were not Japanese.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are contemporary but warm, and you choose mostly by view. Rurimurasaki, the 120m² top suite, sits on the level closest to the river, though KI-NRT found its wet-room lounge overkill and, like every river room in the main building, it faces Wasure no Sato Gajoen. Hanezu (80m², rebuilt in 2023 with an onsen-steam hammam) faces the street. Kirara in the annex sees only forest; one couple preferred the aged Tsubiya to the modern Suou.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn sits on the bank of the Amori River at the edge of Kirishima National Park, with hot spring water gushing out of the rocks and mallards paddling down the waterfalls a few feet from the baths; one couple found the setting spellbinding. There is no onsen town to stroll and no major sight close by, so KI-NRT suggests it for people who have been to Japan several times, and Wasure no Sato Gajoen sits across the river from the main building.

cities.text: Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho'/'Sakura' Hakata→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h20), change to the JR Nippō line back up to Hayato (~40 min), then the ~15-min inn shuttle to Myoken Ishiharaso (reserve ahead).
Reverse of: ~15-min shuttle to Hayato Stn + JR Nippō to Kagoshima-Chūō (~38 min). By car ~50 min via the Kyushu Expwy (Mizobe IC→Kagoshima IC, ¥1,090) — sea-level, winter-trivial.
Reverse of: Inn pickup to Hayato (~15 min), JR→Kagoshima-Chūō (~40 min), Kyushu Shinkansen→Shin-Tosu, 'Relay Kamome'→Takeo-Onsen, 'Kamome'→Nagasaki. No KOJ→NGS flight exists — rail is the way.

Reverse of: Inn car to Hayato, Nippō line→Kagoshima-Chūō (~35–50 min), 'Sakura'→Kumamoto (~45–57 min). By car ~155 km / ~2h30 up the Kyushu Expwy — ⚠ but the Yatsushiro JCT–Ebino IC tunnel spine is Kyushu's canonical snow-closure section (1–3 preemptive full closures per Jan/Feb season, hours to a day+); on a cold-wave day don't plan this drive — rail it, or take the sea-level R3/E3A west coast (+~1h).

Fly to Myoken: ~90 min up front (hotel→HND + domestic check-in), HND→Kagoshima ~1h45 (~20+ daily), ~45 min on the back end (bags + the ¥450 Myōken route bus ~23 min or a pre-called taxi ~15 min — ⚠ the inn's shuttle-taxi was DISCONTINUED pre-Mar-2026 and called taxis need ~40-min lead, may be refused). 90+105+45 = ~4h door-to-door.
Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen Hakata→Kagoshima-Chūō + JR Nippō to Hayato + inn shuttle to Myoken (~2h45). ~6.5h — a full travel day.

inns.name: Asaba

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Asaba is permanently on my personal list of top ryokans for a multitide of reasons.

inns.summary: A 500-year-old Shuzenji inn that KI-NRT keeps permanently on his list of top ryokans and calls the pinnacle of Japanese architecture, hospitality and cuisine near Tokyo, arranged around a koi pond, a night-lit bamboo grove and a working Meiji-era Noh stage where Living National Treasures still perform. Since the 2023 rebuild every one of the 12 suites has a private onsen and there are no bad rooms left: Hagi and the villa Tenko for brook-side calm, Hagoromo for the stage view.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Izu-rooted kaiseki served in your room: Suruga Bay abalone with its liver sauce over sticky rice, spiny lobster with a broth from the head, and farm wasabi that KI-NRT ate on its own. He calls the food divine, the tried-and-true kaiseki formula done to wonderful effect, and the breakfast dashimaki tamago possibly the best he has ever had. One couple found it a little short of Myoken Ishiharaso; another put it above every Fufu kitchen.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every suite has had its own onsen since the 2023 rebuild (Tenko's is much larger than Hagi's, and Moegi's has no view), so the one communal open-air bath now gets little use. It is a large natural-rock rotenburo on a private stretch of the pond with the bamboo grove beyond, alternating between men and women every few hours, and KI-NRT had it to himself at 4PM and 10PM. Two indoor gender-segregated baths and a family bath complete the set.

service.label: Service
service.text: A kimono-clad nakai-san looks after each room and serves both meals there; KI-NRT's, Noriko, pre-heated his shoes moments before he went out, and he says the Aman ninjas have nothing on Asaba's kimono-clad ladies. It is refined but warm, with no hint of snobbery. The one drawback is English. One couple had requests vanish in translation and called the service good but not great, and a 2025 returnee's bag was nearly left behind at checkout.

room.label: Room
room.text: Twelve suites remain after the 2023 renovation, each with its own onsen, and KI-NRT says there are no bad rooms left. Hagi and the 220m2 villa Tenko are the quiet picks, ground-floor with nothing above them and a babbling brook outside instead of the stage. The rebuilt 126m2 Hagoromo is the modern one to get for the Noh stage, with an open-air bath on the terrace. The futons may be the best one couple ever slept on.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Behind the main building a koi pond holds the Noh stage, brought from Tokyo in the Meiji era, with a waterfall on the left and a bamboo grove and forested hill behind; Living National Treasures perform on it several times a year, and at night it is lit and the bamboo looks otherworldly. Inside is light and airy, with a Lee Ufan mural at the entrance and a 1978 Yayoi Kusama painting in the lounge. Winter leaves the grounds barer and less colorful.

cities.text: 'Kodama'/'Hikari' Tokyo→Mishima (~45-55 min, every ~30 min), then the flat-rate cab into the Shuzenji valley (~40-50 min, book with the room). No self-handled change. Rail alt: Izuhakone Sunzu line→Shuzenji (~35 min) + short taxi, +1 change.

Reverse of: The inn-bookable flat-rate cab Shuzenji valley→Mishima (~40-50 min; Asaba ¥12-15k, book with the room — Asaba runs NO shuttle), then the direct Mishima-calling 'Hikari'→Kyoto (1h50, ~2-hourly, dep Mishima :58 — reserve; hourly 'Kodama'+change fallback). No self-handled change. Rail alt: Sunzu line→Mishima (~35 min), +1 change.

inns.name: Tayuta

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: If another personal top 10 ryokan list ever materializes, Tayuta would comfortably be on it. I am not sure which property would have to make way, but space would be found. It is that good.

inns.summary: A 12-villa Amakusa newcomer, opened in September 2024 by a Kumamoto wedding company with no previous ryokan experience, where every suite runs 86–119 m² with a source-fed golden Kinsen onsen bath and island-dotted sea views, and chef Yuuki Nakano's 16-course dinner left KI-NRT stunned. After one stay in the top suite he called it just about perfect, one of a handful of times he has ever been able to say that, and promised it a comfortable place on any future personal top-ten list.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is 16 immaculately plated courses from chef Yuuki Nakano, haute cuisine KI-NRT could not pin to one label: a foie gras sphere in edible volcanic ash, a sushi course with spectacular Ariake nori and the plumpest tiger prawn he has ever eaten, and then a surprise shio ramen he emptied without hesitation. Breakfast is nearly as ambitious, built around seafood. Reserve Amata, the only private dining room, with counter seating and great views.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every villa has its own free-flowing, source-fed bath of the Kinsen spring, which comes up from 820 metres underground, clear at first and then golden as its iron oxidises (the source is 35°C, so the tubs are heated). Japanese guests praise how gentle the water is on the skin, and KI-NRT counts himself a believer. The Amakusa Suite adds a lovely open-air bath plus a private pool and sauna on the terrace (only it and the Sunset Suite have those).

service.label: Service
service.text: Most of the staff came over from the owner's wedding business instead of from hotels, and they watched over KI-NRT constantly in the best possible way, always nearby and never intrusive. Miki Sato described each dinner course with so much joy she seemed about to eat it herself, kitchen apprentice Koma Toda beamed with pride explaining the breakfast dishes, and the GM was a regular, approachable presence. He puts it beyond omotenashi standards.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 12 villas run from the 86 m² Harbor Suite to the 110 m² Amakusa Suite, which has heated floors, and the roof lines, landscaped grounds and duplex-style villa pairs remind KI-NRT of Kerry Hill's Amanemu. Amanemu keeps the edge indoors, with vaulted ceilings, somewhat more upscale furnishings and lighter tones against Tayuta's darker palette, and the one odd choice in the top suite is a single sink, a small miss in a new luxury build.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The villas sit on Higai-jima in Amakusa, close above the island-dotted sea, with ocean views that KI-NRT thinks beat Amanemu's, and there is a bonfire pit outdoors for chilly evenings. It sits closer to the water than Amanemu (Amanojyaku is closer still, all but hovering over it), and the seascape feels wonderfully immediate. Amakusa is remote, with plenty to do if you have a rental car, and it produces what he calls perhaps the world's best uni.

cities.text: Reverse of: Inn-arranged car Tayuta→JR Kumamoto ~1h (per Tayuta's own access chart) via the Five Bridges + Misumi — coastal, snow-proof — then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Sakura'/'Mizuho' Kumamoto→Hakata (~33 min, every 20-30 min). Rail alt: 20-min taxi/boat→Misumi + JR Misumi line 50 min→Kumamoto (+1 change).

Kyushu Shinkansen 'Sakura' Kagoshima-Chūō→Kumamoto (~48 min), change to the JR Misumi line (~50 min — ⚠ 14-18/day, plan the connection), then the 20-min taxi/boat Misumi→Tayuta (the inn's own access chart; inn-synced Takarajima boat where sailing — Iruka 1/2 suspended Dec–Mar, 3-5 sailings remain). Carless, coastal, snow-proof.

Reverse of: Carless via the Misumi corridor: inn-synced 15–20-min boat/taxi to Misumi, Misumi Line→Kumamoto (~50–60 min), then Shinkansen→Shin-Tosu + Relay Kamome→Kamome to Nagasaki (~2h) — all-rail, snow-proof. Drivers' variant (the ferry drive): ~45 min to Oniike Port, Shimatetsu car ferry→Kuchinotsu (30 min, ~every 45), then ~1h45 down the Shimabara peninsula with Sakitsu Church and the Unzen jigoku en route (~3.5h; winter gales occasionally cancel the strait ferry).

Reverse of: By car ~1h10 via the Five Bridges, Misumi and R57 — coastal and effectively snow-proof. Carless parity (~1¼h): 15-min Takarajima-Line boat Matsushima Port⇄Misumi port (+2-min walk to the station) or 20-min taxi, then Misumi Line⇄Kumamoto ~50–60 min — both Tayuta and Amanojyaku sync pickups. ('Amakusa-gō' rapid bus Matsushima→Sakuramachi BT ~1h20, ~9/day, no reservation.)

No Tokyo→Amakusa flight exists. Fly via Kumamoto: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Aso-Kumamoto (KMJ) ~2h, then ~1.5h taxi/arranged car SW across the Amakusa bridges to Matsushima — Tayuta's official access figure; the inns arrange transfers. Rail-purist alt: KMJ limousine bus→Kumamoto Stn (~1h) + Misumi Line (~50 min) + 15–20-min boat/taxi ≈ same door-to-door. (Connecting via Fukuoka to tiny Amakusa Airport works too but isn't faster.)

inns.name: Takefue

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Even with that said - of all of the ryokans we have ever stayed at, Takefue is our absolute favorite.

inns.summary: A vast, lamp-lit bamboo-forest estate near Kurokawa and KI-NRT's favorite ryokan in Japan across three visits, the rare property that is itself the destination, where a butler of a nakai-san runs everything and every bath is private, though the fully exposed ones can shut in deep-winter snow. One guest proposed here; another left plotting a spring return. At $1,300–$1,800 a night it's priced near the very top of its class, and guests call it worth it.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: KI-NRT has always put the food a small notch below the best ryokan kitchens, though on his 2024 stay the kaiseki was better than he remembered and the desserts the most elaborate he has seen (five pastry chefs for 11 rooms). Two-night guests can order a soft-shelled turtle dinner, and the French toast at the Western breakfast gets raves. Other guests run from the one kaiseki meal to have in Japan to hit-or-miss, with average sushi.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Bathing is all private: every room has its own onsen (Shien-an has four) and three rental baths are booked by the hour. Chikurin no Yu, a big two-part bath in the lit bamboo forest, is the one to book at all costs, and KI-NRT calls it one of the most blissful private open-air onsens anywhere; the pool-sized Chikujo no Ma is for the four special rooms only. Yuzu floats in the tubs at night. Deep-winter snow can shut the fully exposed baths.

service.label: Service
service.text: Your nakai-san is a real butler here: she serves every meal including breakfast, books the rental baths and walks you to them. KI-NRT's, Ms. Funama, had become GM by his third visit, and he puts the staff a close second to Sanso Murata, his best anywhere. When a blizzard caught one couple's rental car, the inn had chains driven up from the nearest town. A one-night guest found the staff stretched, with a 20-minute lull at dinner.

room.label: Room
room.text: The four special rooms (Shien-an, Kokyuan, Tenku and Sayo) are the ones to book, though old-world Omachian holds its own. Shien-an, with a Western bedroom, an irori hearth and four onsen, is one of the grandest rooms KI-NRT has ever stayed in, and one couple called the hardware the best of Asaba, Myoken and Takefue. Its shower and indoor bath sit in a separate unheated building, and two winter guests saw snow blow in through the sliding doors.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: A vast, secluded estate in its own bamboo grove a short drive from Kurokawa Onsen, and the one ryokan KI-NRT would spend all day at without wanting to go out: foot baths along the walkways, free ice cream, and a courtyard whose waterfall and bamboo are lit at night so it looks like something out of a fairy tale. Stone steps rule it out for limited mobility, and one river-loving couple found it less soul-nourishing than its fame suggests.

cities.text: Reverse of: Direct highway bus Kurokawa→Hakata/Fukuoka (~2.5–3h, reserve) — no train changes at all.
Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima-Chūō→Kumamoto (~50 min), then ~2.5h bus/taxi up to Kurokawa Onsen (inn pickup from the bus stop).
Reverse of: Direct highway bus Kurokawa→Hakata (~3h, only 2–3/day — reserve), then 'Relay Kamome'→Takeo-Onsen + 'Kamome'→Nagasaki (~1.4h). January snow can detour the Kurokawa road.

Reverse of: Kyushu Ōdan bus one-seat Kurokawa→Kumamoto Stn (~2h38; 3/day down, only 2/day back up — reserve). Also stops at Kumamoto Airport (~1h50) en route. By car ~77 km / ~1h50 via Senomoto + R57 (or the Milk Road rim), budget 2h15–2h30 in January — the Aso rim roads can gate-close in ice.

Fly via Kumamoto: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Aso-Kumamoto (KMJ) ~2h, then the Sankō bus KMJ→Kurokawa Onsen (~1h50, ~5/day) + inn pickup from the bus stop. Closer than backtracking through Hakata's ~3h highway bus.
Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then the direct highway bus Hakata→Kurokawa Onsen (~2h30–3h, reserve) + inn pickup. ~6.5h door-to-door.

inns.name: Sanso Murata

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: the sum of its parts adds up to it being a Top 10 property in Japan as judged by experts as well as word of mouth in the country. After our experience here, we cannot agree more.

inns.summary: A 12-room Yufuin inn whose plain grounds hide the best service KI-NRT has encountered anywhere in Japan (four staff rushing out with umbrellas in a storm, a butler dedicated exclusively to your room for every meal) and a spectacular kaiseki kitchen that shows off Kyushu's meat, fish and produce. After two nights of "pure bliss" he agrees without hesitation with Japan's own word of mouth that this is a top-10 property in the country. The magic is all indoors, and each of the 12 rooms has its own character.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kaiseki dinner was spectacular on both nights, authentically Japanese but gorgeously presented and prepared to bring out the best in the local, seasonal meat, fish and produce, from the subtle yet complex clear soup (KI-NRT is sure there is something secret in the dashi) to the incredible marinated Oita wagyu. Dinner can be served in your room, and your butler explains each course in detail. He calls it a place that will delight any foodie.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Each of the 12 rooms has its own onsen bath fed by natural hot spring water. KI-NRT's, in Hou, was technically indoors, but the glass doors slide open so it becomes semi open-air, and since it was relatively warm during his April stay it was good to have a breeze flow in from outside while soaking. He calls the onsen wonderful, and for onsen buffs he suggests following a night here with a ryokan in nearby Beppu.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT gives Murata first place for service of every ryokan he has stayed at, with Takefue a close second. Arriving in a storm, four staff rushed out, three with umbrellas and one to park the car (all of 30 meters away), and the next day three more met them in pouring rain. One butler, Aika Goto (with her trainee Aki Nagashima), served their room and only theirs at dinner and breakfast, with no rotation between rooms.

room.label: Room
room.text: Hou is a 155 m2 two-story maisonette (Sou next door is 130 m2): a Western living and dining room, a separate tatami room and the onsen bath downstairs, and the bedroom with two Western beds upstairs. It is tastefully decorated, though the Western furnishings "don't scream high end," and each of the 12 rooms has its own character, Hou and Sou the most modern and Western, so choose carefully. A later guest called Gyo divine.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The grounds are nothing to write home about, serene but neither manicured nor full of character, and there is no great view. The inn sits on a small hill a five-minute drive above Yufuin (one of the top onsen towns in Kyushu) in a sleepy, secluded pocket with few tourists. Galleries and cafes surround it, several owned by Murata, including a soba restaurant a short walk away, and a later guest called the lounge's sound system incredible.

cities.text: Reverse of: Ltd Exp back toward Hakata (~2h10).
Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima-Chūō→Hakata (~1h20), ~4-min platform transfer, then the JR 'Yufu' Ltd Exp Hakata→Yufuin (~2h15). ~3h11 total, all-rail.

Reverse of: By car (~210 km, raw ~2h25 per NAVITIME; budget ~3h): Yufuin IC → Oita Expwy → Tosu JCT → Nagasaki Expwy → Nagasaki IC (~¥5,060). Budget 3h+ in January — the Yufuin IC–Hita IC stretch (~45 km) is an official winter-tire-regulation zone (last winter: 7 days of regulation, 2 of closure); past Hita it's plains, and the Nagasaki Expwy has no regulated section at all. (Transit: Ltd Exp 'Yufu'→Hakata ~2h15 + 'Relay Kamome'/'Kamome' via Takeo, ~3.5h total, 2 changes — 2026-07 audit; rare January snow on the Kyudai line's pass.)

Reverse of: Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin-no-Mori' Yufuin→Kurume (~1h40, ~5/day), Shinkansen Kurume→Kumamoto (~25 min). Scenic alt: the Kyushu Ōdan bus through Kurokawa/Aso, one seat, ~4h15, 3/day. By car ~2.5h via the Yamanami Highway.

Fly to Yufuin: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Oita (OIT) ~1h30 nonstop (frequent ANA/JAL/Solaseed; 2026-07 audit vs flightsfrom/sakuratravel timetables), then a pre-booked FIXED-FARE taxi straight to the inn (~55 min, ¥18,320 incl. tolls — Oita Taxi Assoc., say '定額で') — no bus-schedule or shuttle sync. (Budget alt: airport bus→Yufuin Stn ~55 min, 6/day, ¥1,550pp + the inn shuttle — Enowa's needs reserving ≥3 days ahead.) Far saner than the ~5h45 all-rail haul.

Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin-no-Mori' Hakata→Yufuin (~2h10). ~6h door-to-door. (Oita is Yufuin's own airport but has no Komatsu flight — Hakata is the gateway.)

inns.name: Wabizakura

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: My Top 10 Ryokans Overall (in no particular order): [...] Wabizakura (Kakunodate, Semboku, Akita Prefecture)

inns.summary: A ten-room destination ryokan in the quiet Akita countryside near Kakunodate's samurai district, where the owner drilled 1,000 meters to give a town with no onsen its own hot spring, piped to every room. KI-NRT built an entire trip around it and gave it top honors in Tohoku (by a hair), with kaiseki that produced the best fish dish of his life. Reservations are really difficult to get, and repeat guests keep it that way.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kaiseki is built on local wild mountain vegetables, fish and beef, and KI-NRT found the meals divine. The sake-steamed sea bream head was the single best fish dish of his life, plump and juicy and flavored to perfection, in a town nowhere near the ocean; the rice came steamed with snow crab, whitebait and wild parsley, and the wasabi-leaf jelly was phenomenal. He ranks Wabizakura with the very best ryokan meals he has ever had.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Kakunodate is not an onsen town, and Wabizakura has hot-spring water only because the owner kept drilling until, about 1,000 meters down, he hit a high-quality spring. All ten rooms have a bath fed by it, and KI-NRT must have jumped in and out of his about ten times in one chilly afternoon. The one drawback is that the tubs are not open-air: you slide the glass windows open for a semi-open-air feel instead of a soak in the crisp outdoor air.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT stayed once and praised the serenity and privacy of the place, and guests in the two royal suites (Naotake and Shozan) can have every meal served in the suite's own dining room, which he counts among the luxuries of life, but nobody in the thread has written about the staff themselves.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are warm and contemporary, bright and airy and very tastefully done, with zen Japanese decor and modern comforts: floor heating, auto climate control and the latest washlet toilets. The common areas, by contrast, are very traditional and dimly lit in the Samurai-era manner, but extremely stylish. KI-NRT stayed in Naotake, one of two 81-square-metre royal suites (Shozan is the other) with a dining room for in-suite meals.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Wabizakura is very isolated in the quiet Akita countryside, about ten minutes by car from Kakunodate, the former samurai district that is one of the top cherry-blossom spots in Tohoku (full bloom in 2024 began April 16). The traditional entrance gate and architecture give the property an old-Japan look that is still fresh and modern. There is no garden, though, and the landscaping is not as immaculate as at many other luxury properties.

cities.text: Akita Shinkansen 'Komachi' direct Tokyo→Kakunodate (~3h, one seat). Snow-prone on the single-track stretch past Morioka.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01), cross to a through 'Komachi' Ōmiya→Kakunodate (~2h36; Ōmiya→Morioka ~1h51 + Morioka→Kakunodate ~45 min, one train) + ~12-min taxi. Just one change at Ōmiya despite the length. ⚠ Komachi on snow-prone single track past Morioka.
Reverse of: The price of Akita: 'Komachi' Kakunodate→Tokyo (~3h04), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (~2h15) — the longest leg of any route, on the deep-snow Akita branch; a full travel day.
Reverse of: Akita Shinkansen 'Komachi' Kakunodate→Morioka→Sendai as one through train (~2h05, no change), then a ~12-min taxi/inn car at the Kakunodate end (reserve).

inns.name: Shinsen

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: If it had a real Onsen, I'd definitely find a place for Shinsen comfortably in my top 10.

inns.summary: A family-run 15-room gourmet inn in central Takachiho, spread across three distinct garden areas, where every meal is served in a rotating series of private dining rooms and the caviar comes from its own locally raised sturgeon. KI-NRT counts the cooking among the top dining experiences of his life. The one drawback is that there is no real onsen, only heated baths, and that alone leaves it just outside his national top ten. He has a return booked for late 2026, and a new Beppu annex opening mid-2026 could stretch the staff a little.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: KI-NRT counts Shinsen among the top three dining experiences of his life, potentially number one. The house-brand caviar, from sturgeon raised in Takachiho, was far and away the best he has had, the ayu from the Gokase River was the best of his life, and the wild hamachi sashimi and A5 Ozaki-ranch beef were incredible (Bristom calls the Takachiho beef probably his favorite dish ever). Breakfast is elaborate, though not as memorable as dinner.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no hot spring anywhere on the property, and the private open-air hinoki tub off the Manyo villa runs heated water that the inn says has onsen-like minerals. The bathing itself is still a pleasure, in the open air with a view of the villa's rock garden and easy control of the temperature, and KI-NRT called his terrific while Bristom enjoyed his a lot. One winter guest found the bath thermostat set to 20°C, so check it on arrival.

service.label: Service
service.text: Bristom calls this the most memorable service of all his travels: his host Ms Mirei was there from arrival to departure, serving both meals in the private dining room. KI-NRT found the omotenashi a perfect balance, discreet yet anticipatory, dignified yet down to earth, and everyone from the parking attendant to the okami was lovely. The okami, Kumi Sato, runs a tight ship, and the house is unusually flexible, down to a laundry service.

room.label: Room
room.text: Manyo, the top room, is a detached 100-square-metre villa that KI-NRT found contemporary, luxurious and cavernous, with a bedroom with two double beds, a living room and a tatami room, sliding walls to close each off, a large patio with a zen rock garden beyond it and the open-air hinoki tub to the side. His only nitpicks were a single sink where most top suites have two, and a second toilet in a detached hut in the yard, which he found useless.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The 15 rooms are in three buildings a minute's walk apart in central Takachiho, near the famed gorge, each with its own landscaping: a Ryoan-ji-style dry rock garden fronts the main building, and the Bekkan adds manicured planting and a small red bridge. Every meal is in a different private dining room, and KI-NRT loved a Bekkan room whose window faces a garden lit from the ground at night. The yokagura dance is three minutes' walk away.

cities.text: Direct 'Gokase-go' highway bus Hakata Bus Terminal→Takachiho Bus Center (~3h26, 4/day, reserve). Alternative: Kyushu Shinkansen Hakata→Kumamoto (~50 min) + bus to Takachiho (~3h, 1/day).
Reverse of: Ltd Exp 'Takachiho-gō' bus→Kumamoto (~2h45, only 2/day — plan the day around it), then 'Sakura'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~50 min). January ice can suspend the Aso-rim road.
Reverse of: 'Takachiho-gō' bus→Kumamoto (~2h45, 2/day), Shinkansen→Shin-Tosu, 'Relay Kamome'→Takeo-Onsen, 'Kamome'→Nagasaki — a full travel day.

Reverse of: By car ~85 km via R218 + the free E77 Kyushu-Chūō sections (open since Feb 2024): ~1h45 normal, budget 2h in January. R218 stays off the Aso rim (occasional chain regulation on the Kyushu-sanchi crossing; avoid the higher R325/Takamori route in ice). (Transit: 'Takachiho-gō' express bus→Sakuramachi BT ~2h45, only 2/day — reserve.)

inns.name: Sankara Hotel & Spa Yakushima
inns.summary: A 29-room auberge resort in the foothills of UNESCO-listed Yakushima, with an ocean-view pool and French-inspired cooking, which KI-NRT calls as close to an Aman as a Japan property can get, except that the food is better than at most Amans. There is no onsen anywhere on the property and the rates are steep even for a property of this class, but both of his stays were exceptional ("no aspect of our experience caused a blemish"), he thinks the restaurant ought to have a Michelin star, and he would go back for the food alone.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner at Okas is chef Kenji Hayashi's French-inspired cooking built on local ingredients, and the tasting menu changes completely every day without ever turning rich or heavy, so KI-NRT meant to eat there once and went every evening of both stays. He calls the Pain Rustique the finest dinner bread he has ever had, says Okas ought to have a Michelin star, and until Sanso Amanosato thought this was Japan's best auberge kitchen.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no onsen at Sankara, which KI-NRT calls a pity since top properties usually have one, so the indoor and open-air baths in the Sankara Suite are ordinary hot water. Instead there is a large, beautiful outdoor pool (you see it, and the ocean, from the lobby) and a serious spa, where his masseuse remembered his treatment from two years before. mdlgto, a 2016 guest, adds that the undeveloped tidal onsen elsewhere on Yakushima are magical.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is warm, attentive and refined, at what KI-NRT calls an Aman-like level: airport transfers are complimentary and private, and a fleet of cars can be rented from the hotel by the hour. No butler is assigned, but two years on the staff had kept his preferences, so a bottle of wine was waiting instead of the Champagne they knew he dislikes. Most of the staff were the same on his second visit, which he says speaks well of the management.

room.label: Room
room.text: Book the 104 m² Villa Suite (KI-NRT had Room 10) over the 126 m² Sankara Suite. The Villa Suite is clean, spacious and tastefully furnished, its ocean panorama is unobstructed, and the amenities are top notch down to the toothbrush. The Sankara Suite adds separate living and dining rooms, an open-air bath and a spa room, but roofs sit in its line of sight, and he found the spa room overkill when the actual spa is a short covered walk away.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Sankara sits in the foothills of a mountain range on Yakushima with the ocean below, a Bali-esque resort whose buildings are modern in function but muted and earthy in tone, so they have a sense of place without dominating the landscape. Yakushima itself is a UNESCO World Heritage island, unbelievably green, whose famous moss forests inspired Princess Mononoke, and KI-NRT ranks its scenery and hiking among the most incredible in Japan.

cities.text: Fukuoka City Subway Hakata→Fukuoka Airport (~5 min), JAC direct flight FUK→Yakushima (~1h05, ~1/day — frequently weather-cancelled, keep a backup), then the free hotel shuttle (~40 min, reserve ≥3 days).

Airport limousine bus Kagoshima-Chūō→Kagoshima Airport (~40 min), JAC flight KOJ→Yakushima (~35 min), then the free hotel shuttle (~40 min, reserve ≥3 days). The Toppy/Rocket jetfoil from Kagoshima port (~2h to Miyanoura) is the weather-sensitive sea alternative.
Reverse of: JAC Yakushima→Fukuoka (1/day, ~70 min, weather-prone — keep the Kagoshima fallback), subway→Hakata, 'Relay Kamome'+'Kamome'→Nagasaki (~1.4h). Fallback via KOJ + rail ≈5.3h.
Reverse of: No Yakushima→KMJ flight — JAC→Kagoshima (~35–40 min, ~5/day, the reliable route), limousine→Kagoshima-Chūō (~40 min), 'Sakura'→Kumamoto (~50 min).

inns.name: Fufu Nikko

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: My Top 10 Ryokans Overall (in no particular order): [...] Fufu Nikko (Nikko, Tochigi Prefecture)

inns.summary: Fufu's 24-room Nikko property, opened in 2020 on the old grounds of the Tamozawa imperial villa, gave the town its first true luxury inn, modern and hotel-like where most ryokans are traditional, with an onsen bath in every room and a short walk to Tosho-gu. The flaws are small, a very good kitchen that runs to a Fufu formula and pre-arrival emails that go unanswered, and guest after guest comes away glowing. One couple called it everything a luxury ryokan could and should be, and it has a place on KI-NRT's own top ten.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: KI-NRT called the dinners exceptional and puts them in the top ten of all his ryokan meals, with every ingredient explained by his server Chie Watanabe; his one wish was the option of eating in the room. Two members were cooler on the kaiseki, which a 2023 guest found a bit formulaic and close to Fufu Kawaguchiko's, while the teppanyaki (a huge awabi in 2024) is the dinner members single out. A free champagne hour is included.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own onsen bath, and the two Luxury Premium Suites have both an indoor and an open-air bath fed with free-flowing natural hot spring water, facing the forest with complete privacy even with the curtains up. There are shared baths as well, which a 2023 guest found really amazing, the outdoor one especially, and because everyone bathes in their room they sit mostly empty.

service.label: Service
service.text: Everyone who has stayed reports proactive, attentive service once you arrive: a welcome drink in the lounge at check-in, staff who anticipate what you need, and small surprise gestures a 2024 couple would not spoil by describing. KI-NRT found it warm and personal, though a tad corporate next to a family-run inn, since no butler is assigned to you. The one recurring failure is before arrival, where emails can go unanswered entirely.

room.label: Room
room.text: The base Stylish Suite is already a very large room, with two big beds, a large living room and a bathroom whose private hot tub looks out at the view, and a 2023 family saw no need for anything bigger. The two 140-square-metre Luxury Premium Suites face the forest, private enough to leave the curtains open with the lights on; KI-NRT says to ask for number 306, the end unit. Rooms are Western in style, with beds.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Fufu Nikko stands on the former grounds of the Taisho-era Tamozawa imperial villa, and its architecture echoes the villa, so a 2023 guest found the decor expressed a vivid sense of place. The building is modern but understated and blends into the forest; one couple likened it to a luxury safari tent or the best of the Amans. Tosho-gu and Nikko's other great shrines are a 15-minute walk away, and KI-NRT calls it far and away the top inn in town.

cities.text: Tōbu Ltd Exp Asakusa→Tōbu-Nikkō (~2h), then ~5-min taxi.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01), Tōhoku 'Yamabiko'/'Nasuno' Ōmiya→Utsunomiya (~25 min), change to the JR Nikkō Line local→Nikkō (~45 min, ~hourly) + inn shuttle. Two changes (Ōmiya, Utsunomiya) — reaches Fufu via the JR side, not the Asakusa Tōbu.

Tōkaidō 'Nozomi' Kyoto→Tokyo (~2h15, ~4/hr), cross the Tokyo Stn Shinkansen concourse to a Tōhoku 'Yamabiko'/'Nasuno'→Utsunomiya (~50 min), change to the JR Nikkō Line local→Nikkō (~45 min, ~1–2/hr) + inn shuttle. Two self-handled changes (Tokyo, Utsunomiya). Chosen over the Asakusa Tōbu 'Spacia' (same ~1h50 tail, but a ~20–25-min crosstown from Tokyo Stn on top = +1 change). ⚠ ends on the hourly, snow-slow Nikkō local; ⚠ Tōkaidō services run all-reserved over the New Year peak.

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Nozomi' Shin-Osaka→Tokyo (~2h35, ~4/hr), cross to a Tōhoku 'Yamabiko'/'Nasuno'→Utsunomiya (~50 min), then the JR Nikkō Line local→Nikkō (~45 min, ~1–2/hr) + inn shuttle. Three self-handled changes (Shin-Osaka, Tokyo, Utsunomiya) — the extra half-hour over the Kyoto twin is the further Nozomi run plus the Midōsuji hop. ⚠ the hourly Nikkō local is the fragile end; ⚠ all-reserved Tōkaidō over New Year.

Tōkaidō 'Nozomi' Nagoya→Tokyo (~1h34–1h40, ~4/hr), cross the Tokyo Stn concourse to a Tōhoku 'Yamabiko'/'Nasuno'→Utsunomiya (~50 min), change to the JR Nikkō Line local→Nikkō (~45 min, ~1–2/hr) + inn shuttle. Two self-handled changes (Tokyo, Utsunomiya); the shortest of the Tōkaidō-gateway Nikkō links. ⚠ the snow-slow Nikkō local still sets the floor.
Reverse of: Nikkō→Utsunomiya (~45 min), change to a Tōhoku 'Yamabiko'→Sendai (~75–80 min; the 'Hayabusa' skips Utsunomiya) — the cleanest version of this leg.

inns.name: Nishimuraya Honkan

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: My Top 10 Ryokans Overall (in no particular order): [...] Nishimuraya Honkan (Kinosaki Onsen, Hyogo)

inns.summary: The 150-year-old flagship of Kinosaki Onsen and KI-NRT's annual crab pilgrimage: four stays in, he still names its Matsuba-gani kaiseki the best crab cuisine he has ever had and doubts anywhere ever will compare, served in your room in a traditional house built around a garden. His November 2023 stay found the kitchen below its past peaks, though it stays in his rotation. Book the November–March crab season; bathing is in the communal baths plus Kinosaki's seven town bathhouses, since no room in Kinosaki may have an onsen by town rule.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The Matsuba-gani crab kaiseki, served in your room from November to March, is KI-NRT's benchmark: he has yet to stay anywhere that compares to the crab cuisine here and doubts he ever will, and gives it the edge over Bouyourou. The crabs arrive the same day from Tsuiyama and Shibayama, each held alive in its own tank. A 2025 couple called the crab-and-Tajima-beef dinner simply fabulous; his own fourth stay was not quite up to earlier ones.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no onsen in any room here, or anywhere in Kinosaki, which KI-NRT understands to be a town-wide rule; even the top suite's open-air tub is free-flowing but is not hot-spring water. The real onsen is in the inn's gender-segregated communal baths, and the rest of the bathing is the town itself: Kinosaki's seven public bathhouses, all tattoo-friendly. A 2025 couple visited three of the town baths as well as the ryokan's own.

service.label: Service
service.text: Dinner is always served in your own room whatever the room type, and since 2022 breakfast is in the restaurant unless you are in Honjin no Ma. A 2025 couple called the service on their two-night stay impeccable, and KI-NRT has returned four times without a complaint about the staff, though it is the crab and the garden he writes about.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 34 rooms come in a dizzying array of types, and most face the garden except those in the new annex. KI-NRT found the 90m² Honjin no Ma, the top room, spacious and not at all dated, with a Western dining table, but he prefers a ground-floor suite like Kiri no Ma for its eye-level view of the garden.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Kinosaki Onsen is KI-NRT's quintessential onsen town, with a small river through the middle, gift shops, snack shacks and seven public bathhouses, and he calls it one of the most picturesque in Japan. Inside the gates Nishimuraya is a respite from all that, built around an immaculately landscaped inner garden that turns up on magazine covers, and most rooms face it.

cities.text: Ltd Exp 'Kinosaki' Kyoto→Kinosaki Onsen direct (~2h30).
Reverse of: Kinosaki→Kyoto (~2h30) + Shinkansen→Tokyo (~2h15) — a full travel day.

Ltd Exp 'Kōnotori' Osaka Stn→Kinosaki Onsen (~2h40, direct, no change; ¥5,940–6,540, seat reservation mandatory). Central Osaka departure — the Kyoto twin ('Kinosaki' Ltd Exp, ~2h30) is barely shorter, so base city doesn't decide this one. (Zentan bus ~3h, ¥4,100, is the cheap alt.)

Reverse of: Ltd Exp 'Kinosaki'/'Hashidate' Kinosaki-Onsen→Kyoto (~2h30, direct), change to the 'Thunderbird' Kyoto→Tsuruga (~53 min), cross-platform to the Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Tsurugi' Tsuruga→Kanazawa (~43 min). ~4h06 of riding plus two connection buffers. ⚠ Since the 2024-03-16 Hokuriku Shinkansen extension the Thunderbird terminates at Tsuruga, so the Tsuruga change is mandatory — there is no through service. ⚠ The San'in approach is snow-prone in January. Researched 2026-07-26 (was falling to a 5.0/2 hub estimate; the estimate was within 15 min).

inns.name: Shogetsu

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Shogetsu is indeed incredible; there's a good reason for it landing in my personal top 10 list.

inns.summary: A 21-room hilltop ryokan overlooking the Gero Onsen valley, a tall, nondescript building outside but inside all rock gardens, artsy lounges, a spectacular creative-kaiseki kitchen, amazing Gero spring water and valley views from room, lounge and communal bath alike. KI-NRT puts it in his personal top ten and far and away first in Gero. The charm is all inside, and the private-onsen rooms sell out early.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: KI-NRT calls the kaiseki "creative Japanese at its finest" and some of the best he has ever had, and it is the inn he names first for Gifu. Fried new-harvest potatoes with uni and caviar, Hida beef tongue stew with eagle fern tempura and baby sweetfish deep-fried with herbs were all exceptional, and breakfast was not an afterthought. Michaeljinnyc, fresh from a disappointing two nights at Takimotokan Yuki no Sato, says Shogetsu blew them away.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The water is Gero Onsen's own hot spring, renowned for its quality, and KI-NRT calls it amazing: Shogetsu definitely did not disappoint. His corner suite had an open-air onsen bath on the balcony with the valley below, and the Daiyokujo communal bath has the same sweeping view, which he calls incredible.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: KI-NRT stayed in a corner suite with an open-air onsen bath on the balcony, and he calls the views of the valley from the room incredible. Nobody in the thread has described the rooms beyond that outlook.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Shogetsu is a tall, nondescript building on a hilltop with no garden, but inside are artsy lounges, Zen rock gardens with streams and sweeping views over the Gero valley from lounge, rooms and communal baths. KI-NRT admits it is not quite as atmospheric as Wanosato. Gero town was a delight for Michaeljinnyc to explore. For autumn colour mid to late November should be awesome here and at Gero Onsen Gassho Mura, the thatched-roof folk village.

cities.text: Reverse of: 'Hida' Gero→Toyama (~2h20), change to the Hokuriku Shinkansen Toyama→Kanazawa (~23 min). Beats the Takayama + Nohi-bus chain (~3h25). ⚠ ~5 Toyama through-services/day.
Reverse of: 'Hida' Gero→Nagoya (~1h37), change to a Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Tokyo (~1h40), plus the ~5-min drive at the Gero end. Shogetsu's own access page gives this chain.

Reverse of: 'Hida' Gero→Nagoya (~1h35), change ~15 min to a Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'/'Hikari'→Kyoto (~35 min) + the Shōgetsu shuttle and hotel ends (2026-07 audit: same 10-Hida/day correction as takayama>kyoto — hourly only ~11:30–16:30, 2h gaps outside, all-reserved Dec 25–Jan 5, January 大雪 advisories; the old 2.5 was bare rides on an 'hourly' frequency that isn't). One no-change direct: Hida 36 calls at Gero ~16:10 → Kyoto 19:17.

inns.name: Ryotei Hanzuiryo
inns.summary: Ryotei Hanzuiryo is the most famous and luxurious of the Unzen ryokans, and KI-NRT counts it among the most renowned in the country: a 14-room sukiya-style ryotei where an outstanding in-room kaiseki, an otherworldly 300-square-meter villa and omotenashi at its finest all came together on his December 2024 stay. Book one of the two Tokubetsu Shitsu by phone a year out, because they are the only rooms with in-room onsen. He has stayed once and has not said where it ranks for him.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The 'ryotei' in the name means a place that serves high-end Japanese cuisine, and KI-NRT's dinner, served in the room, lived up to it: an Ariake Sea torafugu medley, an arrowhead-mochi dumpling with lily bulb in a grated-daikon dashi that he found unforgettable (like mochi but much lighter), and artful plating. He calls it a top-notch showing of the best Nagasaki has to offer, and the head chef stayed on through the Onko Chishin acquisition.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Only the two Tokubetsu Shitsu have in-room onsen, because the older Unzen properties hold first rights to the hot-spring fields and limit what Hanzuiryo can draw; every other room uses the communal onsen bath, which KI-NRT calls a significant drawback if in-room bathing matters to you. In the Jyuen villa the outdoor rock bath is real onsen and was amazing, and the villa also has a sauna and an indoor bath that is not onsen.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service was among the best KI-NRT has experienced. The room attendant, Ms. Hata, was charming and explained each dish in exhaustive detail; each time they left the room they came back to refreshed towels, tidied cables, replaced cups and a refilled cotton-swab jar; all the staff greeted them with a smile from 50 feet away, and the car was valet-parked each time. Nagasaki Joe, who has also stayed, calls the service traditional and exemplary.

room.label: Room
room.text: The Jyuen villa is 300 square meters, one of two Tokubetsu Shitsu with its own gate and path, with a tatami room, a Western living room, a sauna and a sukiya hallway wrapping around it. KI-NRT found it spacious but not spartan, the down comforter heavenly and the amenities beyond a first-class airline kit. Even standard rooms are 250 square meters. Nagasaki Joe, who has stayed, dislikes the Western furniture mixed into the traditional rooms.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The sukiya-style buildings blend into lush surroundings, moss-laden gardens and koi ponds, and the vibe is incredibly peaceful, reminiscent of Takefue, Gosho Gekkoju and Wanosato; KI-NRT calls the setting mystical. It is a secluded pocket about 10 minutes on foot from central Unzen and the Hells. He notes it is not surrounded by natural forest; the first-floor rooms look straight onto a well-maintained garden with pretty trees.

cities.text: Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen relay Hakata→Isahaya (~1h40 via Takeo-Onsen), then Shimatetsu bus Isahaya→Unzen Onsen (~1h20). One night only — the private-onsen special rooms make a second night pricey.

Reverse of: Bus Unzen→Shimabara Port (~40 min), 'Ocean Arrow' high-speed ferry→Kumamoto Port (30 min, ~every 2h), timed port shuttle→Kumamoto Stn (~25 min), 'Sakura'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~50 min). Gale days: all-rail via Isahaya/Takeo (~4.4h) is the fallback.

Reverse of: Ken-ei bus Unzen→Nagasaki (~1h40), or back to Isahaya and Ltd Exp on. By car ~47 km / ~1h15 (R57 down the mountain → Chijiwa → Isahaya) — only the top ~10 km of the descent carries ice risk.

Reverse of: Shimatetsu bus Unzen→Shimabara Port (~40 min, ~hourly), 'Ocean Arrow'→Kumamoto Port (30 min, ~5/day), timed free shuttle→Kumamoto Stn (~25 min). Ariake gales → all-rail fallback. With a rental: the Ocean Arrow carries cars (¥5,100 4–5 m class + ¥1,600/passenger; 6 RT/day in Jan; car slots open 1 month out — reserve, walk-ups are first-come); the slower Kyusho ferry (60 min, ¥3,900) is the gale-day fallback; Shimabara Port→Unzen is a 19-km climb to 700 m (~26 min, budget 40) — the most freeze-prone road in Nagasaki Pref.

Fly via Nagasaki: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Nagasaki (NGS) ~1h50, then up the Shimabara peninsula by bus — NGS→Isahaya (~35 min) + Shimatetsu bus Isahaya→Unzen Onsen (~1h20), or the infrequent direct airport→Unzen bus (~100 min).
Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Nishi-Kyushu relay Hakata→Isahaya + Shimatetsu bus to Unzen Onsen (~3h). ~6.75h — the longest of these.

inns.name: Shiguchi
inns.summary: Shiguchi is Zaborin founder Shouya Grigg's five-villa kominka retreat, the ryokan he says he always wanted to make, with massive restored farmhouses filled with his art and two private source-fed baths in each. Four stays agree it is Niseko's most soulful luxury option. KI-NRT calls it 'a true gem' and gives the staff's warmth a chapter of its own, and one member put the dinner among the best meals of a two-week Japan trip. At roughly ¥268,000 a night it is one of the most expensive inns even in this company.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner at Somoza is a creative French-Japanese fusion grounded in Hokkaido produce, some of it foraged by staff. KI-NRT's salad of foraged microgreens and salmon roe under sea urchin foam was unforgettable, and the Jomon Pan, a buckwheat-and-acorn bread served on excavated Jomon pottery, transportive. mattjp put it among the best meals of a two-week Japan trip, though Fc912 found the food a little forced and nylonite wanted more Hokkaido wines.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The hot springs are true gensen kakenagashi, flowing straight from the on-site source with no circulation or chemical treatment, and every villa has two onsen baths of its own, one rock and one hinoki, so bathing here is private and in-room. There is also a sauna in a small hut below Somoza's deck. nylonite, there in April with snow still on the ground, called the view from CHI's private bath out over the Hokkaido landscape sublime.

service.label: Service
service.text: The staff got a chapter of their own from KI-NRT: most are Hokkaido-born, many have been there since opening, and their pride shows in every interaction, warm and invested. Takehiro-san, the GM (formerly of the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo), could not have been more accommodating when nylonite's partner fell ill and had to reschedule, and mattjp found the service meaningfully better than at Zaborin next door. Fc912 put it at above average.

room.label: Room
room.text: Five villas in three restored Aizuwakamatsu kominka, all palatial, from CHI (144 m2) to the standalone KA (351 m2 for three or more), held up by massive beams with no nails or screws and filled with Shouya Grigg's art. KI-NRT's KU (247 m2) runs three stories in moody dark wood, but he would book CHI next time, since bedroom and living area share one floor. mattjp gave Zaborin a slight edge on hard product, and every villa has a full kitchen.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Shiguchi sits on a secluded perch above the Iō River valley with no other building in view, just stillness, sky and trees, minutes from Zaborin and the Park Hyatt with none of their intrusion; KI-NRT was reminded of Wanosato, with grander views from its higher site. Somoza, the relocated farmhouse holding reception, lounge and restaurant, has floor-to-ceiling windows framing river and mountains, and Shouya's basement galleries can be toured.

cities.text: ~2 hr by car/private transfer from New Chitose Airport (CTS) due west to Niseko.
~2.5 hr by car from Sapporo (or rail to Kutchan + 15 min drive).

inns.name: ryugon
inns.summary: A rebuilt samurai residence in Minamiuonuma snow country, feudal Japan from the grounds and artsy and avant-garde inside, that KI-NRT says nails it on all counts: innovative local cooking crowned by Japan's best rice, private terrace onsen and polished, unintrusive service. It is room-dependent, because reception is very mixed and probably comes down to the lesser rooms, so book a Villa Suite Premium, ideally room H over the pond; even that top villa comes in under entry-level rooms at the famous names, which is a bonus.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Ryugon cooks Minamiuonuma's Shiozawa Koshihikari rice in individual pots, done to perfection and so good that you eat it by itself, and KI-NRT calls it bar none the best rice in Japan. The rest of the cooking is innovative and mostly excellent, built on local ingredients with real creativity in flavour and plating, though being inland some of the seafood comes in from the coast. Meals are served in private rooms in the main restaurant.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Each of the three Villa Suite Premium rooms has a private open-air onsen bath on its deck, and KI-NRT found his, right on the terrace over the pond, serene, soothing and incredibly refreshing. sirky soaked in his own private onsen in February with mounds of snow around it. Nobody in the thread has written about the shared baths.

service.label: Service
service.text: The staff are professional, prompt and graceful, staying out of the way when not needed and coming at once with a big smile when called, which KI-NRT found very polished and never intrusive. Nobody in the thread has named an attendant or a standout gesture.

room.label: Room
room.text: Book one of the three Villa Suite Premium rooms (75 to 93 square metres), each with a private open-air onsen on the deck; KI-NRT picks H as the most private, with an amazing view over a large pond to the forest. They are junior-suite layouts, and two higher categories (Villa Suite Terrace and Manor House) have since opened, though he still thinks the Premium villas have the best views. Reviews are mixed, which he puts down to the lesser rooms.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Ryugon stands in rural Minamiuonuma, Niigata's snow country, and although rebuilt it looks from the grounds like feudal Japan, as if you had been taken back as a samurai; inside, the common areas mix old, new and avant-garde in an artsy, mostly tasteful way. KI-NRT groups it with the darker samurai-mood houses, next to light and airy Asaba. Heavy snow buries the region in winter, and sirky found mounds of it around his onsen in February.

cities.text: Jōetsu Shinkansen Tokyo→Echigo-Yuzawa (~75 min), then ~30 min by car (inn can arrange).

Reverse of: ⚠ This leg used to encode 2.5h via the Hokuhoku line — that was the HAKUTAKA LIMITED EXPRESS, whose last run was 13 March 2015 (replaced by the Hokuriku Shinkansen; the name moved to a Tokyo–Kanazawa shinkansen). The Hokuhoku's own Snow Rabbit rapid then went in March 2023, leaving all-stops locals. Modern route is all-Shinkansen with ONE change: ~25-min inn car/flat-¥5,000 taxi to Echigo-Yuzawa, Jōetsu 'Toki'→Takasaki (~22 min), cross to the Hokuriku 'Hakutaka'→Kanazawa (~2h05, timetabled; timed pairings run the station chain in 2h55–3h00 — 2026-07-29 re-check against the live timetable, was priced 2h15–18 + 30) . ~3h30 door-to-door. (Hokuhoku alt via Jōetsumyōkō is ~3h40–4h over 2–3 changes on a sparse line where half the trains terminate at Muikamachi and no IC cards are accepted — no faster, far less robust.)
Reverse of: Echigo-Yuzawa→Jōetsu 'Toki'→Tokyo (same-station change), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto. The cleanest northern Kyoto exit — one transfer; snow risk is the inn access road, not the rail.
Reverse of: Echigo-Yuzawa→Ōmiya (~50 min), change to Tōhoku Shinkansen 'Hayabusa'→Sendai (~1h20) — all Shinkansen, one change.

inns.name: Bettei Senjuan

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Not yet. But it's close. Gosho Gekkoju, Bettei Senjuan and Shinsen could easily be in the Top 10 - it depends on what you're looking for.

inns.summary: Established in 1997 as the upscale annex of Ryokan Tanigawa, Senjuan is an artistic showpiece in the shadow of Mt. Tanigawa, with carvings on every beam, a glass-walled corridor onto the Alps and source-fed baths in all 18 rooms. KI-NRT says it could easily crack his top ten and would not hesitate to return. There is little to do here beyond soaking, eating and the scenery, which is exactly why it shines in deep winter, when the garden turns into a private snow park.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The 11-course kaiseki was the highlight of KI-NRT's stay, built on local Gunma ingredients, and the most memorable dish was a savory souffle-like custard with grilled conger eel, red king crab, lily bulb and yuba that he called very original and simply sublime. Breakfast was quite original and pretty darned good too. Guests on Japanese sites are cooler on the meals than on the baths, and the kitchen will vary the menu for a second night if asked.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All 18 rooms have their own open-air onsen bath fed straight from the source, free-flowing and never recirculated, and the tub in Special Room SP looks over the river, forest and Alps, one of the more mesmerizing in-room views KI-NRT has seen. He found the water a bit lukewarm, which Westerners may prefer though Japanese bathers want it hotter; staff adjust it by hand. A riverside private sauna with a cold plunge was added in 2022.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT does not describe the service itself; he mentions only that meals come in a private dining room and that English menus are available on request, which he calls a nice touch. Guests on Japanese sites add that the kitchen will vary the menu for a second night and that staff adjust the in-room bath temperature by hand.

room.label: Room
room.text: Special Room SP, the top suite, has a living room, bedroom, tea room, a mini inner garden and an open-air onsen bath, and it is stylish beyond belief while still traditional, with understated artistic detail on everything from the entrance door to the sliding doors. It is almost completely tatami-matted, so you sit on cushions and sleep on futons. Special Room S is comparable, and KI-NRT says the entry-level room is nothing to shout about.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Senjuan sits in the shadow of Mt. Tanigawa in northern Gunma, and a long curved corridor with floor-to-ceiling glass looks onto the Alps and the grounds, its walls and beams covered in carvings and small seasonal displays (ikebana, a string instrument, a miniature maple display). It is quite secluded, and KI-NRT warns there is little to do other than soaking, the scenery and the food; January guests call the garden a private snow park.

cities.text: Jōetsu Shinkansen Tokyo→Jōmō-Kōgen (~66–70 min), then a ~20-min taxi (¥5,500 on a 2024 guest report; rank taxis wait at the station). Senjuan's own access page gives this exact chain as 約100分 door-to-door from Tokyo Stn — that's the figure used here. Its free pickup runs from MINAKAMI Stn (Jōetsu-line local), not Jōmō-Kōgen, and the inn quotes that relay-bus-to-Minakami chain at 約110分 — so the taxi wins by ~10 min and a great deal of hassle.

Reverse of: ~20-min taxi to Jōmō-Kōgen, Jōetsu Shinkansen→Takasaki (~15 min), cross to the Hokuriku 'Hakutaka'→Kanazawa (2h15–2h18, timetabled). One change, at Takasaki. Sibling of echigoyuzawa>kanazawa and ~30 min shorter for the same reasons Senjuan is always nearer: Jōmō-Kōgen is closer to Takasaki and the last mile is a shorter taxi.
Reverse of: Inn car + Jōetsu Shinkansen Jōmō-Kōgen→Tokyo (~1h50 door-to-door), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (~2h15).

Reverse of: Off the mountain and south by air: inn car + Jōetsu Shinkansen Jōmō-Kōgen→Tokyo (~1h50 door-to-door), Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), then HND→Fukuoka (~2h flight + airport time) and the subway 2 stops into Hakata/Tenjin (~5 min). ~5.5h door-to-door — a normal travel day, not a brutal one.
Reverse of: Inn shuttle to Jōmō-Kōgen, Jōetsu Shinkansen→Ōmiya (~45 min), change to Tōhoku Shinkansen 'Hayabusa'→Sendai (~1h20) — all Shinkansen, one change.

inns.name: Hiiragiya
inns.summary: One of Kyoto's original big three, an 1818 inn facing Tawaraya, and KI-NRT's third stay was his best yet, because the appeal lies in depth, in layers of craftsmanship and in service that anticipates what you need, and nothing about it shouts for attention. It is easier to book than Tawaraya, with an excellent English website, and to his palate better fed, but the fixtures are dated and the futons tried his wife's patience. Pick the Honkan for Edo-period atmosphere, the Shinkan for modern light and an elevator.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is kaiseki served in your room, and KI-NRT found it superb and creative. The standout was a clear soup with hamaguri shinjo, the usually chewy clam reworked into an airy, umami-rich ball, which he called a small stroke of genius, and the sashimi was Shimonoseki fugu with a ponzu and fugu-milt sauce. Breakfast is more restrained but just as good, and to his palate Tawaraya's more rigidly traditional meals are not as memorable.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no hot spring here, since central Kyoto has none, and no communal bath either. Every room has a tub of soft groundwater in koyamaki pine, several honkan rooms have Ogawa Sanchi stained glass over the bath, and there are two free bookable family baths, one in stained glass and one fully lacquered. The craft is in the tubs and the glasswork, and the water is ordinary. Across three stays KI-NRT mentions the family baths but never the soak.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is where Hiiragiya distinguishes itself, and KI-NRT puts the omotenashi as high as anything he has experienced in Japan. The preferences from his two previous stays were waiting in the room (extra-large bath towels, dietary quirks, an air purifier), and they set up a dining table and chair for his mother-in-law, which Tawaraya does not do. They wiped her wheelchair wheels spotless and shipped a forgotten item home for nothing.

room.label: Room
room.text: All 24 rooms are distinct and traditional, decorated by master artisans (stained glass, fine woodwork, kakejiku scrolls). The Honkan is slightly dark and richly atmospheric, as if you had slipped back into the Edo period; the 2006 Shinkan annex is more modern, with an elevator, and beautiful in its own right. His 49 m² Shinkan room did show its age: one sink, a Toto toilet two generations behind, a broken humidifier, and futons at night.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Hiiragiya faces Tawaraya across a narrow one-way street in central Kyoto, about 20 minutes on foot from the Imperial Palace, Gion and Heian Jingu. Inside, holly-leaf motifs run through the carpets, woodwork and linens, courtyard and pocket gardens appear even on the upper floors, and there is a library and a modern art gallery. The decoration changes with the season, and KI-NRT finds it all subtly overwhelming in a very calm, almost zen way.

cities.text: ~15 min by taxi from JR Kyoto Stn to central Nakagyo.
Osaka to Kyoto ~30 min Shinkansen/special rapid, then ~15 min taxi.

inns.name: Sanso Amanosato

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: My Top 10 Ryokans Overall (in no particular order): [...] Sanso Amanosato (Shimoamano, Katsuragi, Wakayama Prefecture)

inns.summary: A modern eight-room auberge in deep Wakayama countryside that people book for its French-Japanese dinner. KI-NRT left calling it one of the very best culinary destinations in existence, and stays through 2025 report the kitchen still at that level. Rooms, baths and scenery are comfortable but secondary, since its top-ten spot is earned at the table, so plan it as a one-night gastronomic detour paired with Koyasan.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Chef Ohigashi's French-Japanese kaiseki is why you stay: nine savory courses and three desserts, among them wild red sea bream cured under white asparagus foam and caviar, and a lobster head stuffed with its tomalley and roasted in aosa-nori butter. KI-NRT calls it one of the very best culinary destinations in existence, ahead of Sankara and Arcana, and RichardInSF found it easily Michelin-star quality. Drinks at the bar are free until 11pm.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The onsen is in three private baths about 100 feet from the rooms, genuine sodium-chloride spring water, two with saunas and only one with an open-air tub, so check the tablet first if outdoors is what you want. There are no communal baths and no booking: an in-room app shows which bath is free, and with only eight rooms you can soak almost any time. The in-room tub is plain heated water. Buster CT1K found the baths nice and not too crowded.

service.label: Service
service.text: Mr. Nakamura, the GM, leads a team KI-NRT calls outstanding, proactive yet unobtrusive: when they asked where the baths were he walked them over, and their car windows had been cleaned before checkout despite being parked under a canopy. Later guests agree, with Buster CT1K reporting a very high standard of attention to detail, zander86 staff who make you feel right at home, and RichardInSF dining-room service worth at least a detour.

room.label: Room
room.text: The Western-style suites (Hachiyo was KI-NRT's) are 64 m2, on the small side for a top room, but light wood, high vaulted ceilings and massive windows make them bright and airy, and there are two separate toilets and a fully stocked bathroom. RichardInSF's suite was large and well-appointed with a real mountain-lodge feel, though his shower ran out of hot water one morning, and Buster CT1K wanted the microfiber towels swapped for cotton.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Amanosato stands on a sleepy farming plain at the foot of the Koya range, with green fields, mountains in the distance and no Japanese garden, as rural as it gets, which KI-NRT counts as part of the charm, and the modern wooden buildings blend into it. Niutsuhime shrine, a UNESCO site, is just down the road and Koyasan is near enough to pair with, and he recommends it as the indulgent second night after a shukubo temple stay there.

cities.text: JR to Kaseda via the Wakayama line (~2h15), then a PRE-BOOKED taxi ~15 min (~¥3k; Yuko-Kihoku 0736-22-3333 — Kaseda has no rank taxis) — frees you from Amanosato's 15:00-only shuttle (4-pax cap).
Reverse of: Shinkansen back to Tokyo (~3–3.5h from Kansai).
Reverse of: Kintetsu Gose Line→Shakudo, transfer to the Minami-Osaka Line→Osaka-Abenobashi/Tennoji (~1h5 riding).

inns.name: Sanso Tensui

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: If our experience there is any indication, I'd argue that it's easily among the 20 best ryokans in all of Japan, and priced at a fraction of the rates that top properties command in nearby Yufuin.

inns.summary: A 19-room onsen ryokan in a moss forest outside Hita, built around giant boulders beside a river and waterfall, with bathing KI-NRT calls second to none at a place he argues is easily among Japan's 20 best. At $420-600 a night it is a real bargain against neighboring Yufuin. The Taisho-era interiors charm some and put off others, and the sulfur smell and waterfall roar are strong enough that sensitive sleepers should take one of the five onsen-free rooms.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Both meals on KI-NRT's December 2024 stay were incredible: cherry trout from Oku Hita fried in whole grains, a cod-milt chawanmushi he found dreamy creamy, and a sake-lees kasu-jiru in place of the usual closing miso soup. The suites eat in their own room and everyone else gets a private room in the main restaurant. zander86 found dinner excellent too and recommends the shabu-shabu or sukiyaki option for a small top-up.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The onsen is source-fed and the hydrogen-sulfide smell is at least as strong as at most springs KI-NRT has tried; he calls the bathing second to none. Three gender-segregated public baths include Takimian, up a long staircase with a view of Sakura Falls, and five free private rental baths face the Goraku River. Kamayu is a two-person tub shaped like an udon bowl with jacuzzi jets, and zander86 was told it and Kiriyu have the best views.

service.label: Service
service.text: Dinner was elegantly served by Yuko Baba, who patiently explained every course in painstaking detail. On zander86's stay the staff surprised him with a birthday gift, which he thought a very nice touch. Neither guest has written more about the service than that.

room.label: Room
room.text: The three special suites each have a terrace and an open-air rock bath on the deck facing the forest. KI-NRT's Kaori is 85 sqm, furnished in Taisho-era style (the sink sits on a Singer sewing-machine base), which is not to his taste, though it gave a soothing sense of place. The sulfur smell is acute even with the doors closed and the river is extremely audible, so sensitive sleepers should take one of the five rooms without onsen.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The 19 rooms sit in a moss forest beside a gushing river and a waterfall, far enough from the centre of Hita that you feel secluded, and the architects built around the massive boulders to preserve the terrain. The buildings are traditional rural Japan and charming, and KI-NRT calls it the top property in the greater Hita region. Mameda-machi in Hita is a preserved merchant quarter with the most impressive Hina doll museum he has seen.

cities.text: Reverse of: Kyudai-line Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin no Mori' Amagase→Hakata, 1h35 ride + the Tensui pickup to Amagase Station (2026-07 audit: the old 1.5 was below the bare ride; ⚠ ~5–6 Amagase stops/day — the 12:14 is the checkout-friendly one).

Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima-Chūō→Kurume (~45 min), change to the JR 'Yufu' Ltd Exp toward Hita/Amagase (~1h25), free pickup from JR Amagase. ~2h40 door-to-door — the Yufu passes through Kurume, so you change there rather than riding on to Hakata and doubling back.

Reverse of: Change at TOSU, not Hakata (the Hakata 'Yufu'↔'Relay Kamome' pairing is a 0-minute connection — impossible): Kyudai Ltd Exp 'Yufu' Amagase↔Tosu (~1h13; ⚠ only 6 Amagase-stopping expresses/day), 'Relay Kamome' Tosu↔Takeo-Onsen (~36 min, every train stops Tosu), 'Kamome'↔Nagasaki (~31 min, same-platform timed change at Takeo). ⚠ Nagasaki→hita direction: only Yufu 3 (Tosu 12:38) lands before 16:09 — leave the hotel by ~10:35; miss it and it's ~4h35 via Yufuin-no-Mori 5.
Reverse of: 'Yufu' Amagase/Hita→Kurume (~50 min), Shinkansen→Kumamoto (~25 min).

Fly via Fukuoka: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Fukuoka (FUK) ~2h, subway 2 stops Fukuoka Airport→Hakata (~5 min), then the Kyudai-line Ltd Exp Hakata→Amagase (~1h30) + free inn pickup. (Oita Airport is on the wrong, eastern side of the prefecture — Hakata is the real gateway to Hita/Amagase.)
Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then the Kyudai-line Ltd Exp Hakata→Amagase for Hita/Tensui (~1h30). ~5.25h door-to-door.

inns.name: Soneka
inns.summary: A four-villa private retreat opened in 2024 on 77,000m2 of forest and meadow near Kitahiroshima, 30 minutes from New Chitose Airport, where check-in, every chef-cooked meal and two baths of rare amber moor onsen all happen inside your own villa. At about 339,000 yen a night it is among Japan's priciest, and after one superb stay KI-NRT calls it his favorite ryokan in Hokkaido, ahead of Shiguchi, because the glorious water, airy villas and dining cooked for you alone are exactly what the rates buy.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Every meal is cooked for your villa alone by a dedicated chef, wood-fired in your kitchen, charcoal robata at the hearth or kaiseki. Chef Kohei Oyama trained Italian before Japanese at Michelin-starred Mieda, and KI-NRT's standouts were a burger of fried Hokkaido corn millet on fresh brioche and Nebokke, smoked, grilled atka mackerel, which he ranks among the finest fish he has ever tasted. Breakfast is simpler but generous.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every villa has an indoor and an open-air bath of moor onsen, a rare plant-derived spring drilled 1,500 meters down and used straight from the source: amber water rich in humic matter that works like a natural skin lotion. Nupu is the only villa where the outdoor bath overflows into an adjoining pool kept pleasantly warm, a gorgeous design, and the water is KI-NRT's main reason for preferring Soneka even to Shiguchi.

service.label: Service
service.text: With four villas and every meal served in-villa, the service was exceptional: Yasuo, the manager, and two hosts, Nanami and Mei, looked after KI-NRT throughout and were always available. Nanami, the trilingual activities coordinator, secured a hard-to-get strawberry-picking slot at Abe Noen, collecting the paper ticket in person that morning, and next day queued at the mochi shop Fuurin Chiriri for a ticket and went along with them.

room.label: Room
room.text: The four two-bedroom villas each have two onsen baths, an outdoor net bed, a kitchen and dining area, a fire pit and the same meadow view, but the layouts differ: Inkara is higher, with the best view, Nitai is wrapped in trees with a tented sauna, and Nupu (159 m2), KI-NRT's pick, is the lightest and least rustic. The one drawback is Nupu's wing layout, an open-air deck between bedroom and living room that Mrs. KI-NRT disliked.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Soneka is a quiet rural retreat surrounded by farmland in Kitahiroshima, its four villas spaced well apart across a tall-grass meadow and no landscaped garden, reception desk or guest lounge; the only shared spaces are a group dining room, the Irori Terrace with its charcoal hearth, an apiary and a pond. KI-NRT found little reason to leave except that no lunch is served, and he and his wife were the only guests on both July nights.

cities.text: ~30 min by car (32 km) from New Chitose Airport (CTS); ~40 min by train to Kitahiroshima + taxi. Free shuttle with advance booking.
~35 min by car (23 km) from Sapporo, or ~30 min by train to Kitahiroshima Stn + taxi.

inns.name: Gosho Gekkoju

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Not yet. But it's close. Gosho Gekkoju, Bettei Senjuan and Shinsen could easily be in the Top 10 - it depends on what you're looking for.

inns.summary: An eight-room hillside ryokan behind a massive gate in Kurokawa Onsen (renamed Gekkoju Kurokawa), with an onsen bath in every room plus private rental baths, including a man-made cave bath and the exposed hilltop Tenku (go after sundown). With Takefue it defines the top of Kurokawa, and KI-NRT says the area's luxury drops off steeply after these two; plenty of guests prefer it, and a 2025 visitor who tried both called it 'the overall best for me.' Book a suite higher up the hill for the valley views.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a twelve-course kaiseki, and both dinner and breakfast are served in your room. KI-NRT puts the food just short of exceptional, much as at Takefue, and a November 2025 guest called it very good.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All eight rooms have their own onsen bath, and in the suites the tub is at the window with the valley below; a November 2025 guest found the view from his bath jaw dropping. There are also several private rental baths, including one inside a man-made cave, which you can use at any time, and Tenku on the mountaintop, reserved at check-in, which he found just as jaw dropping. Do Tenku after dark, because there is no cover from the sun.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is personal and attentive, and a November 2025 guest called the service from Ms Kurumi, who brought both dinner and breakfast to his room, perfect. Because the rooms climb a hillside, staff can shuttle guests on a golf cart, at least to the rooms slightly lower down the hill, which KI-NRT suggests for anyone who struggles with steps.

room.label: Room
room.text: There are only eight rooms, traditional Japanese in style, and because the ryokan is relatively new they are squeaky clean. The suites have ample space, and the ones higher up the hill have the better views of the valley below and the mountains beyond. A November 2025 guest in the Izayoi room called his first look a wow moment: the onsen bath is at the window with the shower beside it, and the dining table has a footbath built under it.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: You enter through a massive gate and feel as if you have been ushered into another world. There is no central garden, but the landscaping across the whole hillside is gorgeous, and KI-NRT uses the arrival here as his benchmark for a wow-inducing entrance and groups the property with Takefue and Wanosato for its peaceful atmosphere. Kurokawa Onsen town below is picturesque, nicer still at night when the lanterns are lit along the river.

cities.text: Reverse of: Direct highway bus Kurokawa→Hakata/Fukuoka (~2.5–3h, reserve) — no train changes at all.
Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima-Chūō→Kumamoto (~50 min), then ~2.5h bus/taxi up to Kurokawa Onsen (inn pickup from the bus stop).
Reverse of: Direct highway bus Kurokawa→Hakata (~3h, only 2–3/day — reserve), then 'Relay Kamome'→Takeo-Onsen + 'Kamome'→Nagasaki (~1.4h). January snow can detour the Kurokawa road.

Reverse of: Kyushu Ōdan bus one-seat Kurokawa→Kumamoto Stn (~2h38; 3/day down, only 2/day back up — reserve). Also stops at Kumamoto Airport (~1h50) en route. By car ~77 km / ~1h50 via Senomoto + R57 (or the Milk Road rim), budget 2h15–2h30 in January — the Aso rim roads can gate-close in ice.

Fly via Kumamoto: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Aso-Kumamoto (KMJ) ~2h, then the Sankō bus KMJ→Kurokawa Onsen (~1h50, ~5/day) + inn pickup from the bus stop. Closer than backtracking through Hakata's ~3h highway bus.
Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then the direct highway bus Hakata→Kurokawa Onsen (~2h30–3h, reserve) + inn pickup. ~6.5h door-to-door.

inns.name: Migiwatei Ochi Kochi

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: Still, this is a place that likely would crack my top 20 list (for now) if I ever bothered to have one.

inns.summary: A modern 17-room adults-only ryokan on the water's edge in Tomonoura, every room facing the Seto Inland Sea with its own deck onsen bath, where the first night's dinner ranked among the best of KI-NRT's ryokan-going life. He would place the inn around his top twenty nationally, and Japanese guests near-unanimously agree. Book one of the four Upper Suites, the only category with in-room dining, and know that it stands on a working harbor, so ferry and port sounds come with the view.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The first night's kaiseki was otherworldly, one of the top ten ryokan meals KI-NRT has eaten: conger eel sashimi with its raw liver, a two-tofu and usui pea custard that was spectacularly creamy without being heavy, and pepper-grilled Takehara wagyu cooked just right, every course explained in detail.
