The second night was less spectacular and only very good, and later web reports describe the same dip, so one night may be the ideal length.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has an open-air onsen bath on its sea-facing terrace, and the two private rental baths (free of charge and larger) made a nice change of pace for KI-NRT. The water is a radium mineral spring that comes out cold and is heated and circulated, so it is real mineral water but not a hot spring at source; he found it soothing on the skin. A January 2025 guest reported the rooftop rental baths closed from December to February.

service.label: Service
service.text: The staff are warm, knowledgeable and on the ball, and they explain each kaiseki course in detail (in Japanese, in KI-NRT's case). Guests in the four Upper Suites have all their meals served in the room, which he loves and which is slowly disappearing even from the top ryokans.

room.label: Room
room.text: KI-NRT found his Upper Suite (#203, Shien) terrific, a wonderful blend of old and new with Western beds, a dining area where all the meals were served, a living room and a wide terrace with its own onsen bath and amazing sea views, styled in warm earthy tones without clutter. The building dates from 2010 and was renovated in 2024, so there is very little sign of wear. There are four Upper Suites, three on the second floor and one on the fifth.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: There is no garden, because the building stands on the coast, and every room and the common areas look out over the Seto Inland Sea to Bentenjima and Sensuijima islands, with the boat dock for Sensuijima steps away. Tomonoura is a working port that oozes history and charm, good for a slow day of temples and island boats, though KI-NRT ranks it below Takayama, Tsumago and Gion as an old town, and ferry and harbor sounds are part of a stay.

cities.text: Reverse of: From the Inland Sea finale to Hiroshima (~1h).
Shinkansen Kyoto→Fukuyama (~1h40), then ~30-min car/shuttle to the Tomonoura waterfront.
Reverse of: San'yō/Tōkaidō Shinkansen Fukuyama→Tokyo (~3.5–4h).
Sanyo Shinkansen 'Sakura'/'Hikari' Hakata→Fukuyama (~1h25; Nozomi skips Fukuyama), then a ~30-min inn shuttle/taxi to the Tomonoura waterfront (reserve the shuttle — fixed times).

inns.name: Bouyourou
inns.summary: Bouyourou is a seven-room crab inn on the Fukui coast, rebuilt in 2021, whose owner personally delivers Echizen-gani to the Imperial household, and in season this may be the best crab meal in Japan, eaten in a private room after a soak in your own source-fed ocean-view bath. Rates are near the top of the whole field, roughly double Nishimuraya Honkan in crab season, and outside November to March there is less reason to come. KI-NRT came for the crab and the soak and the inn knocked both out of the park, but there is no garden, the town has little charm and the rooms are not vast.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: In-season Echizen-gani is the meal here, and KI-NRT called it sublime: sweet, plump and fatty in a way other crabs are not, served as sashimi, shabu-shabu, grilled, boiled, tempura and chilled with caviar, all of it magnificent, and they never got crabbed-out. The preparations are kept simple to bring out the crab, and he still gives Nishimuraya Honkan the edge for creativity and refinement. Fc912 found the crab better than at top Tokyo places.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own hot-spring bath facing the ocean, free-flowing straight from the source and never recirculated, and there are no communal baths at all. KI-NRT came for the crab and the soak and said the inn knocked both out of the park, and on his summer stay the in-room bath was so comfortable that they spent the afternoon jumping in and out of it and went to dinner much later than usual.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT calls the service flawless, and the inn kept its small staff intact through the pandemic. Each of the seven parties eats in its own private koshitsu dining room (seven of them for seven rooms), and instead of committing to an exact meal time at check-in you simply show up any time between 5 and 7, which he found a real convenience after an afternoon in the bath. The courtesy van collects guests at Awara Onsen station.

room.label: Room
room.text: All seven rooms were rebuilt in November 2021 and are suite-style, modern and understated, with heated floors and an uninterrupted ocean view from every one. They are all the same rate and differ mainly in layout, so pick the plan you like on the website. KI-NRT wishes they were roomier, since at around 70 square meters they are comfortable but tight next to the separate-living-room suites of 100 square meters or more that he prefers.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn is a single modern structure that juts out along the violent Sea of Japan coast, and every room has an uninterrupted ocean view. That view is the whole of the setting, because there are no grounds and no garden, and if you want zen-style traditional architecture you will not find it here. Mikuni Onsen town is a recent invention that KI-NRT found drab and dreary, with no main strip to stroll, though the Tojinbo Cliffs are not far.

cities.text: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Tsurugi' Kanazawa→Awara-Onsen (~27 min), then the inn's free ~10-min shuttle (reserve by the day before; pickup 14:30–18:00) — Kofuyuden Beniya is in central Awara Onsen town, not out on the Mikuni coast (awara.co.jp/access; 2026-07 audit).
Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Hakutaka' direct Tokyo→Awara-Onsen (~2h55, a through service since the 2024 Tsuruga extension), then chauffeured car to Bouyourou on the Mikuni coast (~20 min).
Reverse of: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Tsurugi' Awara-Onsen→Tsuruga (~30 min), cross-platform change (~10 min), 'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp→Kyoto (~55 min) — segments re-timed 2026-07 audit; total holds.
Reverse of: ~30-min taxi/bus from Mikuni/Awara to Komatsu Airport, the KMQ→Fukuoka hop (~1h40, ~4 daily ANA/ORC), then the subway 2 stops into Hakata (~5 min). ~3.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: ~30-min taxi/bus to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Nishi-Kyushu relay→Nagasaki via Takeo-Onsen (~2h). ~5.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: ~30-min taxi/bus to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h17). ~5.25h door-to-door.

inns.name: Kansuiro
inns.summary: A nine-room historic ryokan at Murasugi Onsen outside Niigata, chosen by KI-NRT over its renowned neighbors for the architecture and radium springs, and he came away calling the charm off the charts, a rare classic property he prefers to his usual wa-modern taste. The cuisine and the top villa deliver without compromise; the mineral-steam bathing culture keeps every bath indoors, and the grilled nodoguro is at its best in fall and winter. He has stayed once so far.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kitchen makes full use of Niigata's bounty: the sashimi (with peony shrimp from Sado) was incredibly fresh, the Shibata-raised beef sirloin excellent, and the Koganeton pork simmered with pickled plums comes from pigs fed on cheese whey. A clear soup of wheat gluten with red shiso was simple in concept but masterful in execution. The one disappointment was the grilled nodoguro, out of season on KI-NRT's visit; it peaks in fall and winter.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The water is Murasugi Onsen hot spring, one of Japan's foremost radium springs; the four stand-alone villas have their own onsen (Rinsenkaku's is semi-open-air) and rooms in the Taisho-no-ma main building use the communal and family baths. Every bath is indoors and sealed on purpose: the proprietress advises keeping the glass doors shut so you inhale the mineral-rich steam, and patting dry instead of showering so the minerals stay on the skin.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service was polished and elegant, with alert and accommodating staff, and the personal dinner and breakfast servers went to great lengths to explain each dish, down to how the Koganeton pigs are raised and why they are fed whey. Every guest eats privately, in the room or in a private dining room in the reception building (Rinsenkaku's stone steps make carrying a multi-course meal up hard, and KI-NRT did not mind one bit).

room.label: Room
room.text: Rinsenkaku, the top villa, is a two-story wooden structure assembled in the 19th century on raised ground, with tatami rooms, a Western-style living room and a semi-open-air onsen bath, and verandas run around it with enough foliage for privacy and views of the garden and pond. It has been carefully updated: the floors do not creak, and there is fast Wi-Fi, two toilets and a shower area for two. KI-NRT found nothing to compromise on.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The beauty of the grounds strikes you first, as moss-covered paths, creeks and ponds give the property an almost mystical charm and the Meiji-era main building and villas add to it. It is the kind of place where your blood pressure drops the moment you arrive. Founded in 1614, Kansuiro is a clear exception to KI-NRT's usual preference for wa-modern properties, with charm off the charts and a sense of place few others can match.

cities.text: Local train Niigata->Suibara ~35-40 min (via Niitsu), then ~15 min taxi to Murasugi Onsen.
Joetsu Shinkansen Tokyo->Niigata ~2h, local to Suibara ~40 min, then ~15 min taxi.

inns.name: Aizu Tsuruga Higashiyama Sohonzan
inns.summary: A one-party-per-day private-house ryokan in Higashiyama Onsen, converted in 2022 from the owner's grandfather's architect-built home, funded by the family's horsemeat restaurants and holding nothing back on the room, the minibar or the table. KI-NRT places it among the very best of Tohoku alongside Wabizakura and Kawasemi and says the off-the-charts word of mouth is deserved, after one stay. It combines easily with Atamiso, about an hour away.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a lavish Aizu Buke kaiseki, and since the family runs horsemeat restaurants the basashi runs to rare cuts like tategami and futaego with caviar, and a spinal-cord sashimi KI-NRT calls their favourite horse part. The salt-grilled wild ayu was amazing. Not everything was best-ever, though he left extremely satisfied, and breakfast is a cut above, with iwana sashimi and eel caught that morning and grilled at the counter.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The Suite's own deck has a free-flowing onsen bath fed straight from the source, with a view of the river and a sauna room alongside, and an electronically controlled glass door opens it up for the open-air sensation. KI-NRT calls it a wonderful onsen, and since the house takes one party a day, the bath is yours alone.

service.label: Service
service.text: Sohonzan takes one group of guests a day, which gives an intimacy KI-NRT says properties with several rooms cannot hope to match, and it is wonderfully hosted by the GM, Mr. Monoe, and by Ms. Aya Sakata, who was his room attendant. The one thing missing was some bathroom items (toothbrush, shower cap, shaving kit), which he takes for an oversight, and when he raised it the GM said it would be fixed quickly.

room.label: Room
room.text: The Suite is technically in the basement, but the back of the house sits on an embankment above the river, so it is bright and airy, and it is Japanese-modern: heated tatami floors, electronic curtains and windows, two bathrooms and a sprawling deck with a fire pit. KI-NRT calls the in-room drinks out of control: three dispensers of sake, wine and champagne and a fridge with a wider choice than most refrigerators, all of it complimentary.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Sohonzan is a 1972 house built by a famous architect for the owner's grandfather, and through the gates you see the main house, a gorgeous garden with a koi pond and a detached tea house. The three-storey main house has lounges, dining rooms and a second tea room in a Taisho-era mix of Japanese and Western styles, which KI-NRT enjoyed exploring. Aizu-Wakamatsu's castle and sake breweries are close by, and Ouchi-juku is under an hour away.

cities.text: Tōhoku Shinkansen Tokyo→Kōriyama (~80 min), change to the JR Ban'etsu-West line→Aizu-Wakamatsu (~65–80 min), then a ~15-min taxi to Higashiyama Onsen. ⚠ the Ban'etsu-West crosses snow country.
Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya, cross to a 'Yamabiko'→Kōriyama, then the Ban'etsu-West line→Aizu-Wakamatsu + taxi. ⚠ the Ban'etsu-West crosses snow country.

Reverse of: Ban'etsu West Line Aizu-Wakamatsu→Kōriyama (~65 min), transfer to Tōhoku Shinkansen→Sendai (~40 min), plus the ~15-min Higashiyama Onsen taxi. (Direct Aizu–Sendai highway bus ~2h22 is the no-change alt.)

inns.name: Beniya Mukayu
inns.summary: A stylish Japanese-modern ryokan in Yamashiro Onsen that does almost everything right (a top suite KI-NRT called perfect, in-room onsen, gorgeous grounds, an excellent crab-season kitchen), and then serves dinner in one shared, echoing dining hall with no private or in-room option. That single flaw is why he gave it a rare reserved verdict, is "not in love" with it, and would try neighbors before returning, even as crowds and ryokan first-timers adore it. Book a top suite and the earliest dinner seating.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner in crab season was a definite highlight for KI-NRT, and the food was never his complaint: snow-crab dishes, grilled homemade sesame tofu, charcoal-grilled blackthroat seaperch in dashi, and a Noto-salt gelato with seared monaka, all done to perfection. He puts Nishimuraya and Matsusaki ahead of it for crab, and one quirk is the sushi arriving at the very end, when you are too full to enjoy it. Ikyu diners mark dinner 4.79 out of 5.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has a private open-air bath of Yamashiro onsen water drawn direct from the source, though not the continuously flowing kind. From the Byakuroku Terrace Suite you slide the veranda glass open and soak facing the garden, where the green of the leaves pops out at you (KI-NRT found it mesmerizing). In-room tubs were renewed in 2022 and the public baths rebuilt in 2023, plus a well-known herbal spa. He has not described the public baths.

service.label: Service
service.text: Dinner service was a letdown for KI-NRT: unlike most luxury ryokans, no server is assigned to each group, so different dishes arrived from different hands and each was explained in a different amount of detail, which felt to him like a big hotel restaurant and not like a small family-run ryokan. He has not described the service outside the dining room. The house has a reputation for welcoming foreign and same-sex couples.

room.label: Room
room.text: The Byakuroku Terrace Suite, the top category, is 100 square metres with a separate bedroom and living room, dual vanities, an indoor terrace for cold days and an expansive private balcony over the garden; it was newly renovated when KI-NRT stayed, spotless and airy in earthy tones, and his one-word verdict was perfect, the type of room you spend the entire day in. A January 2022 guest ranked her two nights in Byakuroku among her best-ever stays.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Behind the house is a tranquil moss garden with an old tea house and a stone pagoda, with lush forest all around, and a massive historic tree is lit up at night, which gives the whole place a "mythical" atmosphere. KI-NRT calls the grounds wonderful and the entrance pretty, though the forest is not quite as magical as at Takefue or Chikurintei. Yamashiro Onsen town is a walk away, and a family who stayed loved popping down to explore its shops.

cities.text: Kanazawa→Kaga-Onsen (~15–30 min), then Beniya Mukayu's free on-demand shuttle (~15 min; runs 14:20–18:00, call your arrival time ahead; returns every 30 min 8:45–11:15) — or a ~¥3k taxi.

Hokuriku Shinkansen direct Tokyo→Kaga-Onsen — 2h48 on the best pairing (Maps 2026-08-02, single line, no self-change), then the Beniya shuttle ~15 min (call ahead; inbound window 14:20–18:00). ⚠ Kagayaki skips Kaga-Onsen since the 2024 Tsuruga extension, so it is the through-Hakutaka you want; earlier departures that miss it run 3h06–3h47 with a change at Kanazawa or Tsuruga.

Reverse of: Beniya Mukayu shuttle→Kaga-Onsen (~15 min), 'Tsurugi'→Tsuruga (~37 min), cross-platform change (~10 min), 'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp→Kyoto (~55 min) — 2026-07 audit; the old ~1h30 used a stale pre-extension Thunderbird time.

Reverse of: Yamashiro Onsen sits right by Komatsu Airport: ~15-min taxi to KMQ, the KMQ→Fukuoka hop (~1h40, ~4 daily ANA/ORC), then the subway 2 stops into Hakata (~5 min). ~3.5h door-to-door — the shortest Hokuriku→Kyushu run.
Reverse of: ~15-min taxi to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Nishi-Kyushu relay→Nagasaki via Takeo-Onsen (~2h). ~5.5h door-to-door.
Reverse of: ~15-min taxi to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h17). ~5h door-to-door.

inns.name: Enowa Yufuin
inns.summary: An ultra-modern 18-room newcomer (June 2023) on a hilltop farm above the Yufuin valley, built around Tashi Gyamtso's vegetable-driven cooking, which KI-NRT found eclipsed even SingleThread and called reason alone to stay. Rooms are huge with kakenagashi onsen in every one; service was still green in late 2024, though later guests report no such stumbles. Book a Villa or Pavilion, because most other rooms have no view or pool, and plan the stay around dinner.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Tashi Gyamtso, formerly sous chef at Blue Hill at Stone Barns, runs a farm nearby and builds each day's vegetable-driven dinner on what he picks from the fields that morning. KI-NRT found his creations extraordinary, just barely eclipsing SingleThread, his previous benchmark, and reason alone to stay. japanesegeek's vegetarian wife called it the best food she has ever tasted, and he put it on par with Tokyo's best French restaurants.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own free-flowing (kakenagashi) hot-spring bath, the house's beauty water, and there are no shared baths. The two top Pavilions add a pool on the deck heated by the onsen overflow, which guests have used happily even in February, and KI-NRT counted the in-room onsen and pool among the pluses of his stay. The Hill Top Sauna is booked in private three-hour slots, and the 6 to 9am winter slot catches Yufuin's sea of clouds.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service was polite and professional on KI-NRT's December 2024 stay but nothing like the proactive service at Sanso Murata: he had to call the front desk repeatedly for the same request, the buggy took at least 15 minutes to come, and the stand-in manager seemed inexperienced. On the plus side, towels were refreshed several times a day. japanesegeek found the staff superb and kindly relaxed, and later guests no longer mention the early stumbles.

room.label: Room
room.text: All 18 rooms are ultra-modern and big, and every one has its own onsen bath. The ten villas, eight of 108 square metres and the two 165-square-metre Hilltop Sky Pavilions, add an outdoor onsen and an infinity pool heated by onsen overflow; the eight 78-square-metre hotel rooms have neither. KI-NRT's pavilion was well built, with a few lapses in the bathroom fittings. His pick is a 108-square-metre villa, a true suite for less.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Enowa sits on a hilltop above the Yufuin valley with its own large working farm, in the town KI-NRT calls the country's greatest concentration of luxury ryokans. The two top Pavilions look out over a panoramic sweep of the valley, though Mt. Yufudake is at the far end and off to one side, and most rooms have no view. On winter mornings the valley below fills with Yufuin's sea of clouds, and January days run around 8°C with dustings of snow.

cities.text: Reverse of: Ltd Exp back toward Hakata (~2h10).
Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima-Chūō→Hakata (~1h20), ~4-min platform transfer, then the JR 'Yufu' Ltd Exp Hakata→Yufuin (~2h15). ~3h11 total, all-rail.

Reverse of: By car (~210 km, raw ~2h25 per NAVITIME; budget ~3h): Yufuin IC → Oita Expwy → Tosu JCT → Nagasaki Expwy → Nagasaki IC (~¥5,060). Budget 3h+ in January — the Yufuin IC–Hita IC stretch (~45 km) is an official winter-tire-regulation zone (last winter: 7 days of regulation, 2 of closure); past Hita it's plains, and the Nagasaki Expwy has no regulated section at all. (Transit: Ltd Exp 'Yufu'→Hakata ~2h15 + 'Relay Kamome'/'Kamome' via Takeo, ~3.5h total, 2 changes — 2026-07 audit; rare January snow on the Kyudai line's pass.)

Reverse of: Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin-no-Mori' Yufuin→Kurume (~1h40, ~5/day), Shinkansen Kurume→Kumamoto (~25 min). Scenic alt: the Kyushu Ōdan bus through Kurokawa/Aso, one seat, ~4h15, 3/day. By car ~2.5h via the Yamanami Highway.

Fly to Yufuin: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Oita (OIT) ~1h30 nonstop (frequent ANA/JAL/Solaseed; 2026-07 audit vs flightsfrom/sakuratravel timetables), then a pre-booked FIXED-FARE taxi straight to the inn (~55 min, ¥18,320 incl. tolls — Oita Taxi Assoc., say '定額で') — no bus-schedule or shuttle sync. (Budget alt: airport bus→Yufuin Stn ~55 min, 6/day, ¥1,550pp + the inn shuttle — Enowa's needs reserving ≥3 days ahead.) Far saner than the ~5h45 all-rail haul.

Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin-no-Mori' Hakata→Yufuin (~2h10). ~6h door-to-door. (Oita is Yufuin's own airport but has no Komatsu flight — Hakata is the gateway.)

inns.name: Miyakowasure
inns.summary: A ten-room hideaway in remotest Akita with a source-fed open-air onsen in every room, memorable regional cooking and total silence. KI-NRT called it worth a return, both reviewers left happy, and 8 of 10 fellow guests during his stay were repeaters. The interiors have not been touched since the 2005 opening, and the Edwardian furniture jars against the tatami, so the rooms are tired. You stay for the bath and the quiet and put up with the rooms.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is traditional, creative and built on Akita specialties: cold Inaniwa udon with aged nameko, shark fin with daikon and a Hinai Jidori chicken hot pot. The star was the Iwana Nanban-age, a white-spotted char twice-fried in a tangy vinegar sauce and crisp enough to eat head to tail, which KI-NRT called sublime. Breakfast held its own with three grilled fish and a wild-mushroom dashi, and NZJuniorDoc found the food as good as Satoyama Jujo's.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every one of the ten rooms has an open-air bath fed directly and continuously from the source, and nine of them look over the turquoise Tama River. Kusabue, the top room, is the only one with an indoor bath too, and its hinoki outdoor pair is a traditional tub plus a reclining bath; KI-NRT thinks in-room onsen doesn't get much better than this. The communal Hiba-wood bath is open 24 hours, and the bookable private rock bath is a jacuzzi.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service was excellent overall, largely thanks to Maki Fujiwara, who was hostess, dinner server and breakfast server, grew up near Lake Tazawa and is proud of her region, and annotated the menu with furigana; KI-NRT notes that the same person at both meals is increasingly rare. The one hiccup was a robotic, inflexible man at check-in who insisted on fixing meal times before the private bath slot until KI-NRT firmly asked him to follow their lead.

room.label: Room
room.text: Nothing in the rooms has been renovated since the inn opened in 2005, and it shows. Even Kusabue, the top room, pairs a tatami room with a carpeted Western living room of flamboyant Edwardian furniture (a chandelier, a glittery lamp, pieces that have clearly aged), and with no dedicated bedroom the futons go down after dinner, a setup KI-NRT has never warmed to. He wanted a complete interior redesign.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: A narrow, winding 4km gravel road past a reservoir dead-ends at the inn, so the seclusion is absolute, and when you step out of the car there are no buildings, power lines or traffic noise, just forest and the turquoise Tama River. The grounds have hydrangeas, sakura and onsen fountains and an inner courtyard with a dry rock garden. Indoors the traditional architecture is mixed with flamboyant Edwardian furnishings, which KI-NRT found jarring.

cities.text: Akita Shinkansen 'Komachi' direct Tokyo→Kakunodate (~3h, one seat). Snow-prone on the single-track stretch past Morioka.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01), cross to a through 'Komachi' Ōmiya→Kakunodate (~2h36; Ōmiya→Morioka ~1h51 + Morioka→Kakunodate ~45 min, one train) + ~12-min taxi. Just one change at Ōmiya despite the length. ⚠ Komachi on snow-prone single track past Morioka.
Reverse of: The price of Akita: 'Komachi' Kakunodate→Tokyo (~3h04), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (~2h15) — the longest leg of any route, on the deep-snow Akita branch; a full travel day.
Reverse of: Akita Shinkansen 'Komachi' Kakunodate→Morioka→Sendai as one through train (~2h05, no change), then a ~12-min taxi/inn car at the Kakunodate end (reserve).

inns.name: Mt.Resort Unzen Kyushu Hotel
inns.summary: A luxury hotel rebuilt from scratch as a modern boutique property, right next to Unzen Jigoku, the steaming sulphur hells, with front-row views of them from most rooms and the lounge, and after a posh 2018 renovation it has a rooftop lounge over the hellscape and the feel of an all-inclusive. KI-NRT's three-night stay in a Hanare room was 'almost perfect', with food he puts up with the best ryokans and hotels in Japan, while Nagasaki Joe on a one-night return found the nine-course dinner good but uneven and the hotel hard to beat for a hot-spring stay in a great sightseeing location.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: You choose Japanese or Western-Japanese fusion for both meals, and KI-NRT puts the quality up with Japan's best ryokans and hotels: an abalone steak in abalone-liver cream sauce done to perfection, amazing Nagasaki beef, and a matsutake gohan they could not stop eating. Breakfast, with eggs Benedict and a sea bream meunière, was equally special. Nagasaki Joe found the nine-course dinner good but uneven (tough sashimi) and breakfast the same.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The Hanare rooms have both an indoor and an open-air outdoor onsen bath, which KI-NRT found wonderful, and he counts the onsen quality among the reasons his three nights were almost perfect. The water is Unzen's own, since the hotel stands right beside Unzen Jigoku, the steaming hot-spring hells. Nagasaki Joe, who stayed one night in 2022, says the hotel is hard to beat for hot-spring bathing.

service.label: Service
service.text: Throughout KI-NRT's three nights the manager, Mr. Taura, personally served the meals, an encyclopedia of food and local ingredients, and Hanare guests dine in their own private room. The pacing of the meals was the best he has ever experienced, nine-plus courses in 90 minutes that never felt rushed, because the staff and kitchen keep an eye on how fast you eat so each course arrives when you want it. He calls the staff elegant and friendly.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are those of a modern boutique hotel, with local art, and most of them have a front-row seat to Unzen Jigoku. KI-NRT chose a Hanare, a detached building, for the extra privacy and space: the bedroom is separate from the living room, there are indoor and outdoor onsen baths, and Hanare guests dine in a private room, but you give up the view of the hells that the other rooms have. Nagasaki Joe describes the 2018 renovation as posh.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The hotel stands right next to Unzen Jigoku, the hot-spring hells, and the buildings blend into the landscape without dominating it; from most rooms and the lounge you have a front-row seat to the steaming vents, sulphur smell included (KI-NRT likes it). The grounds are immaculately maintained and the whole place is tranquil. Nagasaki Joe mentions the rooftop lounge over the hells and calls it a great sightseeing location.

cities.text: Rail Hakata to Isahaya, then ~50 min bus/car up to Unzen.
Shinkansen then transfers to Isahaya, then ~50 min bus/car to Unzen.

inns.name: Wanosato

kinrt_rank_claim.quote: My Top 10 Ryokans Overall (in no particular order): [...] Wanosato (near Takayama, Gifu Prefecture)

inns.summary: An eight-room farmhouse ryokan on an idyllic river in the forest outside Takayama, with cooking that fans and detractors alike call superb; KI-NRT found the dining far superior to the equally renowned Honjin Hiranoya Kachoan in town. His 2020 stay surpassed his high expectations, but a 2023 guest found the Garyu villa mouldy and the staff too few and will not return, and a 2024 guest did not enjoy the stay either, so the whole falls short of what the parts alone would suggest. You stay for the setting and the food and should not expect polished upkeep.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Food is the one thing every guest agrees on. KI-NRT called it exquisite and up there with the best of Japan's luxury ryokans: Takayama's forte is vegetables, Hida beef and river fish, and the kitchen is creative with them, from a Hida beef sukiyaki with a broth unlike any he had tasted to a tofu with foie gras he called phenomenal. Even Koen dc, the 2023 guest who will not return, put the meals among the best of a Michelin-heavy trip.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The hot-spring water is only in the communal baths (men's and women's) in the thatched main house; the in-room tubs are plain hot water and there is no open-air bath in the rooms. With only eight rooms the communal bath is rarely occupied, and KI-NRT went twice and never shared it with another soul. He does not think the lack of in-room onsen is a big deal, though it is not ideal.

service.label: Service
service.text: On KI-NRT's 2020 stay service was discreet, and everyone was professional and charming but rather reserved (except Momoka, the second night's dinner server, a big ball of charm, energy and sweetness); nothing went unattended and there were no major flaws, though he was not expecting big-hotel service from eight rooms. Koen dc in August 2023 found the staff welcoming, friendly and hardworking but too few, so the service he expected was not there.

room.label: Room
room.text: The Garyu villa, one of four detached villas among the eight rooms, is 110m² on the riverbank, with two sitting rooms, a bedroom, a big living area with an open irori hearth, old beams and a bathroom with shower and wooden tub, and you hear the river from the room; KI-NRT found it well-appointed. Koen dc stayed in the same villa in 2023 and found it mouldy and dusty on entering, with housekeeping too thin to keep up houses this large.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Wanosato is eight rooms, four of them detached villas, beside an idyllic river in a gorgeous forest about 25 minutes by car from Takayama, around a gassho-zukuri thatched farmhouse whose lounge has an open irori hearth, exposed beams and antiques on the walls. It feels a world away from town, and even Michaeljinnyc, who did not enjoy his 2024 stay, posted his photos because the scenery deserved it. Koen dc found the grounds poorly kept in 2023.

cities.text: Reverse of: Nohi/Hokutetsu highway bus Takayama Nohi Bus Center→Kanazawa Stn west exit via Shirakawa-gō (~2h15, direct, reserve — the bus centre is at Takayama Stn, a 7-min walk from the inn). No rail link exists; the bus is the fast way.

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya (~2h30), change ~15 min to a Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Tokyo (~1h42) + hotel/station ends. (Via Toyama is nominally quicker — 'Hida' ~1h30 + Hokuriku Shinkansen ~2h06 — but only ~4 Toyama through-trains run per day.)

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya (~2h30; 10/day — hourly only ~11:30–16:30, with 2h gaps outside), ~15-min transfer to a Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (34 min). Alt with NO change: Hida 36 departs Takayama 15:33 direct to Kyoto, arr 19:17. ⚠ The Takayama line is snow-exposed — JR Central posts 大雪 advisories most Januaries; keep same-day slack. (All-reserved Dec 25–Jan 5; mixed seating otherwise.) Equal-time alternative that dodges that exposure: the Nohi highway bus Takayama→Nagoya + the same Nozomi — Maps returns this chain, not the Hida, as its three fastest (3h25–3h33 station-to-station), so take whichever the weather favours.

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya (~2h25; 10/day, hourly only ~11:30–16:30, 2h gaps outside), ~20-min cross-platform transfer to a Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Nozomi' Nagoya→Shin-Osaka (~50 min, frequent), then the Midōsuji subway Shin-Osaka→Umeda/Namba (~5–10 min) + the walk to the hotel. Two changes, at Nagoya and Shin-Osaka. ⚠ the Takayama Line is snow-exposed — JR Central posts 大雪 advisories most Januaries, and Dec 25–Jan 5 is all-reserved; keep same-day slack. Equal-time alternative that dodges the exposure: the Nohi highway bus Takayama→Nagoya + the same Nozomi. Sources: japan-guide Takayama access; JR Central Tōkaidō/Takayama Line timetables.

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya, ~2h25 direct, 10 a day (hourly only ~11:30–16:30, 2h gaps outside), ¥5,610 unreserved / ¥6,140 reserved, + the 7-min walk from the inn/old town. ⚠ Snow-exposed — JR Central posts 大雪 advisories most Januaries, all-reserved Dec 25–Jan 5. Equal-time alternative when the line is under an advisory: the Nohi highway bus Takayama Nōhi BC→Meitetsu BC Nagoya, ~2h45, reserved.

inns.name: Atamiso
inns.summary: An eleven-room ryokan above the Gohyakugawa River near Koriyama that ran effectively private when KI-NRT stayed in May 2022, taking just two parties at a time, with chef Asano serving and explaining every course himself. He calls it one of the preeminent ryokans in Japan and prefers it to its flashier neighbor Suzukane, and only the rooms, which show slight signs of age, count against it. It has been closed since February 2025 for onsen plumbing work and a full renovation, so confirm it has reopened before planning around it.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Chef Satoshi Asano served all twelve courses himself on KI-NRT's 2022 stay and explained each, down to why he simmered a dish instead of making it a soup. The cooking leans to traditional local flavors, including Aizu Kozuyu, the old feudal lords' soup, which tasted of nothing special but was a pleasure to be served, and not every course was awesome. Breakfast had more energy and passion than at most inns because Asano supervises that too.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The water is Bandai Atami hot spring, a favorite of KI-NRT's, and the two communal open-air baths, both with a river view, are each given to one party for the whole stay; he had the women's bath and found it calming, peaceful and oh so relaxing, though neither is large. Only Sogetsu of the two special rooms has an in-room open-air onsen (he had its keys while sleeping in Tenga no Ma). The onsen plumbing has been under repair since February 2025.

service.label: Service
service.text: With only two groups in the house the service is extremely personal, and you get to know the staff even in one night. KI-NRT's butler, having heard that Mrs. KI-NRT writes readings beside the kanji on menus for him, brought out a dinner menu she had inscribed with katakana herself, and at check-out he found chef Asano washing the windows of their car. Michaeljinnyc, on arrival in June 2024, called it completely unforgettable.

room.label: Room
room.text: Tenga no Ma, the special room with the terrific view over the Gohyakugawa River, is reasonably spacious, with a separate living room and a tatami room where the futons come out at night. Nothing is shiny and new (one sink, slow internet, a slightly dated bathroom), but it is well maintained. Sogetsu, the other special room, has no view but an open-air onsen bath. Over half of the eleven rooms are very small and humble, so book a special room.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Atamiso sits on the banks of the Gohyakugawa River in lush vegetation, with a spectacularly landscaped small garden, and the mix of landscaping and natural setting brought KI-NRT's heart rate down on arrival. It is quiet and quaint, the tranquil, secluded inn he sets against busier ones like Yamagata The Takinami. It is a backwater with not much around, which suits it if you have a car and want to hike Goshikinuma Ponds and Mt. Bandai.

cities.text: Tōhoku Shinkansen Tokyo→Kōriyama (~80 min; 'Yamabiko' stops, most 'Hayabusa' skip Kōriyama), change to the JR Ban'etsu-West line ~15 min to Bandai-Atami + short taxi (reserve the inn car). Inland Fukushima — periodic January snow, but the main line is reliable.
Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h, avoiding central Tokyo), cross to a 'Yamabiko'→Kōriyama, then the Ban'etsu-West local→Bandai-Atami + shuttle. Ōmiya + Kōriyama changes.
Reverse of: JR Ban'etsu-West Bandai-Atami→Kōriyama (~15 min), change to the Tōhoku 'Yamabiko'→Sendai (~30 min) — the region-hub leg, researched rather than estimated.

inns.name: Hotel Ridge
inns.summary: An intimate nine-room Otsuka-owned property on a ridge above the Naruto Strait, and KI-NRT's default refined stop for anyone entering Shikoku from Osaka or Kobe. Service is the strongest part (staff who remembered his wine picks and his room from a cherry-blossom stay years back), backed by a strait panorama he calls breathtaking at sunrise. His first stay left him lukewarm, closing with 'not that type of place'. The 2023 Zeiso villa fixes that gap, and his return ended with 'mission accomplished'.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is split between Banri-so (kaiseki) and California Table (French-Japanese fusion). KI-NRT found Banri-so solid with standouts (Naruto Strait sea bream, an Awa beef katsu sandwich he calls the best he has had), but the grilled courses lacked distinction and the cherry salmon was overcooked. California Table was only good on his first visit, but the lobster teppanyaki and Awa wagyu were exceptional on his return. Breakfasts never repeat.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The hotel drilled 1,500 metres for a hot spring, but the yield only supports the gender-segregated communal baths. Each side has a small indoor and outdoor bath, one-person size, and the water is disinfected, partly recirculated and reheated because it comes up lukewarm. KI-NRT still enjoyed it but says it will not satisfy anyone after a serious onsen. The rooms have heated tap water in an excellent setup with a push-button jacuzzi.

service.label: Service
service.text: The service is impeccable and it held across a four-year gap. On KI-NRT's return the same staff were there, including manager Takeshi Hara, and they remembered his wine selections, his wife's preference for warm drinking water and, when he tested a younger staff member, even that they had stayed in Room 103 during cherry blossom season. Guests are chauffeured to dinner in a Toyota Century although both restaurants are a short walk away.

room.label: Room
room.text: All nine rooms face the Naruto Strait, but the eight standard ones are identical 60 sqm rooms with Western furnishings (no tatami or futon even in the Waso type) and a sitting area of a small table and two chairs, which KI-NRT found underwhelming next to the rest of the property. Zeiso, added in 2023 by merging two rooms into a 120 sqm standalone villa, has a more contemporary Japanese look, and his verdict on it was mission accomplished.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The hotel sits on a quiet ridge at the northeastern tip of Shikoku, and all nine rooms look out over the Naruto Strait to the Great Naruto Bridge and Awaji Island. Watching the bridge glow at sunrise was, for KI-NRT, a breathtaking moment and reason enough to plan another return. A dry rock garden sits outside Banri-so, and the Otsuka Museum of Art and the Naruto whirlpools are a 5-10 minute taxi ride away, which he thinks justifies two nights.

cities.text: Hotel Ridge is roughly 30 min by car from Tokushima Awaodori Airport and about 40 min from central Tokushima.
Highway bus from Osaka across the Akashi-Kaikyo and Naruto bridges via Awaji is about 2h to Naruto, then a short taxi to the resort.

inns.name: Iki Retreat Kairi Murakami
inns.summary: Onko Chishin's 2018 rebuild gave remote Iki its only luxury inn: 12 bay-facing rooms, each with a gold, source-fed onsen on the deck, and a kitchen that turns the island's uni, grouper and Iki beef into its reason to exist. KI-NRT says it isn't in his top ten and 'I don't feel it needs to be': it is unique and memorable, especially the onsen and the food, without being a place to build a trip around, and Iki itself is not somewhere he would send a first-time (or tenth-time) visitor to Japan.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is at the counter, kaiseki one night and teppanyaki the next, and on both of KI-NRT's nights there was copious uni, abalone, fish and Iki beef, which he puts alongside Kobe and Matsusaka. The 'Mama Nakase' tomatoes were so sweet he asked whether syrup had been added. He stops short of calling it the best meal of his life, though some dishes were among his most memorable, and pWei found seafood and produce of a quality rare these days.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All 12 rooms have their own open-air onsen bath on the deck, fed straight from the source and looking over Yunomoto Bay, and the water turns gold once it meets the air from its high iron content, much like the gold onsen of Arima. There are also communal baths and a private bath you can rent in 45-minute slots. KI-NRT called them wonderful hot springs and sorely missed them a year later at the Goto sister property, which has none.

service.label: Service
service.text: The staff were all enthusiastic and professional, many of them born and raised on Iki, full of advice on the island and able to explain every dish in detail. The receptionist, who also handles pre-arrival email, was a big ball of sunshine whose replies came promptly and went well beyond the question asked. pWei in 2025 found the service good, with GM and executive chef Seiichi Ota explaining the courses himself and free pick-ups at the ports.

room.label: Room
room.text: All 12 rooms face Yunomoto Bay, and all but the entry-level Corner Tatami Room have Western beds. The top room is the 120-square-metre Kairi Suite, the only one with both a tatami room and a Western living room with couches, so if sitting on the floor is not for you, get it. KI-NRT found it tastefully done, a nice blend of traditional and modern. Two oddities: the bathroom has a urinal, and there is only one sink.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Kairi is on the northwest side of Iki, a remote island between Japan and Korea, with commanding views over Yunomoto Bay; there is no garden, and the ocean view stands in for one. Iki is not somewhere KI-NRT would send a first-time visitor to Japan. It is paradise for history buffs, though, with the Harunotsuji Yayoi-period site and Kojima Shrine on an islet you can reach only at low tide, and even in peak season it stays blissfully uncrowded.

cities.text: Nishitetsu bus #99 Hakata Stn→Hakata Port (~20 min), Kyushu Yusen jetfoil 'Venus'→Iki, Ashibe/Gonoura (~1h05–1h10), then the inn's free shuttle (~15 min, reserve). The car ferry is the slower ~2h20 alternative; winter thins frequency, not duration.
Reverse of: Jetfoil→Hakata Port (~65–70 min), bus to Hakata Stn (~20 min), 'Sakura'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h35). Winter seas suspend jetfoils — the ~2h20 car ferry usually still runs.

Reverse of: ORC turboprop Iki→Nagasaki (30 min, 2/day — ORC's only Iki route), then the airport limousine bus→Nagasaki Stn (~45 min). Winter wind can cancel the small plane — fallback: jetfoil→Hakata + rail (~3.5h).
Reverse of: Jetfoil→Hakata Port (~65–70 min), bus→Hakata Stn, 'Sakura'→Kumamoto (~38 min). Winter seas suspend jetfoils — the car ferry runs.

inns.name: Iwanoyu
inns.summary: An 18-room Taisho-era onsen ryokan in the Nagano mountains that is a fixture on the stay-before-you-die lists, and at roughly 40,000 yen a head it is a screaming bargain by top-ryokan standards, which is exactly why KI-NRT braced for gotchas and found them, all in the lower room categories. Onsen, kitchen, staff and grounds are top notch, but the Sengotei shower and missing bath are teeth-gnashing. Both reviewers left net positive and would return, but only for Senzantei, the four rooms that erase most of the flaws and that you book by phone 11 months ahead or off a long waitlist.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: All meals are served in private rooms, and KI-NRT found the kaiseki exquisite: foraged mountain vegetables, freshwater fish, local rice and beef, a sashimi trio of snow trout, scalded char and carp, and a dobinmushi that used maitake in place of matsutake and tasted awesome anyway. Few ingredients are delicacies, but he felt the kitchen did a terrific job with humble Nagano produce. zander86 called the food fantastic.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: None of the rooms has an onsen bath, so all the bathing is shared or rental: a 24-hour gender-segregated open-air daiyokujo, four first-come private rental baths (a fifth is reserved for Senzantei guests) and a huge co-ed cave bath with Romanesque columns like Istanbul's Basilica Cistern, swimwear provided. The water runs lukewarm, which let KI-NRT soak longer, though he wanted it hotter. zander86 preferred the private baths to the cave.

service.label: Service
service.text: There is no okami on site and no dedicated room attendant, and the staff count is much larger than at other ryokans of this size, but the staff behave as if they were part-owners, everyone seemed to take pride in working there and to care about the guests, and KI-NRT found the service friendly and eager. zander86 called the staff amazing. Ms. Ogasawara, a local server who speaks decent English, is worth asking for if you do not speak Japanese.

room.label: Room
room.text: Book one of the four Senzantei rooms: a separate bedroom (elsewhere the tatami room doubles as one), better river views, the only in-room baths (ordinary tubs) and unlimited use of their own rental bath, and zander86 found his well kept with a supremely comfortable futon. KI-NRT's Sengotei room had Taisho charm and heated floors, but no WiFi, no bath, one sink and a cheap plastic shower the size of a porta potty, which he called unforgivable.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The grounds stunned KI-NRT even at the tail of foliage season: a river bisects the property, crossed by a bridge, with man-made creeks and mini waterfalls between the buildings, foot baths and pots of flowers along the path, and art pieces throughout. Inside it is Taisho-era old Japan, a mix of Japanese and Western decor that he felt fit the mood, with three lounges. The property is so large that zander86 seldom met other guests.

cities.text: Reverse of: Ltd Exp 'Azusa' Kamisuwa/Shimosuwa→Shinjuku (~2h13–2h22, direct), plus the ~5–10-min inn car. Suwa's real advantage: the Azusa reaches it ~25 min before Matsumoto, so it is the closest north inn to Tokyo after the Gunma pair. Azusa timetable: Shinjuku→Kamisuwa 2h13–2h22, Kamisuwa→Matsumoto 24–25 min. Kamisuwa (Sui Suwako, ~10-min car) and Shimosuwa (Iwanoyu, ~5-min car) are one stop apart, so they share this loc.

Reverse of: Via Matsumoto: 'Shinano'→Nagano (~50 min), change to the Hokuriku Shinkansen→Kanazawa (~65–70 min). Getting to Matsumoto from Suwa (inn car + the 24–25-min 'Azusa', then a self-handled change onto the onward train) costs one MORE transfer and ~20 min vs the Matsumoto counterpart — priced in here; the onward rail is identical and already researched.

inns.name: Kohanyu
inns.summary: A four-room adults-only hideaway on Shikoku, built by a retired couple around a lucky spring strike and the owner's world-class vintage audio collection, where KI-NRT came expecting the river and the food and left most moved by the sound. The cooking is honest local organic fare that he puts below top-10 kaiseki, but the water, the villa acoustics and the personal welcome healed mind and body, and he calls it a refined, adult hideaway. Rakuten's reviewers give it a perfect 5.0, and a member's account elsewhere is just as enthusiastic.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kaiseki is built on Kochi produce, with pesticide-free vegetables from the inn's own garden (co-owner Masayo Nishimura is a certified vegetable sommelier), dashi made daily from bonito, kelp and baby sardines, bonito sashimi and Tosa Akaushi beef, a rare local breed. KI-NRT's highlights were a chawanmushi with brown-rice mochi and fried taro in ankake sauce; for him the meal was memorable but not a top-10 kaiseki, and breakfast is lighter.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The spring is the owners' own, struck when they drilled for a bath at their retirement home, an isotonic spring at 24.5°C with slightly opaque golden nigori water that fizzes gently with bicarbonate, neither filtered nor recirculated. Each of the four rooms has an open-air bath over the river where the water is heated only as it enters the tub, which keeps its richer texture, while the public bath heats it in a tank and loses a little.

service.label: Service
service.text: With only four groups a night the attention is personal. Ms. Yamasaki at dinner and Ms. Ferchichi at breakfast were engaging and knowledgeable and eager to explain each dish (Ms. Ferchichi's husband is Tunisian and speaks fluent English), attentive without being intrusive. After dinner the owner, Mr. Nishimura, invited KI-NRT to AEL HALL, his own home theatre, for about an hour of opera, jazz and orchestral performances through Altec speakers.

room.label: Room
room.text: The four rooms are named for their vintage speaker systems (Paragon, McIntosh, Altec and Western Electric) and beyond the audio differ little. KI-NRT's 100-square-metre Western Suite is a villa engineered for sound, with Sonus Faber speakers set into a counter aligned with the river horizon and a 1972 Western Electric tube amp so clear he could pinpoint each musician. Floor-to-ceiling glass puts you over the river, and no room has a television.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Kohanyu is a secluded plot at the edge of the Monobe River in a remote corner of Kochi, where the water is a deep green framed by lush vegetation and the one man-made structure across the river is mostly hidden by trees, so the view is nearly untouched. The lounge looks straight out at it, with jazz through massive Electro Voice speakers, more than 2,000 CDs to borrow and a deck with its own speakers. Simply gazing out felt restorative.

inns.name: Minamikan
inns.summary: A renowned but still underrated 16-room Matsue ryokan that KI-NRT calls by far the top in all of Shimane, where he loved a full 3-night stay in Mizu no Oto, the 121-square-metre suite with its own excellent onsen bath. The famous dry rock garden, which is particularly picturesque at night, and the castle-town location add to it, and the value comes up in nearly every account, since even the top suite ran 40,000 yen per person half board. All three stays were happy ones, though nobody in the thread has written about the service or the rooms in any detail.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Elaborate kaiseki, served in a private room in the main building and built on local Shimane ingredients, which KI-NRT thought was done to great effect. Nobody has singled out a particular dish, and the praise is for the spread as a whole.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The Mizu no Oto suite has its own onsen bath, which KI-NRT called excellent. Nobody in the thread has written about the communal baths, so if bathing matters to you, book that suite.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here, though all three stays were happy ones.

room.label: Room
room.text: The inn has 16 rooms, and the one KI-NRT stayed in, Mizu no Oto ('the sound of water'), is the tokubetsu-shitsu in the annex building, an enormous 121 square metres with a bedroom, a dining room and a Japanese-style living room. Nobody in the thread has written about the furnishings or the condition of the rooms.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Minamikan sits right on the water in Matsue with one of the most famous dry rock gardens in all of Japan, particularly picturesque at night, and it is an 8-minute walk from the amazing Matsue Castle and about 45 minutes by car or bus from Izumo Taisha, one of the most important shrines in the country. Fc912 found Tottori and Shimane as a region peaceful, with few tourists and many sites to explore, and particularly enjoyed visiting Yuushien.

cities.text: Okayama to Matsue ~2h35 on Yakumo LEX, then ~5 min taxi to Minamikan.
Izumo Airport to Matsue Stn ~30 min by connecting bus, then ~5 min taxi.

inns.name: Onyado Kawasemi
inns.summary: A twelve-room Iizaka Onsen ryokan where every room has an open-air onsen bath and meals served in the room, set around a pond garden, with a kitchen whose Japanese reputation drew KI-NRT there. He left an admirer, and the fresh-tatami upkeep surprised him for a place in the boonies. Against that stands the January 2025 stay by jpit2107, who found it luxurious but dated and soulless, very comfortable yet not charming, in a locale not worth the trip from Tokyo on its own. It belongs as one stop on a Tohoku circuit, which is how KI-NRT places it in his own Tohoku routes.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The executive chef joined when the ryokan opened 27 years ago and has run the kitchen for over a decade. KI-NRT found dinner exceptional, though not head and shoulders above the best ryokan meals he has had, and liked how local and inventive it was: a lobster clay pot under a savory sabayon, a shinjo soup built around a foie gras cake. Breakfast was uninspiring. A January 2025 guest called the food good, heavy on status ingredients like karasumi.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every one of the twelve rooms has its own open-air onsen bath, and KI-NRT thought so much of the one in his Wabisuke suite, which looks over the pond and garden and is stylish and in good condition, that he never tried the gender-separated communal bathhouse, since he could not imagine it being better. He called the onsen awesome. A January 2025 couple had their first private onsen here and found it lovely, and the shared bath nice too.

service.label: Service
service.text: The one drawback in KI-NRT's stay was the nakai who served the room, an older lady who was formulaic, rushed her explanation of each course as if she wanted it out of the way, and did not read the situation, so she was not as warm as the butlers at other top properties, though nothing about her was rude. The operation around her runs to a very high standard, and the staff skew older than at Satonoyu. The January 2025 couple had no complaints.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are traditional but felt fresh to KI-NRT, with the smell of new tatami and none of the wear of old properties; you sleep on futons and sit on zabuton, since there is no chair. Book Wabisuke, one of the two special rooms (the other is a maisonette, which he does not like), with three living areas and a private deck over the pond and garden. A January 2025 couple found their room very comfortable but dated and soulless.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The property is built around a manicured garden with a gorgeous pond in the middle, very green with moss and trees, and flowers in front of the rooms (azaleas outside KI-NRT's in May); he calls it every bit as picturesque as Satonoyu, whose beauty is natural where Kawasemi's is tended. The surroundings do the ryokan no favors, though. A January 2025 couple found Iizaka Onsen, at least in winter, about as charming as a suburban cul-de-sac.

cities.text: Tōhoku Shinkansen Tokyo→Fukushima (~90 min), change to the Fukushima Kōtsū Iizaka line→Iizaka Onsen (~20–25 min, runs ~every 30 min).

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01), Tōhoku 'Yamabiko' Ōmiya→Fukushima (~1h07), then the Iizaka tram (~23 min) + shuttle. Two changes (Ōmiya, Fukushima→tram); the Tōhoku trunk is snow-reliable.
Reverse of: Iizaka line→Fukushima, Tōhoku Shinkansen→Tokyo, Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto.
Reverse of: Fukushima Kōtsū Iizaka Line→Fukushima (~23 min), Tōhoku Shinkansen→Sendai (~25 min), plus the inn's ~10-min courtesy pickup at the Iizaka end.

inns.name: Satoyama Jujo
inns.summary: A 14-room design ryokan in Niigata snow country built around Keiko Kuwakino's foraged, vegetable-driven cooking at Sanaburi, which KI-NRT says gets no better anywhere than here and at Enowa. Book The House Izumi, the huge restored farmhouse with its own source-fed bath, because the main-building rooms are bland by comparison. All three stays across two winters were enthusiastic, and there is no dissent.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is at Sanaburi in the main building, where Keiko Kuwakino cooks mostly from foraged mountain vegetables and an astonishing variety of mushrooms, with several fish courses and sometimes wild boar or deer. KI-NRT called the kotake mushroom risotto on Minamiuonuma Koshihikari rice a masterpiece and says vegetable-led cooking gets no better than here and Enowa, with a slight nod to Enowa. Ask for one of the private rooms in advance.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The House Izumi has its own open-air onsen bath fed by a spring that rises directly beneath the house, which makes it the only place with access to the Echigo Yukiguni Onsen, plus a sauna. The main building has a communal daiyokujo with an open-air rotenburo, and a December guest who came for snow bathing found the view from it amazing. Only a handful of the 12 main-building rooms have onsen of their own, so the rest rely on the communal bath.

service.label: Service
service.text: Arrivals at The House Izumi are met by a staff member who handles check-in there, and a private shuttle runs the 10 to 15 minutes between the house and the main building, which you use at least once for dinner at Sanaburi. There are English-speaking staff on hand. When February snow stuck sirky's transfer vans a few hundred metres from the entrance, everyone walked in and he still called the stay great. Nobody has complained about the service.

room.label: Room
room.text: The House Izumi is a restored 182-square-metre kominka farmhouse for one party a night, which KI-NRT found "huge, private, comfortable and just quirky enough to be memorable", with several living and tatami rooms, a sitting area for the valley view, a sauna and an open-air bath. The 35 to 50-square-metre main-building rooms seem kind of bland by comparison, and only a handful have onsen. Snag Izumi if it is available.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The House Izumi sits on a small hill above the Minamiuonuma valley, ringed by mountains, in the rice region KI-NRT agrees grows Japan's best Koshihikari, and this is snow country, buried all winter (the snowbound view from the communal rotenburo was the highlight of a December stay). The main building is charming, but in November 2024 its grounds and koi ponds were ripped apart by relandscaping, which is probably finished by now.

cities.text: Jōetsu Shinkansen Tokyo→Echigo-Yuzawa (~75 min), then ~30 min by car (inn can arrange).

Reverse of: ⚠ This leg used to encode 2.5h via the Hokuhoku line — that was the HAKUTAKA LIMITED EXPRESS, whose last run was 13 March 2015 (replaced by the Hokuriku Shinkansen; the name moved to a Tokyo–Kanazawa shinkansen). The Hokuhoku's own Snow Rabbit rapid then went in March 2023, leaving all-stops locals. Modern route is all-Shinkansen with ONE change: ~25-min inn car/flat-¥5,000 taxi to Echigo-Yuzawa, Jōetsu 'Toki'→Takasaki (~22 min), cross to the Hokuriku 'Hakutaka'→Kanazawa (~2h05, timetabled; timed pairings run the station chain in 2h55–3h00 — 2026-07-29 re-check against the live timetable, was priced 2h15–18 + 30) . ~3h30 door-to-door. (Hokuhoku alt via Jōetsumyōkō is ~3h40–4h over 2–3 changes on a sparse line where half the trains terminate at Muikamachi and no IC cards are accepted — no faster, far less robust.)
Reverse of: Echigo-Yuzawa→Jōetsu 'Toki'→Tokyo (same-station change), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto. The cleanest northern Kyoto exit — one transfer; snow risk is the inn access road, not the rail.
Reverse of: Echigo-Yuzawa→Ōmiya (~50 min), change to Tōhoku Shinkansen 'Hayabusa'→Sendai (~1h20) — all Shinkansen, one change.

inns.name: Tsuchiyu Bettei Satonoyu
inns.summary: A seven-room hideaway deep in the Fukushima mountains, built around Shinpeki, a two-level private rotenburo beside a forest stream that KI-NRT ranks with Takefue's best bath. Setting and service run at the level of Tohoku's top inns, and the kitchen is the one relative weakness, finely crafted but below the region's best tables. Book Shinpeki the moment you arrive, because it can only be reserved on the day and the slots go fast.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a Tohoku kaiseki served in your room or in a private koshitsu dining room, and the dishes are finely crafted: KI-NRT's standouts were the clear soup with sea bream in a kudzu coating that locks in the umami, and the inro-mushi of steamed Spanish mackerel, crab and kabocha under a glossy crab gin-an. He found the food satisfying but not as memorable as at his next two ryokan stops.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There are no communal baths, only four private bathing areas booked in 45-minute slots, plus the in-room baths, and the spring water is soft and silky. Shinpeki is the one to take: an upper rock bath and a hinoki tub lower down beside the forest stream, and KI-NRT ranks it with Takefue's Chikurin no Yu among the most blissful private open-air onsens he has soaked in. The others felt anticlimactic after it, though Minahada is pretty decent.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service was fantastic and personal: Kazuki, a warm and welcoming local, handled check-in, looked after them and served dinner, and Serina ran breakfast and the mornings just as expertly. The house also sells only seven of its nine rooms so that every guest gets a Shinpeki slot, the guest-first approach KI-NRT most appreciates in a high-end ryokan, where profit never overshadows hospitality.

room.label: Room
room.text: Kason is the only stand-alone villa and the only suite, a few steps from the main building down a path lined with weeping cherries, and it has a bedroom with Western-style beds, a living room, an empty washitsu for extra futons and an impressive open-air stone bath, expertly carved and set into its surroundings. The other eight rooms looked pleasant, and all have heated floors, as most top Tohoku ryokans do. Get Kason if you can.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Satonoyu is deep in the Fukushima mountains at the bottom of a steep hill of hairpin turns, ringed by untouched forest, and KI-NRT recalls the setting as awe-inspiring; where Kawasemi's beauty is a manicured garden, Satonoyu's is the natural environment. A short trail drops from the side entrance into the valley past a creek of wild watercress, serow roam nearby, and mid-May's shinryoku green or the autumn leaves are the seasons to aim for.

cities.text: Tōhoku Shinkansen Tokyo→Fukushima (~90 min direct), then the ~25-min taxi to Tsuchiyu Onsen — the same taxi connector used on every other Fukushima-hub leg (tsuchiyu>akayu, tanigawa>tsuchiyu, etc). Skip the Fukushima Kōtsū public bus: it's sparse (a 2h15 midday gap) and was mistakenly used for this leg only, inflating it to 3.75h.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01 'Kagayaki', avoiding central Tokyo), cross to the Tōhoku 'Yamabiko' Ōmiya→Fukushima (~1h07), then ~25-min taxi to Tsuchiyu. Single clean change at Ōmiya on reliable lines.
Reverse of: ~25-min taxi down to Fukushima, Tōhoku Shinkansen Fukushima→Tokyo (~95 min, same-station change), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (~2h15).

Tōhoku Shinkansen Sendai→Fukushima (~25 min), then the ~25-min taxi up to Tsuchiyu Onsen (Satonoyu runs NO station shuttle — ¥5,440 fixed-fare taxi from the west exit; it will meet the ¥840 Tsuchiyu bus stop if told ahead). Same connector as every Fukushima-hub Tsuchiyu leg.

inns.name: Yamagata The Takinami
inns.summary: A 19-room, street-facing ryokan in Akayu Onsen, remade in 2017 under a magazine editor's direction, with a spring-fed bath in every room and counter-seated kaiseki built on obscure Yamagata mountain ingredients, cuisine KI-NRT ranks top-10, possibly top-5, of every ryokan he has tried. Book KURA01, the 129 m² first-floor suite with a private garden and volcanic-rock tub, which is the only room he considered worth staying in. It is a lively, social house where you are constantly involved, and he enjoyed that even though he usually prefers solitude.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kaiseki was spectacular and, KI-NRT says, the most unique he has ever had: overwhelmingly Yamagata ingredients with subtle European touches, from a course of ten wild mountain vegetables of which even he knew only half to rice-fed koi sashimi in umeboshi dashi and fried chou pastry with butterbur-shoot gelato. Mrs. KI-NRT calls it the best meal of her life, and he ranks the kitchen in his top 10, possibly top 5, of all ryokans he has tried.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has an in-room onsen fed directly from the spring; first-floor rooms have tubs carved from Zao volcanic rock, which KI-NRT says gives a more authentic soak because the water meets less air, while upstairs rooms have hinoki tubs filled from above. White yunohana flakes of minerals float on the water, and KURA01 adds an open-air hot-stone bath in its garden. The communal bath is small, but he had it to himself both times.

service.label: Service
service.text: Shortly after check-in guests are invited to a complimentary tasting of Yamagata sake, followed by a demonstration of juwari (100% buckwheat) soba that later turns up at dinner, and on KI-NRT's stay sake sommelier Mr. Hirayama ran it with an engaging talk on the property's history and local culture. He calls it a wonderfully hosted ryokan and one of the rare places where he did not mind being constantly involved.

room.label: Room
room.text: KURA01, a one-of-a-kind 129m² first-floor suite in a converted storehouse with a private garden and open-air stone bath, is refined and sophisticated and the only room KI-NRT judged worth staying in. The other rooms are 60m² or less, many of them two-storey maisonettes he does not care for, and from photos their furnishings look cheap by comparison. There is no floor heating, which he calls a significant drawback for a Tohoku winter.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn is a 19-room house facing the street in Akayu Onsen, so it has none of the private, tranquil atmosphere of a small secluded ryokan like Atamiso, and you meet other guests often. The Edo-period main building was remade in 2017 under magazine editor Toru Iwase into farmhouse bones with avant-garde decor. Seasonal outings (a cherry-blossom walk to Eboshiyama Park, summer fireflies, a dawn observation deck) suit guests without a car.

cities.text: Yamagata Shinkansen 'Tsubasa' direct Tokyo→Akayu (~2h20) — pick a train that stops at Akayu — then a short taxi/inn shuttle.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01), Tōhoku 'Yamabiko' Ōmiya→Fukushima (~1h07), change to the 'Tsubasa' over the Itaya pass→Akayu (~52 min) + short taxi. Two changes (Ōmiya, Fukushima). ⚠ heavy January delay exposure on the final Tsubasa leg.
Reverse of: 'Tsubasa' Akayu→Tokyo (~2h19), Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (~2h15) — one clean change, but the 'Tsubasa' has a winter-suspension history.

Reverse of: Yamagata Shinkansen 'Tsubasa' Akayu→Fukushima (~35 min — a SE backtrack), transfer to a northbound Tōhoku Shinkansen→Sendai (~25 min), plus a 5-min taxi/inn shuttle at the Akayu end (reserve).

inns.name: Chalet Ivy Jozankei
inns.summary: A 2019 all-suite riverside ryokan that KI-NRT calls Jozankei's premier luxury stay, with Aman-grade design, an involved okami and memorable Hokkaido kaiseki, an easy hop from Sapporo. The one drawback is the bathing, because the source water is tempered with tap water and there is no open-air bath, so Takinoya still wins on onsen while Chalet Ivy wins nearly everything else. Both first-hand stays were happy ones, with nothing said against it.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner was the highlight of KI-NRT's stay: A5 Hida beef wrapped in komatsuna, local sashimi and above all a miso-marinated abura bozu (skillfish) with fried sakura leaves and a condensed-milk hollandaise, full of good fat and flavor. He found the two-hour meal far superior to his dinner at Ao no Za, and breakfast impressed him equally. Stays include a preloaded card for the self-serve alcohol dispenser, and there is a lounge with free snacks.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All 26 suites have their own onsen tub, and the gender-segregated communal bath is modest in size and often blissfully empty, with a full spa, a sauna and a gym alongside. The water comes from the Jozankei source but is cut with tap water to bring the 88°C spring down to 41°C, and KI-NRT wished for a more advanced system like Myoken Ishiharaso's and for a terrace with an open-air bath. Takinoya has purer water and bigger communal baths.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT calls the service outstanding, better than at the Tsuruga Group's luxury properties. The okami, Mayumi Yamamoto, was the first hospitality hire and spent 18 months helping develop the place before it opened, and her presence is felt throughout as she warmly interacts with guests. kyeung2 found the English-speaking staff very friendly, and they picked him up at the bus stop and arranged his car to the airport.

room.label: Room
room.text: Every suite is at least 67 square metres with its own onsen tub, in warm beige and light gray, country charm meeting modern Japanese design, which KI-NRT says could pass for an Aman or Zecha property. He took the top Premium 2-Bedroom Suite (137 square metres), bigger than he needed but with better views, and found it spacious, well appointed and soul-soothing. The one thing he would add is a terrace with an open-air bath.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The ryokan stands on the Toyohira River in Jozankei, Hokkaido's largest onsen town, with around 20 ryokans and 1.5 million visitors a year, public footbaths, canoeing on the river and kappa statues around town. KI-NRT found it a comfortable 24°C in the green season while Tokyo baked at 35°C, and says one night is enough unless you ski or hike. Inside there is a private media room, one of the unusual amenities of a ryokan this size.

inns.name: Hakone Suishoen
inns.summary: A 23-room Fufu-group ryokan in Hakone that does not use the Fufu name, because it is more traditional in architecture and aesthetics and caters to a slightly more mature crowd, and its dining rooms are set in a Taisho-era Mitsui villa. KI-NRT returned deliberately, places it right up there with Gora Kadan, Ginyu and Yama no Chaya despite being less celebrated, and treats it as the group's service standard; a later member's stay confirmed the staff as the standout. Book the kaiseki, because the teppanyaki is a pleasant change of pace but it is not the kitchen's best work.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Suishoen serves a wonderful kaiseki, and it is one of the few luxury ryokans that also offers teppanyaki, a good way to mix things up on a long trip. The counter seats only eight, so reserve it when you book (KI-NRT called two months ahead and got in off the waitlist). He does not think it measures up to Japan's best: Iwate is the only beef, and the wagyu hamburger steak was good but not memorable. The kaiseki is the way to go here.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Bathing at Suishoen is done in your own room, because the Luxury Suites and Precious Suites come with open-air onsen baths on their own decks, fed by natural hot springs. Nobody in the thread has written about the water itself, and nobody mentions a shared bath, so the onsen here is a private soak on your own deck.

service.label: Service
service.text: A member who toured six inns in late 2024 was constantly blown away by the service from the moment he parked: all the staff were attentive and proactive, the teppanyaki head chef spoke into a microphone when his wife got up so someone appeared to show her the way, and after dinner a waitress carried dessert and the rest of their champagne to the room through pouring rain. KI-NRT holds Suishoen up as the Fufu group's service benchmark.

room.label: Room
room.text: This is a modern-style ryokan, so if you want traditional tatami authenticity look elsewhere, and if you want the ryokan experience without the culture shock it is your place. KI-NRT stayed twice in Negau, one of the two 96-square-metre Luxury Suites: a separate Western-style bedroom and living room, an outdoor onsen bath, luxurious and stylish, if a tad on the dark side. Toki, a Precious Suite, is slightly smaller and connects to Negau.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Meals are served in the main building, a gorgeous Taisho-era villa built as the summer home of the Mitsui family's founder and now a designated Important Cultural Property, and that building is the showpiece of the property. The inn is in Hakone, which KI-NRT recommends for a first trip because there is so much to do in the area, and nobody who has stayed describes a view from the rooms or the grounds.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Onyado Chikurintei
inns.summary: Chikurintei is the only bona-fide luxury ryokan in Takeo Onsen, with 11 secluded rooms at the foot of Mt. Mifuneyama, every one with a private onsen bath, both meals served in your room, and service KI-NRT ranked above Aman's. The weak point is the kitchen, because for all its regional ingredients dinner did not live up to its tour-de-force reputation on his December 2024 stay. He would happily return, but in bloom season, when the park next door is at its best.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner uses top regional ingredients such as Saga beef filet and nodoguro, but KI-NRT did not feel it lived up to its tour-de-force reputation: there were fewer dishes than at other luxury ryokans, the nodoguro wrapped around vegetables was strange, and the fried potato stuffed with sea urchin was dry and buried the uni. The fried buckwheat dumplings with walnuts were terrific. Ikyu guests find the meals close to perfect; he did not.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Takeo's spring water is a true onsen, smooth on the skin from its sodium bicarbonate, and all 11 rooms have their own bath flowing from the source, with Shuho adding a private open-air bath off its rock garden. There is a communal open-air bath too, and if the water in your room runs too hot an engineer shows up at once to adjust it. Guests have free use of the famous Rakan-no-Yu sauna two minutes away, but it refuses tattooed guests.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is sophisticated and elegant. The room attendant, Emi Suzuki, in a silk kimono, was an amazing advisor on touring the area and gave them a real education on the kitchen's cooking methods, and the room was refreshed every time they went out, even for a 30-minute walk in the park next door. KI-NRT says Aman's room ninjas have nothing on her. They are flexible too, giving you a chair and table instead of floor seating with a day's notice.

room.label: Room
room.text: Shuho, the 250 square meter stand-alone villa that hosted Emperor Akihito in 1992, has its own entrance, an open-air onsen bath, a private rock garden and commanding views of Mt. Mifuneyama, and it was renovated in 2017, though KI-NRT found wasted space in tatami rooms that serve no purpose. He would have been happy in a mid-category Japanese-Western room, plenty spacious and all with onsen; Gochiku and Shakunage are the popular picks.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn stands at the foot of Mt. Mifuneyama beside Mifuneyama Rakuen, a gorgeous park founded in 1845, two kilometers from the historic bathhouse district of 1,300-year-old Takeo Onsen. The gardens around the mountain burst with color from azaleas, wisteria and maples in March and cherry blossom in April, and KI-NRT came in leafless December and wants to return when the flowers are out, because in winter the park goes silent and monochrome.

cities.text: Ltd Exp 'Relay Kamome' Hakata→Takeo-Onsen (~1h, no change), then a short taxi — the Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen begins at Takeo-Onsen.
Reverse of: 'Relay Kamome' Takeo-Onsen→Shin-Tosu (~40 min, ~hourly), then 'Sakura'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h13).

Reverse of: ~5-min taxi to Takeo-Onsen Stn (Chikurintei's shuttle is ARRIVAL-only, 14:00–18:30 — don't plan on it at checkout), Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen 'Kamome'→Nagasaki (23–31 min, ~hourly, 22/day) + ~10 min to the hotel. 0.42 was the bare ride; 0.7 is door-to-door.
Reverse of: 'Relay Kamome' Takeo-Onsen→Shin-Tosu (~40 min), Shinkansen south→Kumamoto (~25–30 min).
Reverse of: 'Relay Kamome' Takeo-Onsen→Hakata (~58 min), subway 2 stops to Fukuoka Airport (~5 min), FUK→HND (~2h, very frequent). All-rail is a ~5.5h haul — fly.
Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Ltd Exp 'Relay Kamome' Hakata→Takeo-Onsen (~1h). ~4.75h door-to-door.

inns.name: Yama no Chaya
inns.summary: An onsen ryokan in a narrow forested Hakone valley, with an open-air onsen bath in each room, meals served in the room and three shared baths (one outdoors, up a short path), at roughly $600–850 half board, well under what a Tokyo hotel costs. Every first-hand account runs warm to glowing, and the kitchen is the consistent star. KI-NRT is cooler, calling it a solid choice, though not quite as centrally located as Gora Kadan or Ginyu, and he puts Asaba at the top of his own list for the region. The valley is serene, but there are no views.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kaiseki is what every guest praises first. LisainCA's family of foodies found the dinner exceeded expectations, delicious, fresh and varied (the kitchen even brought a mini hibachi so her pescatarian daughter could grill her own fish), and the breakfast was just as good. Smiley90 calls it possibly the best food he ate in Japan, and FlyingTurk1, who finds ryokan food generally underwhelming, still thought it superior to Takefue's.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own open-air onsen bath, and there are three shared onsen besides: two indoors, one of which you can book for your own party for an hour (the other alternates between men and women), and a beautiful outdoor bath reached up a small path. It was raining during LisainCA's stay, and the inn set out outdoor slippers and umbrellas for the walk. Smiley90 calls the onsens excellent.

service.label: Service
