cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner can be a whole tagged snow crab per person from Hashidate port, served as kobako crab, then chilled sashimi, charcoal-grilled, boiled and finally zosui. There is an owner-chosen wine list to go with the kaiseki, and Rosanjin, the artist-gourmet, lived and worked in the house for a year. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.57 and repeatedly praise the dinner kaiseki.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The spring won a gold medal at an international mineral springs exposition in Germany in the early Taisho era, and eleven of the seventeen rooms have an open-air cypress bath fed straight from it. The three communal baths are large and quiet, one arranged as two tubs, hot at 42 to 43 degrees and tepid near 37. Ikyu guests put the bath at 4.74, their highest mark.

service.label: Service
service.text: Eighteen generations of one family have run the house, holding the Maeda clan's hot-spring stewardship, and the hospitality is courteous and formal. Ikyu guests put the service at 4.56 and divide on it: many praise the staff, but a recurring view is that the service could be more polished for an inn at this price.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are historic and full of art, with Rosanjin's screens and ceramics and works by Suda Seika on display, and the whole inn was renovated from 2018. Ikyu guests give the rooms and amenities 4.47, their lowest mark for the inn, so the rooms are where the crowd's enthusiasm is most measured.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn is in Yamashiro Onsen on the Ishikawa coast, but guests describe the inside more than the town: Rosanjin spent a year living and working here, and the corridors are tatami from the front door onward, so you walk barefoot through the inn and past his gallery.

cities.text: Kanazawa→Kaga-Onsen (~15–30 min), then Beniya Mukayu's free on-demand shuttle (~15 min; runs 14:20–18:00, call your arrival time ahead; returns every 30 min 8:45–11:15) — or a ~¥3k taxi.

Hokuriku Shinkansen direct Tokyo→Kaga-Onsen — 2h48 on the best pairing (Maps 2026-08-02, single line, no self-change), then the Beniya shuttle ~15 min (call ahead; inbound window 14:20–18:00). ⚠ Kagayaki skips Kaga-Onsen since the 2024 Tsuruga extension, so it is the through-Hakutaka you want; earlier departures that miss it run 3h06–3h47 with a change at Kanazawa or Tsuruga.

Reverse of: Beniya Mukayu shuttle→Kaga-Onsen (~15 min), 'Tsurugi'→Tsuruga (~37 min), cross-platform change (~10 min), 'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp→Kyoto (~55 min) — 2026-07 audit; the old ~1h30 used a stale pre-extension Thunderbird time.

Reverse of: Yamashiro Onsen sits right by Komatsu Airport: ~15-min taxi to KMQ, the KMQ→Fukuoka hop (~1h40, ~4 daily ANA/ORC), then the subway 2 stops into Hakata (~5 min). ~3.5h door-to-door — the shortest Hokuriku→Kyushu run.
Reverse of: ~15-min taxi to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Nishi-Kyushu relay→Nagasaki via Takeo-Onsen (~2h). ~5.5h door-to-door.
Reverse of: ~15-min taxi to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h17). ~5h door-to-door.

inns.name: Atami Sekaie
inns.summary: Atami Sekaie is a modern 25-room ryokan on the hillside above Sagami Bay, and bathing is its strength, with a private source-fed ocean-view rotenburo in every room plus a pool-size main bath, and the easiest access in Izu. Ikyu guests mark it 4.68 across 307 stays and mostly rave, with the bath their highest mark, while TripAdvisor's softer 3.8 cites train noise and English-service friction. The one drawback to know before you book is that the JR tracks run directly below.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is restaurant-based modern kaiseki across two kitchens, Japanese at TSUKUSHI and a meat-focused teppanyaki counter at 1SHIO, and your plan decides which kitchen you eat in. Ikyu guests praise the teppanyaki and the griddle breakfast cooked in front of you; the teppanyaki draws the steadier praise, while opinion on the Japanese kaiseki is more divided. They put the food at 4.67, in the middle of their marks for the property.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own source-fed open-air bath on the balcony looking over Sagami Bay, and that balcony bath is what Ikyu guests praise again and again. Behind it is the pool-size Koumei-no-Yu main bath with a sauna and a cold bath. Ikyu guests put the bath at 4.75, their highest mark for the inn.

service.label: Service
service.text: A free shuttle meets guests at Atami Station, about five minutes away. Ikyu guests describe natural, unforced service and small surprise gifts on anniversary and birthday stays, which make up a good share of the bookings, and put service at 4.65. Floor staff who work from a script are the complaint in the cooler reviews, and TripAdvisor's foreign guests report friction with English, part of why it fares far worse there than on the Japanese sites.

room.label: Room
room.text: All 25 rooms are modern and each has its own source-fed open-air onsen on a wide balcony facing the ocean, with the trees just below and Sagami Bay beyond, which guests single out as the highlight of the room, and even the reviews that fault the food or the staff call the room and the view good. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.72, second only to the bath among their marks. The recurring complaint is JR train noise from the tracks directly below.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn perches on the hillside above Sagami Bay in Atami, and from the balconies the view is trees below and the open sea beyond. The one drawback is that it sits directly above the JR line, and train noise is the complaint that recurs, especially among the foreign guests on TripAdvisor.

cities.text: Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Kodama' Tokyo→Atami (~43–45 min; a few 'Hikari' ~35 min, 'Nozomi' skips Atami), then Sekaie's free shuttle (~5 min). The first Shinkansen stop out of Tokyo — the shortest Izu-area entry.
Reverse of: Inn shuttle to Atami, direct 'Hikari' Atami→Kyoto (~1h57, one seat — but only ~3 Atami-calling Hikari/day; 'Nozomi' skips Atami), else 'Kodama' + change at Mishima/Nagoya (+1 tx).

inns.name: Ayunosato
inns.summary: An affordable inn in Hitoyoshi Onsen, the quiet hot-spring town in southern Kumamoto where Suiranrou is the famous name and Ayunosato is the alternative when it is full. Recent stays describe a decline. Fc912's summer-2025 visit was fine for the reasonable rate but the service was seriously lacking, because most of the staff were foreign trainees who had not been trained enough, and KI-NRT's friends on their third stay found the same thing and said it starts with an okami who is not very engaging and uses her mobile phone near reception. Fc912 would not return.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the food here.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Ayunosato is in Hitoyoshi Onsen, a hot-spring town, but nobody in the thread has written about the baths here, so the water situation is unknown.

service.label: Service
service.text: Both recent stays complain about the service, and both point at the okami. Fc912 found most of the staff were foreign trainees who could not give the service expected, and saw the okami hanging out with friends in the common area. KI-NRT's friends on their third stay made the same remark: she used her phone near reception (a big no-no in Japanese hospitality), never greeted guests, and at dinner said only "do you want some sake?".

room.label: Room
room.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the rooms here.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Hitoyoshi Onsen is in southern Kumamoto, which is not much of a tourism hotspot, because most travelers to the prefecture go to Amakusa, the Mt. Aso region or Kumamoto City and its castle, and Fc912 found the town a bit in the middle of nowhere. Fc912 stopped there only to break up the long drive from Kirishima up to Amakusa, and the town's famous inn is Suiranrou; Ayunosato is where Fc912 ended up when Suiranrou was fully booked.

cities.text: Shinkansen Hakata to Kumamoto (~45 min), then highway bus to Hitoyoshi (~1.5 hr); Hisatsu rail still severed since 2020 floods.
Highway bus Kagoshima to Hitoyoshi (~1.3-1.5 hr), then ~10 min car; inn offers pickup at the terminal.

transit.note: A-tier Suiranrou; Hisatsu Line Yatsushiro-Yoshimatsu section not restored, access by bus.

inns.name: Azuma Farm Koiwai
inns.summary: Azuma Farm Koiwai is Adrian Zecha's farm resort on the historic Koiwai Farm below Mt Iwate, with 24 Shiro Miura villas, farm-driven French-technique dinners, private sauna pavilions and deep January snow. It opened in April 2026, has under a year of operating history, and nobody in the thread has stayed yet. The villa baths are filled with onsen water and the dedicated onsen facility was slated for November 2026 at the earliest, so confirm it has opened before booking a winter stay.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is included and is a French-technique tasting menu built on Sanriku seafood, Koiwai dairy and wagyu, which is the farm-to-table premise of the place. Nobody in the thread has eaten here yet.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Each villa has a large stone bath meant to be filled with hot-spring water, and there are three private sauna pavilions on the grounds. The dedicated onsen facility was slated for November 2026, so ask whether it has opened before you book a winter stay. Nobody in the thread has bathed here yet.

service.label: Service
service.text: The resort is Adrian Zecha's project with Azumi's Hayase and JR East, and it only opened in April 2026. Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 24 villas are built of red pine and cedar, and each has its own large stone bath. They are brand new (the resort opened in April 2026) and nobody in the thread has slept in one yet.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The resort sits on the 130-year-old working Koiwai Farm at the foot of Mt Iwate, at Shizukuishi in Iwate, under deep snow in January, and Kyoto architect Shiro Miura of Rokakuya, a sukiya-style specialist, designed its buildings from 100-year-old red pine and cedar he picked out and had felled on the farm itself. Nobody in the thread has visited yet.

cities.text: Tōhoku Shinkansen 'Hayabusa' Tokyo→Morioka (~2h15), then the free hotel shuttle from Morioka Station (~25–30 min, reserve). The Tōhoku line is famously snow-reliable.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya (~2h01), cross to a 'Hayabusa'/'Komachi' Ōmiya→Morioka (~1h51), then the free hotel shuttle to Koiwai (~28 min, reserve). Single change at Ōmiya on the snow-reliable Tōhoku main line; length is the only real cost.
Reverse of: Hotel shuttle to Morioka (~25–30 min), Tōhoku Shinkansen 'Hayabusa'→Sendai (~40 min).

inns.name: Azumi Setoda
inns.summary: Azumi Setoda is Adrian Zecha's first Azumi, a restored 1876 salt-merchant estate turned 22-room inn on Setoda that is often cited as the bench-setter for the modern ryokan. Ikyu guests rate it 4.58 across 14 reviews and praise the French-trained chef's fusion kaiseki and the attentive staff, and the one recurring friction is group bookings at dinner. You stay for the architecture and for the slow pace of the Inland Sea.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a French course from a chef who trained twelve years in France, cooked as a fusion of French and kaiseki technique, and Ikyu guests describe it as a string of surprises, with the chef's skill and his care over each ingredient visible on every plate. Ikyu diners put the food at 4.64.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Bathing splits between a deep hinoki tub in every room and Yubune, the bathhouse across the street with lemon baths and a sauna, which Japanese guests call a sento. Ikyu guests describe the in-room tubs as spacious and open, and they mark the bath 4.5, their lowest mark here.

service.label: Service
service.text: Ikyu guests describe warm, personal attention from the front of house through to the kitchen, with the dining-room staff and the chef's team both drawing praise, and service is the warmest of the Ikyu marks at 4.71. The one recurring friction is group bookings at dinner, and several guests have found a party crowding the dining room or the advertised Western course withdrawn for a group night, so confirm the dinner plan when you book.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 22 rooms sit inside the restored 1876 Horiuchi salt-merchant estate, and each has its own deep hinoki bath; some are two-storey maisonettes. Ikyu guests praise the design of the rooms and the built-in joinery, which more than one ranks among the best in Japan, and they repeatedly call the in-room bath and shower room spacious and open. They put the rooms at 4.57, level with the building and the facilities.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn is the 140-year-old compound of the Horiuchi salt-merchant family in Setoda, a port town on Ikuchijima in the Seto Inland Sea, renovated by Kyoto architect Shiro Miura, known for contemporary sukiya-style teahouse work. Setoda itself has few places to eat in the evening, so reserve dinner at the inn.

cities.text: Reverse of: Ferry back to Mihara (~30 min), then JR/Shinkansen to Hiroshima.
Shinkansen Kyoto→Mihara (~1h50), then ~30-min ferry to Setoda Port + 5-min walk — arriving by sea is the point.
Reverse of: Ferry to Mihara (~30 min), Shinkansen Mihara→Tokyo (~4h).
Sanyo Shinkansen 'Kodama' Hakata→Mihara (~2h10–2h30; Nozomi/Mizuho skip Mihara), then the Habu Shōsen ferry Mihara→Setoda (~25 min) + short walk. Confirm the day's last winter ferry.

inns.name: Bessho SASA
inns.summary: Bessho Sasa is the adults-only private-onsen-suite annex of Hotel Kaneyamaen in Fujiyoshida, where every suite gets its own Fuji-facing hot-spring bath and in-suite counter kaiseki. Its own Ikyu guests are split, and a 4.38 average over 61 reviews covers guests who question whether the premium floor is worth its price over the main hotel alongside guests who call the Fuji views and taiko welcome unforgettable.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is kaiseki served in the suite at a live counter, and the lounge pours Yamanashi wine and beer free of charge. Food is where Ikyu guests are least happy, at 4.07 their lowest mark, and the reviews split between guests who enjoyed every course and guests who left disappointed with the meals.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every suite has its own natural hot-spring open-air bath facing Mt. Fuji, and Kaneyamaen's 10th-floor observatory bath looks at the mountain too. The spring is around pH 10, and the shared baths are those of the big family hotel downstairs. Ikyu guests give the bath 4.57, their highest mark.

service.label: Service
service.text: Arrival brings a traditional welcome and a taiko drum performance, and the taiko is what Ikyu guests keep naming as the best part of the stay, even in reviews critical of the food. The service itself is praised across the reviews, including the critical ones, and Ikyu guests give it 4.44.

room.label: Room
room.text: The suites are the premium floor of a large hotel, the fourth and fifth storeys of Kaneyamaen, and they are adults only. Ikyu guests give the rooms 4.34, one of their lower marks here, and the critical reviews ask whether the premium floor justifies its price over the main hotel.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The suites are the top two floors of Hotel Kaneyamaen, a large ryokan in Fujiyoshida, and they are placed for the view of Mt. Fuji, so the stay hinges on whether the mountain shows, and the Ikyu reviews turn on it, with cloud on arrival a recurring disappointment and a clear morning the highlight. Downstairs is lively and full of families, which some guests enjoy and others find mass-market.

cities.text: Reverse of: JR 'Fuji Excursion' Ltd Exp Kawaguchiko→Shinjuku direct (~2h, ~4/day). Miss it → Fujikyu→Ōtsuki + Chūō Ltd Exp = ~2h25, 1 change.

Round the south side of Fuji rather than back through Tokyo: Fujikyu 'Mishima·Kawaguchiko Liner' bus Kawaguchiko→Mishima (~1h30–1h40, roughly hourly, ¥2,700 — japan-guide, Oct 2025), one change at Mishima, then the Tōkaidō Shinkansen Mishima→Kyoto (~1h51 on a Hikari that calls at Mishima, ~2h27 on the all-stations Kodama — ekitan). ~4h15 door-to-door with the inn shuttle and the change. (Via Tokyo — 'Fuji Excursion'→Shinjuku, cross to Tokyo Station, 'Nozomi'→Kyoto — is ~4h30 and two changes, and the Fuji Excursion runs only ~4/day.)

inns.name: C'est La Vie
inns.summary: A quirky antique-furnished inn in northern Saitama that KI-NRT flags as effectively the region's only luxury option, known for reportedly incredible food, stellar service, and a station pickup in a rare Toyota Classic sedan. Nobody in the thread has stayed, and KI-NRT only relays guest feedback, but Jalan guests back the reputation, averaging 5.0 across 532 reviews and praising a homey small-hotel feel, bathing among greenery and local-ingredient kaiseki.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Nobody in the thread has eaten here. KI-NRT passes on only that the food is supposedly incredible from guest feedback. Jalan guests give both dinner and breakfast full marks and describe local-ingredient kaiseki that leans on vegetables and sansai, with seasonal menus and plating and tableware praised as often as the cooking itself.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the bathing here. The rooms have their own open-air bath set among greenery, and Jalan guests give the bath full marks, though none of them says whether the water is hot-spring.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT relays that service is stellar, though only from guest feedback, and that they collect you at the station in a rare retro Toyota sedan, the Toyota Classic, of which only 100 were made. Jalan guests give service full marks and describe attentive staff from check-in to check-out.

room.label: Room
room.text: Rooms are on the small side and quirky, furnished with antiques, by the reputation KI-NRT relays, and nobody in the thread has slept in one. The rooms are where Jalan guests are least effusive (4.6 where everything else is at or near 5.0), though they still describe calm, lovely furniture and an open-air bath in the room, and they put cleanliness at 4.8.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: C'est La Vie is a tiny hotel in northern Saitama, quite a bit north of Kawagoe and close to the Gunma border, and KI-NRT points out that when you are talking luxury in Saitama the pickings are slim. Jalan guests describe a homey small-hotel atmosphere with greenery around the bath and interiors dressed for the season.

cities.text: JR to Kumagaya then Chichibu Railway to Nogami ~2.3h, then ~20 min shuttle to Nagatoro.
JR to Kumagaya + Chichibu Railway to Nogami ~1.5h, then ~20 min shuttle.

inns.name: Daikon no Hana
inns.summary: Daikon no Hana is a 52-room onsen ryokan in the Sendai area, and its strength is the water: every bath runs straight from the source with nothing recirculated, and KI-NRT singles out the rental bath surrounded by forest. He stayed many years ago and describes it as the country home-style, relaxed alternative to the pricier, more tranquil and more traditional Saryo Souen, a matter of taste between the two. Nobody in the thread has written about the food, the rooms or the service.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the food here.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All the onsen at Daikon no Hana run straight from the source and nothing is recirculated, and there are some nice baths, especially the rental bath surrounded by a forest, which KI-NRT singles out.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: At 52 rooms it is fairly large for a luxury ryokan, but nobody in the thread has written about the rooms themselves.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Daikon no Hana has a country home-style atmosphere, and KI-NRT contrasts it with Saryo Souen, the other luxury choice around Sendai, which is more tranquil and more traditional; he calls the choice between the two a matter of taste. He was last at both places many years ago.

cities.text: Akiu Onsen is roughly 30-40 min by car or shuttle bus from JR Sendai Station.
Tohoku Shinkansen Hayabusa from Tokyo to Sendai is about 1h30, then roughly 40 min by car out to Akiu Onsen.

inns.name: ESPACIO The Hakone Geihinkan Rin-Poh-Ki-Ryu
inns.summary: Espacio is nine villas at the bottom of a private cable car in Hakone's Dogashima river valley, with undiluted source onsen piped to every villa and saunas in most. At $2,100–$3,500 a night it is one of the most expensive stays here. Ikyu guests rate it 4.49 across a thin sample of 13 reviews, praising the arrival, the butler service and the bathing, while the two weakest reviews both question whether it is worth the price.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Takahiro Yamagishi of Kyoto's Tominokoji Yamagishi, a kaiseki restaurant that has held a Michelin star every year since 2017, supervises the kitchen. There is no restaurant on the property, so dinner and breakfast are served in your villa, and the courses are finished on the spot so they arrive hot, which guests notice and appreciate. Even the two harshest Ikyu reviewers found the food delicious, and Ikyu guests put it at 4.54.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every villa has its own bath fed with undiluted, free-flowing Dogashima spring water, five of the nine add a sauna, and the flagship TAKUMI villa adds a plunge pool and a hot-stone bath. Nobody has complained about the water, and bathing is the highest of the Ikyu marks at 4.69, though from only 13 reviews.

service.label: Service
service.text: A butler is assigned to your villa for the whole stay, and most of what you see of the staff happens at your own door, since there is no restaurant, bar or lounge to go out to. Four of the five sampled Ikyu reviews call the service excellent or very good, and the praise holds even where the same guests are unhappy about the interiors or the price. Ikyu guests put service at 4.54, level with the food and the rooms.

room.label: Room
room.text: The nine villas are each a house of their own, standing behind their own gates along the monorail line, with undiluted Dogashima source water running to each villa's bath and a sauna in five of the nine. The flagship villa, Takumi, adds a plunge pool and a hot-stone bath. Guests call the villas clean and very nice, with touches like choosing your own key-card design and souvenir chopsticks, and Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.54.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn lies at the bottom of Hakone's Dogashima river valley below Miyanoshita, reached by its own cable car dropping a hundred metres, and then a mini-monorail runs past the garden to each villa's gate. There is no restaurant, bar or library, so you spend the whole stay inside your villa.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Guntû
inns.location: Floating — the Seto Inland Sea (boards near Onomichi)
inns.prefecture: Floating — the Seto Inland Sea (boards near Onomichi)
inns.summary: Guntû is a 19-cabin floating ryokan that cruises the Seto Inland Sea, designed by Yasushi Horibe, with a sushi bar and terrace cypress baths on the top suites. It books as a cruise instead of as a room, and at $3,750–$5,250 a night it is the most expensive stay here. The only guest reviews are on Tabelog, where 3.08 over 19 reviews is respectable on that restaurant-review scale, and the repeat passengers there praise the attentive crew and the eat-as-you-like menu. Nobody in the thread has sailed on it.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Meals run on the ship's own rule, whatever you like, as much as you like: the chefs cook what you ask for from the fresh ingredients on display, there is a sushi bar, and the dinner menu changes daily around that day's recommendations, so no two voyages eat the same. The handful of Tabelog reviewers, several of them repeat passengers, are satisfied with it, but nobody in the thread has eaten on board.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The top suites have private open-air cypress baths on their terraces over the water, and there is a communal hinoki bath for everyone else. These are heated tubs on a ship, so there is no hot-spring water anywhere on board. Nobody in the thread has written about the bathing here.

service.label: Service
service.text: The crew is what the Tabelog reviewers praise most, and the repeat passengers among them describe friendly, attentive hospitality that leaves nothing wanting. The press routinely calls Guntû one of the world's great hotel experiences. Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 19 cabins are Yasushi Horibe's work, and the top suites have open-air cypress baths on private terraces facing the water. Nobody in the thread or among the Tabelog reviewers has written about the cabins themselves.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Guntû cruises the Seto Inland Sea from a marina near Onomichi, so the islands and water outside the window change through the stay, and Yasushi Horibe shaped the ship's roofline and hull to echo the tiled-roof towns of the Setouchi coast. Routes vary between voyages.

cities.text: Reverse of: JR Sanyo local Onomichi→Fukuyama (~15 min), Sanyo Shinkansen Fukuyama→Hiroshima (~25 min) — change at Fukuyama (faster than Shin-Onomichi, 3 km out of town).

Bookend down the Sanyo Shinkansen: 'Nozomi'/'Sakura' Kyoto→Fukuyama (~1h40), then JR local Fukuyama→Onomichi into town. (Shin-Onomichi is direct but sits ~3 km out, so Fukuyama-and-local lands you at the station.)

inns.name: Hakone Retreat före & villa 1/f
inns.summary: A Scandinavian-styled forest resort of 18 log-house villas in Sengokuhara, deliberately built as something other than a ryokan. Ikyu guests give it 4.03 over 34 reviews, and the reviews explain the middling number: forest quiet and the private-onsen villas draw raves, but service is the recurring sore point, with undertrained staff and breakfast lapses. It is a villa resort with private onsen tubs and makes no claim to be a traditional inn.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is in the kaiseki room or at the wood-fired grill instead of in your villa, so you choose between a Japanese course meal and food cooked over a wood fire, and either way you walk out of the villa to eat. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.29, well above their mark for the service, and the complaints run to the serving more than the cooking, with breakfast the meal that repeatedly falls short.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every villa has its own open-air onsen bath fed from a Hakone spring, and there are shared indoor and outdoor baths as well. Ikyu guests put the bathing at 4.21, and they praise having the spring to themselves at the villa.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is the weak point, and three of the five recent Ikyu reviews are about it. The recurring complaints are halting, undertrained staff, many of them foreign hires with limited Japanese, meals that go wrong in the serving, guests hurried toward checkout, and a level of care that does not match the price. Ikyu guests put service at 3.47 against 4.2 or better elsewhere.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 18 villas are Scandinavian-styled log houses, each standalone with a wood stove and its own onsen bath, which is a long way from a ryokan room, and some villas take dogs. The rooms hold up in the reviews even where the service does not, and Ikyu guests put them at 4.24 against 3.47 for service.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The resort spreads its villas across about 50,000 m² of Sengokuhara forest off the Hakone Ekiden course, and in 2025 it won a Good Design Award for the way the new Ibuki villa area fits the woods and the site's history. Guests write about the silence of the forest before anything else.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Hatago (Arima)
inns.summary: A small Arima inn where every room has its own bath of the golden kinsen spring water. The only stay in the thread is KI-NRT's from roughly a decade ago, which he remembers as pretty decent with junior-suite-sized rooms and a maybe on returning, yet in January 2026 he shortlisted Hatago first for an Arima night and found it fully booked. You stay here for the gold-spring bath in your own room; nobody in the thread has written about the food, the service or anything else.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the food here.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own bath of Arima's famous kinsen, the golden spring, and some rooms have an open-air bath as well. The kinsen is high in iron and salt, emerges transparent and turns reddish-brown on contact with air. It is not fed straight from the source here, though: by KI-NRT's own digging only four Arima facilities draw directly from the spring, and Hatago is not one of them. Nobody in the thread has described the baths themselves.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: KI-NRT took the Hatsuzora Suite about a decade ago and found the rooms more junior-suite sized than suite sized, though the stay was pretty decent and he is a maybe on returning.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Hatago is in Arima Onsen, Japan's oldest recorded hot spring and one of its big three onsen towns with Kusatsu and Gero, and KI-NRT counts it among Arima's big four luxury ryokans with Gosho Bessho, Nakanobo Zuien and Arima Onsen Kinzan. He has never been particularly fond of Arima or its town, though it is a delightful place for walks, browsing the shops and sampling carbonated onsen rice crackers. Nobody in the thread has described the grounds.

cities.text: Osaka Stn/Umeda to Arima Onsen ~60 min direct highway bus, then ~5 min to inn.
Shin-Kobe/Sannomiya to Arima ~30 min by bus or Kobe Electric Rly, then ~5 min.

inns.name: Hitotsu Notojima
inns.summary: Hitotsu Notojima is Hokuriku's first sushi auberge, opened in 2023 on Notojima island in the calm inner bay off Nanao, with six sea-facing rooms, a bar-lounge along the water and a wood-fired sauna, run around a Noto-seafood sushi dinner and a sushi-chef's breakfast at the counter (drinks were all-inclusive until September 2026). There is no hot spring, and the room baths hold plain water with the bay for a view. Ikyu guests give it 4.81 across roughly 26 stays, with hospitality and cooking their high marks, and it holds a Michelin Key. Nobody in the thread has stayed here yet.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a Noto-seafood sushi omakase at the counter and breakfast is a sushi-chef's spread at the same counter (grilled nodoguro one morning), which is why the house calls itself a sushi auberge. Ikyu guests mark the cooking high, near 4.85, and call the sushi and the sake superb, though the local sake stopped being all-inclusive in September 2026.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no hot spring here. The sea-facing rooms have a private view bath and a wood-fired sauna looks out over the same bay, and that sauna is one of the three things the house sells, with the sushi and the view. Ikyu guests put the bathing a little below their other marks, so the sauna and the view are what you get from the bathing here, and there is no spring water.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is personal and all-inclusive. Check-in is a welcome drink in the lounge above the bay, and staff pour and talk with you over the water. With six rooms the stay runs between that lounge and the sushi counter, where dinner and breakfast are served, and drinks and the minibar are in the rate until September 2026. Ikyu guests mark hospitality highest of all their marks, at 4.88, and attentive, unhurried care recurs across reviews.

room.label: Room
room.text: The six rooms all face the sea and run around 51 square metres, each with a private view bath over the calm inner bay off Nanao and a minibar included with the stay. Ikyu guests give the rooms their softest mark, 4.69; they are comfortable and well-kept but the plainest part of the stay.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Hitotsu Notojima stands on Notojima, an island in the sheltered inner bay off Nanao, and opened in 2023. The view over the bay as you walk in is what guests write about first, the bar-lounge runs along the water, dolphin and sunset cruises leave from the private pier below, and a golf course and a clear-water beach are nearby. The peninsula is still rebuilding after the 2024 Noto earthquake.

cities.text: Reverse of: A ~10-min taxi across the Notojima bridge to Wakura-Onsen, then the JR Ltd Exp 'Noto Kagaribi' Wakura-Onsen→Kanazawa (~1h08, ~5/day, direct) — about 1h20 door-to-door.

Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' Tokyo→Kanazawa (~2h28), change to the JR Ltd Exp 'Noto Kagaribi' Kanazawa→Wakura-Onsen (~1h08, ~5/day — confirm the connection), then a ~10-min taxi across the Notojima bridge. One change at Kanazawa.

'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp Kyoto→Tsuruga (~45 min), Hokuriku Shinkansen Tsuruga→Kanazawa (~50 min), change to the JR Ltd Exp 'Noto Kagaribi'→Wakura-Onsen (~1h08), then a ~10-min taxi across the Notojima bridge. Two changes (Tsuruga, Kanazawa).

inns.name: Hoshinoya Fuji
inns.summary: Japan's first luxury glamping resort puts 40 concrete cabins on a slope above Lake Kawaguchi, every one aimed at Fuji, with terrace living and dawn canoeing in place of tatami and kaiseki, which makes it the deliberate opposite of a ryokan. There is no onsen, just a small public bath, and Rakuten guests split on the service, some praising courteous staff and others finding some of it careless.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner here is not a ryokan kaiseki, and nobody in the thread or among the Rakuten guests has written about the food.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no hot spring. Each cabin has an ordinary bathroom, and the only shared bathing is a small public bath of heated water, so bathing here amounts to a tub, and Rakuten guests say nothing about it.

service.label: Service
service.text: Rakuten guests split on the service, Hoshinoya's programmed kind built around outings like dawn canoeing and the Cloud Terrace forest lounge. Some describe courteous, wonderful staff who live up to the reputation, while others found some of the staff careless and the stay well short of it. The complaints are about logistics on a resort spread across a slope, where you depend on the staff to book outings and to get between cabin and reception.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 40 cabins are minimalist concrete boxes, each with a heated open terrace so you can live outdoors in any season, and every one of them faces Fuji. Rakuten guests call the room and the location the best part of a stay.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Architect Rie Azuma set all 40 cabins on a forested slope above Lake Kawaguchi so that every one faces Fuji, and each minimalist concrete cabin has a heated open terrace aimed at the mountain, with a forest lounge called the Cloud Terrace. It was Japan's first luxury glamping resort. Rakuten guests call the location superb and the Fuji view the point of the stay, and KI-NRT calls snow-capped Fuji gorgeous in winter.

cities.text: Reverse of: JR 'Fuji Excursion' Ltd Exp Kawaguchiko→Shinjuku direct (~2h, ~4/day). Miss it → Fujikyu→Ōtsuki + Chūō Ltd Exp = ~2h25, 1 change.

Round the south side of Fuji rather than back through Tokyo: Fujikyu 'Mishima·Kawaguchiko Liner' bus Kawaguchiko→Mishima (~1h30–1h40, roughly hourly, ¥2,700 — japan-guide, Oct 2025), one change at Mishima, then the Tōkaidō Shinkansen Mishima→Kyoto (~1h51 on a Hikari that calls at Mishima, ~2h27 on the all-stations Kodama — ekitan). ~4h15 door-to-door with the inn shuttle and the change. (Via Tokyo — 'Fuji Excursion'→Shinjuku, cross to Tokyo Station, 'Nozomi'→Kyoto — is ~4h30 and two changes, and the Fuji Excursion runs only ~4/day.)

inns.name: KANAYA RESORT HAKONE
inns.summary: KANAYA RESORT HAKONE is a 14-room forest villa on 6,500 tsubo of Sengokuhara woodland, the retreat arm of the Kinugawa Kanaya Hotel. The kitchen is French eaten with chopsticks, carrying on the legacy of Nishi-Azabu's Seiyozensho John Kanaya, and every room has a free-flowing Ōwakudani bath, with service that guests praise as much as the food. Ikyu guests put it near 4.80 over about 103 stays, with meals, baths and service their high marks; there is no large public bath, and the building is stairs-heavy and not barrier-free.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is French cooking eaten with chopsticks, carrying the legacy of Nishi-Azabu's Seiyozensho John Kanaya, served in the Black-and-Gold dining room: a signature egg-and-double-consommé opener, fish courses and an optional melt-in-the-mouth chateaubriand, then a Japanese ochazuke breakfast. Ikyu guests put the meals near 4.89, their top mark, and the cooking is what their reviews praise most.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own bath fed free-flowing from the milky-white Ōwakudani source, a silky 'beauty' water whose colour shifts through the day, and it comes as an open-air bath, an indoor stone bath or a tub in the Western rooms. There is no large public bath, which a few guests miss, but the bathing here is meant to be private and in your room. Ikyu guests put the baths near 4.85.

service.label: Service
service.text: Guests praise the hospitality above all else. The staff carry on the philosophy of the old John Kanaya house, warm and attentive without hovering, and Ikyu reviews repeatedly describe small things anticipated before guests ask. Ikyu guests put the service near 4.86, and several call it the reason they return.

room.label: Room
room.text: The fourteen wood-and-stone rooms are tuned to the forest, from Superior twins of 41 to 52 square metres up to the 113-square-metre John Kanaya Suite, each with a private Ōwakudani bath and windows onto the trees. Ikyu guests put the rooms near 4.71, the softest of their marks, and the building is stairs-heavy and not barrier-free.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn stands on a 6,500-tsubo estate of primeval forest in Sengokuhara that has drawn villa-goers since the Meiji era, with moss-walled paths, a garden Forest Terrace for champagne and wide Fuji-and-Hakone skies, yet only about 90 minutes from Tokyo. The grounds are compact and easy to navigate, though there is almost no common space beyond the restaurant and a tiny bar; Ikyu guests put the facilities near 4.63, the lowest of their marks.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Kaiseki Inn Suihuen
inns.summary: Suihuen is a fifteen-room kaiseki house on the high ground above Gero Onsen, looking across the valley to Gero-Fuji, with private open-air baths in eight of the rooms and a 'yojo kaiseki' dinner brought course by course to your own room. Ikyu's crowd gives it 4.75 across 107 reviews, and cooking (4.83) is its clear high mark while rooms (4.68) come in lowest. The inn's free shuttle takes four minutes from Gero Station, and Takayama is forty-eight minutes up the same line.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Suihuen calls itself a kaiseki inn, and dinner is a 'yojo kaiseki' brought course by course to a private room, built on Hida beef and Gero's prize-winning local rice. There is also a separate Hida-beef tearoom, Kangetsu, on the property. Ikyu guests put the cooking at 4.83, the inn's clear high mark and the only one above its 4.75 overall, and it is what returning guests lead with.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Gero's alkaline water is one of Japan's three great springs and famously silky on the skin, and here it runs to private open-air baths in eight of the fifteen rooms, with an open-air bath, a large public bath and a bookable private bath below. Ikyu guests put bathing at 4.75, and guests who have stayed elsewhere in Gero single out the water quality in both the room baths and the public one.

service.label: Service
service.text: Guests keep describing the staff as courteous from welcome to send-off. Meals are served in the room, and the staff who bring them are described as consistently pleasant across the whole stay and not only at the set-pieces. Ikyu guests put hospitality at 4.75. A fifth-time visitor to Gero puts the house in the town's top one or two on overall satisfaction and recommends it without qualification.

room.label: Room
room.text: There are fifteen rooms across the main building and the adults-oriented Yukatei annex, eight of them with private open-air baths, ranging from barrier-free premium suites to junior suites with a garden or valley bath. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.68, the inn's softest mark, and at this price that is an honest trade, because the house spends on the kitchen and the water and less on square metres.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Suihuen sits on high ground above the Gero Onsen townscape, in a landscaped hillside garden near the Gassho-mura open-air village, and Gero-Fuji (Mt. Nakane) fills the view across the valley. Gero Station is four minutes below by the inn's shuttle, and Takayama is forty-eight minutes up the same Takayama Line.

cities.text: Reverse of: 'Hida' Gero→Toyama (~2h20), change to the Hokuriku Shinkansen Toyama→Kanazawa (~23 min). Beats the Takayama + Nohi-bus chain (~3h25). ⚠ ~5 Toyama through-services/day.
Reverse of: 'Hida' Gero→Nagoya (~1h37), change to a Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Tokyo (~1h40), plus the ~5-min drive at the Gero end. Shogetsu's own access page gives this chain.

Reverse of: 'Hida' Gero→Nagoya (~1h35), change ~15 min to a Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'/'Hikari'→Kyoto (~35 min) + the Shōgetsu shuttle and hotel ends (2026-07 audit: same 10-Hida/day correction as takayama>kyoto — hourly only ~11:30–16:30, 2h gaps outside, all-reserved Dec 25–Jan 5, January 大雪 advisories; the old 2.5 was bare rides on an 'hourly' frequency that isn't). One no-change direct: Hida 36 calls at Gero ~16:10 → Kyoto 19:17.

inns.name: Kamenoi Besso
inns.summary: A 1921 lakeside estate on Lake Kinrin at the foot of Mt. Yufu, with seventeen rooms all built differently, garden-source kakenagashi in every tub and public rooms (a teahouse, a bar, a gramophone lounge) that guests keep writing about. It holds Two Michelin Keys in 2025, one of only twenty properties in Japan to do so. KI-NRT calls it 'the original luxury Yufuin inn' and has a return booked for November 2026. Ikyu's crowd (4.87 across 122 reviews) ranks it near the top of Kyushu, and dinner is the one softer note. Nobody in the thread has written a full review yet.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a kaiseki of Ōita mountain vegetables and local meat, in the room for the hanare and in the restaurant for the main building. Tuesday to Thursday there is also Jūbankan, a counter annex with wine pairings. Food is where Ikyu guests mark the inn lowest, at 4.77, and dishes arriving lukewarm is the recurring complaint.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The spring is the garden's own, and every tub runs kakenagashi from it: two shared bathhouses, three open-air baths and the tubs in all seventeen rooms, ten of them outdoors. The shared baths stay open all night, and even the main-building twins now have indoor onsen tubs. There is no sauna and no private-hire bath. Ikyu guests put the baths at 4.89.

service.label: Service
service.text: KI-NRT, who stayed years ago, calls Kamenoi the original luxury Yufuin inn and has booked a return for November 2026. Arrival is old-school, with several staff lined up at the entrance when you pull in, and Ikyu guests put service at 4.87, describing warm, unhurried attention from everyone they met. Praise for the staff is uniform across the reviews, including the ones that fault the food.

room.label: Room
room.text: The seventeen rooms are all built differently: eleven detached hanare under the trees, with dinner served in the room, and six Western-style twins in the main building with Danish furniture alongside local craft. Special Room 7, a 140 square metre two-bedroom villa, has just been renovated, and ten rooms have their own open-air bath. The cheapest twins are 36 to 45 square metres, up stairs, and take no children below junior-high age.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Ten thousand tsubo of garden under 200-year-old trees beside Lake Kinrin at the foot of Mt. Yufu, begun in 1921 as a private villa. The lane outside is packed with tourists, but once you cross the small bridge the noise stops and you hear birdsong and koi in the pond. The public rooms matter as much as the garden: the Tenjōsajiki teahouse in a relocated sake warehouse and a fireside lounge with records on the gramophone each evening.

cities.text: Reverse of: Ltd Exp back toward Hakata (~2h10).
Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima-Chūō→Hakata (~1h20), ~4-min platform transfer, then the JR 'Yufu' Ltd Exp Hakata→Yufuin (~2h15). ~3h11 total, all-rail.

Reverse of: By car (~210 km, raw ~2h25 per NAVITIME; budget ~3h): Yufuin IC → Oita Expwy → Tosu JCT → Nagasaki Expwy → Nagasaki IC (~¥5,060). Budget 3h+ in January — the Yufuin IC–Hita IC stretch (~45 km) is an official winter-tire-regulation zone (last winter: 7 days of regulation, 2 of closure); past Hita it's plains, and the Nagasaki Expwy has no regulated section at all. (Transit: Ltd Exp 'Yufu'→Hakata ~2h15 + 'Relay Kamome'/'Kamome' via Takeo, ~3.5h total, 2 changes — 2026-07 audit; rare January snow on the Kyudai line's pass.)

Reverse of: Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin-no-Mori' Yufuin→Kurume (~1h40, ~5/day), Shinkansen Kurume→Kumamoto (~25 min). Scenic alt: the Kyushu Ōdan bus through Kurokawa/Aso, one seat, ~4h15, 3/day. By car ~2.5h via the Yamanami Highway.

Fly to Yufuin: Tokyo→Haneda (~30 min), HND→Oita (OIT) ~1h30 nonstop (frequent ANA/JAL/Solaseed; 2026-07 audit vs flightsfrom/sakuratravel timetables), then a pre-booked FIXED-FARE taxi straight to the inn (~55 min, ¥18,320 incl. tolls — Oita Taxi Assoc., say '定額で') — no bus-schedule or shuttle sync. (Budget alt: airport bus→Yufuin Stn ~55 min, 6/day, ¥1,550pp + the inn shuttle — Enowa's needs reserving ≥3 days ahead.) Far saner than the ~5h45 all-rail haul.

Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Ltd Exp 'Yufu'/'Yufuin-no-Mori' Hakata→Yufuin (~2h10). ~6h door-to-door. (Oita is Yufuin's own airport but has no Komatsu flight — Hakata is the gateway.)

inns.name: Kanshuku-en Eshikoto
inns.summary: Kanshuku-en Eshikoto is an eight-villa auberge opened in November 2024 by the Kokuryu sake brewery beside its ESHIKOTO complex near Eiheiji, the Soto Zen head temple, and each is a whole-villa rental of about 103 square meters with a semi-open-air onsen bath and Echizen-craft art. Dinner is at the Michelin one-star Japanese En or the French cadre, with the house Kokuryu sake. Ikyu guests give it 4.71 across 38 stays, with the villas and the bathing their high marks and breakfast the recurring quibble. Nobody in the thread has stayed yet, though KI-NRT recommends it to anyone visiting Eiheiji.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is at En, the Michelin one-star Japanese restaurant, or the innovative French cadre, with the house Kokuryu sake, and breakfast is a French-touched Japanese spread at the neighboring acoya. Ikyu guests mark the meals their softest note (4.54), and while the cooking is praised, breakfast is the recurring quibble, judged too plain for an inn of this class.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every villa has a semi-open-air bath fed by the alkaline Eiheiji Zen spring, a sodium-chloride-bicarbonate 'beauty' water that arrives by pipe and is not free-flowing. It looks out over the fields and the Kuzuryu River, and Ikyu guests put the bathing among their highest marks, just behind the villas themselves, with the in-villa soak and its valley view what they praise.

service.label: Service
service.text: It is a quiet eight-villa auberge run by the Kokuryu sake house next door, and brewery tours come with a stay. Ikyu guests mark hospitality solidly (4.74), below the villas and bath. The whole-villa privacy and the sake-and-food framing suit a low-key stay better than a staffed ryokan's bustle.

room.label: Room
room.text: The eight villas are whole-villa rentals of around 103 square metres in three concepts, with art chosen by the ceramicist Koichi Uchida from Echizen crafts and global pieces, and most face the Kuzuryu River. Ikyu guests give the rooms and amenities their highest mark, with the design and the space the standout, and KI-NRT describes the place as new and modern.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The villas stand at the foot of Mt. Johoji on the Kuzuryu River in Eiheiji, beside the Kokuryu brewery's ESHIKOTO complex and near the Soto Zen head temple, which KI-NRT calls phenomenal and historic, though he notes the inn is a bit out of the way. Cherry blossom comes in spring, deep snow and river mist in winter, and zazen and the dawn sutras at Eiheiji are a short drive away.

cities.text: Reverse of: A ~25-min cab straight between Eshikoto and Fukui Stn (Maps 22 min / 13.7 km), then the Hokuriku Shinkansen Fukui→Kanazawa (23–28 min, Maps). No rail change at all — no Echizen Railway.

Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' Tokyo→Fukui (2h49–2h58, Maps 2026-08-02; all 9 daily stop Fukui), then a ~25-min cab straight to Eshikoto (Maps 22 min / 13.7 km) — no rail change at all. Rail alt: Echizen Railway→Eiheijiguchi (~25 min, clockface :25/:55) + the inn pickup (request at booking — Eiheijiguchi is unmanned, no taxi rank) ≈ 3.6–3.8h with 1 change. (Was 3.5h off a ~2h51 + 30-min-cab pairing; re-timed 2026-08-02.)

'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp Kyoto→Tsuruga (~45 min), Hokuriku Shinkansen Tsuruga→Fukui (~18 min), then a ~25-min cab straight between Fukui Stn and Eshikoto (Maps 22 min / 13.7 km) — no Echizen Railway, no rail change. One change, at Tsuruga.

inns.name: Kinnotake Tonosawa
inns.summary: Kinnotake Tonosawa is an adults-only Hakone gorge property built around in-room open-air onsen bathing from its own alkaline spring. Ikyu guests rate it 4.51 across 86 reviews, and the reviews split sharply by floor: the 4F suites get unanimous five-star reports while the lower floors generate nearly all the complaints, and two recent reviews report a drop in staff experience and warmth. Book a 4F suite or reconsider.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is kaiseki in one shared dining room with two seatings, and there is no in-room dining. Ikyu guests often name the food a highlight of the stay. The alternative is the teppanyaki counter Zen, and the 4F suites get an upgraded menu with A5 kuroge filet and Ise-ebi. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.62.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All 21 rooms have their own open-air bath, free-flowing from the property's pH 9.5 spring, and the water runs at a coolish 40°C, though staff will raise it; there is no communal bath. In most rooms the washing area is outdoors, a cold dash in winter, and only TEN adds an indoor hinoki bath. Ikyu guests often call the room bath the best part of the stay and put it at 4.57.

service.label: Service
service.text: On the suite floor check-in happens in the room and the minibar is free, the lounge pours sparkling wine and beer free-flow until 22:00, and the staff will raise the temperature of the in-room bath (it runs around 40°C) if you ask. Most Ikyu guests describe warm, attentive staff, and Ikyu puts the service at 4.64, but two 2025 reviews describe a drop, with mostly trainee-badged, inexperienced young staff, smiling but not yet steady.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 4F suites TEN, SORA and KUMO are the rooms to book: every review on the inn's own per-room pages for them is five stars, while all the complaints about roof views, noise and cramped tubs come from the 1F and 2F rooms. KI-NRT, relaying friends who stayed, warns that the entry-level rooms are small, long and narrow, and that the decor is more country home than traditional ryokan. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.43, near their lowest mark.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: You enter over a suspension bridge across the Tonosawa gorge, and all the rooms face the forest and river away from Route 1. The inn is adults-only (12 and up). On January 2 and 3 the Hakone Ekiden relay crosses Route 1 by the bridge, a three-minute walk away, so a New Year stay puts you on the course.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Kofuyuden Beniya
inns.summary: A long-established 24-room inn in Awara Onsen with a private partly open-air bath in every room and Echizen snow crab in winter, which is why most people make the trip. Ikyu guests hold it in very high regard (4.82 across 183 reviews), praising the crab kaiseki and hands-on hospitality, and the recurring caution is that the room-bath water runs very hot. It is a different inn from Beniya Mukayu in Yamashiro, which is in a different prefecture.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Winter here is Echizen crab, served in your room, and you choose how it comes: the whole crab boiled, or the legs as sashimi with the shoulders and shells grilled. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.9, their highest mark, and the crab kaiseki and the unhurried pacing of the in-room dinner are what they praise most.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: All 24 rooms have their own semi-open-air onsen bath piped straight from the source, unrecirculated and unchlorinated, which KI-NRT singles out for anyone wanting a real onsen stay. The recurring note from Ikyu guests is that the water runs very hot, so the staff warn you to add cold water before getting in; they put the bath at 4.75, their lowest mark for the inn.

service.label: Service
service.text: Ikyu guests put service at 4.85 and describe warm, hands-on hospitality, an in-room dinner paced course by course and staff who warn you about the hot room bath before you get in. Two 2026 reviews are cooler on the staff's polish. Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: All 24 rooms have their own semi-open-air onsen bath, and since the 2021 rebuild KI-NRT finds them traditional in type but airy and fresh. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.79, just below their marks for the food and the service, and describe them as clean and well kept.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn was rebuilt in 2021 by the architect Tetsuo Kobori (winner of both the Architectural Institute of Japan Prize and the JIA Grand Prize in 2017) after a 2018 fire destroyed the property and three registered cultural-property buildings. It stands in the heart of Awara Onsen, Fukui's quiet Sea-of-Japan hot-spring town and the most prominent in the region, and KI-NRT recommends pairing Fukui with Eiheiji, which he calls phenomenal.

cities.text: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Tsurugi' Kanazawa→Awara-Onsen (~27 min), then the inn's free ~10-min shuttle (reserve by the day before; pickup 14:30–18:00) — Kofuyuden Beniya is in central Awara Onsen town, not out on the Mikuni coast (awara.co.jp/access; 2026-07 audit).
Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Hakutaka' direct Tokyo→Awara-Onsen (~2h55, a through service since the 2024 Tsuruga extension), then chauffeured car to Bouyourou on the Mikuni coast (~20 min).
Reverse of: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Tsurugi' Awara-Onsen→Tsuruga (~30 min), cross-platform change (~10 min), 'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp→Kyoto (~55 min) — segments re-timed 2026-07 audit; total holds.
Reverse of: ~30-min taxi/bus from Mikuni/Awara to Komatsu Airport, the KMQ→Fukuoka hop (~1h40, ~4 daily ANA/ORC), then the subway 2 stops into Hakata (~5 min). ~3.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: ~30-min taxi/bus to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Nishi-Kyushu relay→Nagasaki via Takeo-Onsen (~2h). ~5.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: ~30-min taxi/bus to Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h17). ~5.25h door-to-door.

inns.name: Lakeside Villa Suimeikaku
inns.summary: An eight-room chalet-style ryokan from 1967, the only property sitting directly on Lake Shikotsu, full of old-school charm and serving a posh Italian gourmet dinner. Michaeljinnyc, the one member to have stayed, calls it the best hotel he has stayed in in Hokkaido and would go back, but he wrote nothing about the bathing, the service or his room.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is Italian gourmet cooking, which Michaeljinnyc called fantastic, very posh and old school, and he thought enough of it to come back and add it to his post. He named no dishes.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every one of the eight rooms has a natural hot-spring indoor bath facing Lake Shikotsu, and two private open-air baths sit at the shore, Ruri in cypress and Hisui in stone. The inn pitches them as the closest baths to the lake of any local lodging, and it does not publish how the water is delivered. The one guest who has written about the inn never mentions bathing.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: Suimeikaku is a single-story chalet-style building from 1967 with eight rooms and plenty of old-school charm, but Michaeljinnyc did not describe his own room, and nobody else in the thread has stayed.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Suimeikaku sits directly on the shore of Lake Shikotsu, the only hotel here with a true lakeside position, in a single-story chalet-style building from 1967 that is full of old-school charm. Michaeljinnyc puts Shikotsu miles ahead of Lake Akan and calls this the best hotel he has stayed in in Hokkaido.

cities.text: ~30-40 min by car/shuttle from New Chitose Airport (CTS) to Shikotsuko Onsen.
~60 min by car from Sapporo to the lakeside onsen.

inns.name: Machiyado Ichiryu
inns.summary: An adults-only town inn of eleven rooms a few minutes' walk from Takayama's morning market and old streets, opened in November 2024 in place of the 53-year-old Ryokan Seiryu, whose 25 rooms were rebuilt as 11, six of them suites, each with a semi-open-air bath. Around them are three private baths on the Hida Takayama spring, an all-day lounge with Hida sake and an irori hearth, and Hida beef dinners served in a warehouse annex across the lane. The Ikyu crowd gives it 4.70 over 55 reviews, with hospitality (4.84) far ahead of meals and bathing (4.58 each).

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The inn calls itself a Hida beef specialist, and dinner is top A5 cuts served course by course in private rooms in a converted warehouse across the lane. An all-day lounge pours local Hida sake and draft beer, with snacks that change by the hour. Ikyu guests put meals at 4.58, the inn's softest mark, because a real minority reports over-marbled or tough beef or a thin breakfast, while many others call the pacing faultless.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no large public bath. The Hida Takayama spring (a mild alkaline simple onsen) reaches guests through three ground-floor private baths, two of them free whenever vacant and the premium Miyagawa reservable by the hour for ¥4,400. Every room also has a semi-open-air bath, but it runs plain hot water, and guests say so repeatedly at this price. Ikyu guests put bathing at 4.58, and the other gripe is that the tubs are deep and have no step.

service.label: Service
service.text: Hospitality is what guests write about first, and Ikyu guests put it at 4.84, the inn's strongest mark by a clear margin. They describe valet parking with a hand-drawn map of the lot, staff waiting outside with umbrellas for the walk to dinner, unprompted lifts to the station, handwritten notes in the room and a contactless butler box at the door. The staff are mostly young, and guests take that as warmth. Nobody has complained of inexperience.

room.label: Room
room.text: Eleven rooms only, six of them suites, were rebuilt from the old Ryokan Seiryu's 25, and each has its own semi-open-air bath. They run 40–50 m² and up in a Japanese-Western style, with Hida-crafted furniture, tatami corners, semi-double twins, ReFa shower heads and amenities throughout, and free minibar and lounge drinks. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.73. The higher floors get the mountain view, and the lower ones look onto neighbouring roofs.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Ichiryu is the rare ryokan that cooks a full dinner and still lets you walk out the door and be sightseeing: the Miyagawa morning market is three minutes away, the preserved sake-brewery streets of the old town five, Takayama Jinya six, and the station and the Kanazawa bus seven. The lounge (Hida furniture, an irori hearth, a terrace) is where the inn keeps its town-inn character. It is adults only, and elementary age and under are not accepted.

cities.text: Reverse of: Nohi/Hokutetsu highway bus Takayama Nohi Bus Center→Kanazawa Stn west exit via Shirakawa-gō (~2h15, direct, reserve — the bus centre is at Takayama Stn, a 7-min walk from the inn). No rail link exists; the bus is the fast way.

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya (~2h30), change ~15 min to a Tōkaidō 'Nozomi'→Tokyo (~1h42) + hotel/station ends. (Via Toyama is nominally quicker — 'Hida' ~1h30 + Hokuriku Shinkansen ~2h06 — but only ~4 Toyama through-trains run per day.)

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya (~2h30; 10/day — hourly only ~11:30–16:30, with 2h gaps outside), ~15-min transfer to a Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Nozomi'→Kyoto (34 min). Alt with NO change: Hida 36 departs Takayama 15:33 direct to Kyoto, arr 19:17. ⚠ The Takayama line is snow-exposed — JR Central posts 大雪 advisories most Januaries; keep same-day slack. (All-reserved Dec 25–Jan 5; mixed seating otherwise.) Equal-time alternative that dodges that exposure: the Nohi highway bus Takayama→Nagoya + the same Nozomi — Maps returns this chain, not the Hida, as its three fastest (3h25–3h33 station-to-station), so take whichever the weather favours.

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya (~2h25; 10/day, hourly only ~11:30–16:30, 2h gaps outside), ~20-min cross-platform transfer to a Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Nozomi' Nagoya→Shin-Osaka (~50 min, frequent), then the Midōsuji subway Shin-Osaka→Umeda/Namba (~5–10 min) + the walk to the hotel. Two changes, at Nagoya and Shin-Osaka. ⚠ the Takayama Line is snow-exposed — JR Central posts 大雪 advisories most Januaries, and Dec 25–Jan 5 is all-reserved; keep same-day slack. Equal-time alternative that dodges the exposure: the Nohi highway bus Takayama→Nagoya + the same Nozomi. Sources: japan-guide Takayama access; JR Central Tōkaidō/Takayama Line timetables.

Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Hida' Takayama→Nagoya, ~2h25 direct, 10 a day (hourly only ~11:30–16:30, 2h gaps outside), ¥5,610 unreserved / ¥6,140 reserved, + the 7-min walk from the inn/old town. ⚠ Snow-exposed — JR Central posts 大雪 advisories most Januaries, all-reserved Dec 25–Jan 5. Equal-time alternative when the line is under an advisory: the Nohi highway bus Takayama Nōhi BC→Meitetsu BC Nagoya, ~2h45, reserved.

inns.name: Madoka no Mori
inns.summary: A forest ryokan in Gora (opened 2014) whose strengths are the shared facilities: three open-air forest tubs per gender fed by a second spring, a private stone sauna and a basement speakeasy bar. The crowd picture is strong (Jalan 4.9, Ikyu 4.78 across 86 reviews). Recent Ikyu reviews split on where it is heading, though: most still rate it near-perfect, while two 2025-26 stays sense the service sliding toward ordinary. Book a bedroom-plus-tatami or a deluxe room and avoid the 30 m² studios.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Hida beef shabu is the standout course, extraordinarily buttery, and a new head chef has refreshed the tableware and the appetizer courses. Standard rooms eat in private dining rooms; in-room dinner is for the suites only. The sushi course is the weak link and the menu barely rotates. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.84, their highest mark here, and even the critical reviews call the meals excellent.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The inn draws on two hot-spring sources: the big baths run on one the staff describe as sterilizing, the in-room tubs on a second, moisturizing one, and they will tell you to take the big bath first. Each gender side has one indoor bath and three open-air tubs in the forest, and a private stone sauna (ganbanyoku) can be booked by the slot. Two 2025-26 reviews question the cleanliness of the big baths.

service.label: Service
service.text: Guests are greeted with a welcome drink and the house pastry chef's pudding, with handmade sweets left in the room, and Ikyu guests describe the staff as uniformly pleasant and well trained, putting service at 4.8. The inn has a strong repeat clientele, and returning guests say the unobtrusive attentiveness is what brings them back. Two 2025-26 reviews report the service slipping toward that of an ordinary luxury ryokan.

room.label: Room
room.text: Every room has its own onsen tub, but the 30 m² studios, where the beds take over and there is no sofa, draw the most repeated complaint. Ask for one of the 36.5-41 m² bedroom-plus-tatami rooms instead, or the 53 m² deluxe rooms Ebine 311 and Akebonosou 215 with their window sofas; KI-NRT's advice for a first Hakone trip is a suite here. The rooms have exposed-beam ceilings, and the 2014 fittings are starting to show.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Madoka no Mori sits in the forest above Gora at about 550 m, high enough for occasional real snow, and the January-February reports are uniformly positive. Inside, the corridors are tatami and guests walk them barefoot, the lobby is spacious and impressive, and KI-NRT counts it (with its sister Gora Hanaougi) among the few traditional-style inns at the top of Hakone, where most of the highly regarded properties are modern and Western in design.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Meigetsuso
inns.summary: Meigetsuso is twenty detached sukiya villas on a wooded hillside above Kaminoyama Onsen, fifteen of them with their own open-air rotenburo, and it runs as an in-room Yamagata kaiseki retreat with hiba-cypress communal baths. Ikyu regulars rate it 4.77 across 39 reviews and call the food some of the best of all their stays. Winter access over the Itaya pass is prone to snow delays.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is seasonal Yamagata kaiseki from local ingredients, served in the room, and the course guests talk about is the beef comparison that puts Yonezawa beef next to Yamagata beef. Breakfast rice is kettle-cooked in two local varieties, and the cellar lets you pick from three labels of Juyondai sake. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.84 and several rank it among the best of all their stays.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Fifteen of the twenty villas have their own open-air rotenburo, and there are also two reservable private baths and communal baths in Aomori hiba cypress with outdoor tubs. Ikyu guests put the baths at 4.79, and it is the private baths, in the room and the reservable ones, that they praise most.

service.label: Service
service.text: The inn pays the taxi fare from the station, which several guests mention with surprise, and with only 20 detached villas and dinner and breakfast served in the room, contact with staff is low-key and you see little of the other guests. Repeat visits are a theme in the Ikyu reviews, where several writers are back for a second or third stay or end by saying they will return. Ikyu guests put service at 4.85, the highest mark they give the inn.

room.label: Room
room.text: The twenty rooms are detached sukiya-zukuri villas on a wooded hillside, with a relocated 1920 kura storehouse on the grounds. One room type has a tatami room, a dining room and a twin-bed Western bedroom plus a half-open-air bath and a terrace facing the Zao range. Another is a 55-square-metre main room and living room with a Zao view. Ikyu guests give the rooms 4.67.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Meigetsuso sits on a wooded hillside facing the Zao range at Kaminoyama Onsen, a quiet castle town in Yamagata off the foreign-tourist circuit, and with only twenty rooms the whole place is quiet. From the verandas you look at the Zao peaks, and at night the moon the inn is named for. Late January puts the Zao snow monsters next door, and KI-NRT had planned a stay here around cherry picking in nearby Sagae and Tendo.

cities.text: Yamagata Shinkansen 'Tsubasa' direct Tokyo→Kaminoyama-Onsen (~2h40), then a ~6-min taxi. ⚠ the Itaya-pass Tsubasa is among Japan's most winter-delay-prone segments.
Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Ōmiya, then the through 'Tsubasa'→Kaminoyama-Onsen (one ride from Ōmiya) + short taxi. Single change at Ōmiya. ⚠ the Itaya-pass Tsubasa is the fragile leg.

Reverse of: Direct Yamako Kaminoyama–Sendai expressway bus (~1h15, 6–8/day). Chosen over the rail alt (Tōhoku Shinkansen→Fukushima ~13 min + Yamagata 'Tsubasa'→Kaminoyama-Onsen ~50 min + ~6-min taxi, ≈1.25h/1tx): same clock, but no change and it avoids the winter-fragile Itaya-pass 'Tsubasa'.

inns.name: Ochiairo
inns.summary: A heritage onsen inn at an Izu river confluence, built around a bath-and-sauna complex inside 90-year-old architecture. It holds a Michelin 1-Key, and is #1 of 47 in Izu on Booking at 9.4 and 4.64 across 101 Ikyu reviews. The recurring complaint is service short of the price. Book by room name, because only four rooms have private open-air onsen, and note that the rebuilt thermal spring now runs mixed-gender in bathing wear.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: An 8 to 9 course Izu kaiseki is served in private dining rooms, and the menu changes completely across a two-night stay; the breakfast cult item is wasabi rice, and there is also a steakhouse, which KI-NRT points out is a rarity at a traditional ryokan. Sake, wine and champagne pairings are included. Several 2026 guests found dinner neither good nor bad for the price, and Ikyu guests give the meals 4.54.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The tea-room sauna at the Moon Bath, produced by sauna expert Dai Matsuo, made Japan's SAUNACHELIN ranking in 2019 and 2020, and the hinoki-lined Tengu Sauna is one of the few in Japan to use hot-spring water for its steam, with a river plunge of about 14°C in winter. The private Hoshi-no-yu bath is free if you reserve at check-in, and tattoos are fine. The rebuilt thermal spring is mixed-gender in bathing wear, which Japanese guests dislike.

service.label: Service
service.text: Everything is included (station shuttle, a nightly-restocked minibar, a beer as you leave the bath). The reviews split on the hospitality itself, and Ikyu guests put service at 4.46, their lowest mark for the inn, with the recurring complaint that the staff fall short of what the price demands.

room.label: Room
room.text: Only four rooms have a private open-air onsen, so book by name: Ukifune (74 m², heritage Meiun-tei wing), Kobai and Tokonatsu (both with an indoor tub too) and Yamazakura, which has the best outdoor bath but no indoor one. The Meiun-tei three are the most secluded but farthest from the baths (stairs, no elevator); Yamazakura is steps away. Corridors and tatami are floor-heated.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn drapes down a hillside in Yugashima, inland Izu, where the Nekkoshi and Hontani rivers meet, and the bath complex hangs right over the confluence; KI-NRT calls it the famed Ochiairo. It is quiet wherever you are in the building, with a reading room and tea lounge off the main building and the heritage architecture kept immaculate. The one blemish anyone mentions is the derelict buildings visible across the river.

cities.text: Shinkansen Tokyo→Mishima (~50 min), Izuhakone Sunzu line→Shuzenji (~35 min), then the free inn shuttle ~25 min (Ochiairo includes it — reserve; Arcana is a sparse Tokai bus or ~20-min taxi).
Reverse of: Inn shuttle back to Shuzenji (~25 min), then Izuhakone Sunzu line + Tōkaidō Shinkansen Shuzenji→Kyoto door-to-door ~2h38 (Google Maps live routing, confirms the Mishima change).

inns.name: Risonare Yatsugatake
inns.summary: Hoshino's Bellini-designed alpine-village resort at Yatsugatake has 172 rooms, a design pool and wine education around a 2,000-bottle cellar, and it is family-friendly and lively, the counterpoint to the quiet inns, at the bottom of its price class at $300–600 a night. The Ikyu crowd (4.32 across 74 reviews) is lukewarm and pool-shy, marking the bathing weakest at 3.69 against food's 4.62, and couples without children should expect a resort run for families.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The food program is built around wine, with a cellar of about 2,000 bottles, a daily Wine School and winemaker's dinners. At the YY Grill Ikyu guests praise the cooking and the wine that goes with it, and the buffet lets you choose your main. After dinner the Awa Lounge pours wine and grape juice free of charge. Ikyu guests give the food 4.62, the property's best mark.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no hot spring. Bathing is an all-weather design pool and a spa with heated water, and some rooms have a private open-air bath, the one private soak at a 172-room resort. Families praise the pool as clean, big and child-friendly, and Ikyu reviewers write about the pool far more than the bath; most of them are there with children, so expect children in the water. Ikyu guests give the bath 3.69, the property's lowest mark by far.

service.label: Service
service.text: This is a 172-room Hoshino resort, and the service is resort operations at scale for families with children. Ikyu guests repeatedly call the staff lovely, and those booking through Ikyu mention small perks waiting in the room. Ikyu guests give the service 4.46.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are spread through the resort's alpine-village complex. Nobody has written about the rooms themselves. Ikyu guests give them 4.35, middling next to the food and service.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Italian architect Mario Bellini designed the master plan, a walkable alpine village at the foot of Yatsugatake on the Yamanashi-Nagano wine border. It is overwhelmingly a family and children's resort, and the Ikyu reviews come almost entirely from families with small children, so couples travelling without them should expect a lively, child-filled lobby.

cities.text: Reverse of: JR Chūō Ltd Exp 'Azusa' Kobuchizawa→Shinjuku direct (~1h50–2h, ~hourly).
Tōkaidō Shinkansen Kyoto→Nagoya (~35 min), Chūō 'Shinano' Ltd Exp Nagoya→Shiojiri, then Chūō (Azusa/local) to Kobuchizawa + shuttle — the Nagoya cross-country beats routing back through Tokyo.

inns.name: River Retreat Garaku
inns.summary: River Retreat Garaku is Toyama's design showpiece on the Jinzu gorge, with Hiroshi Naito architecture, serious art, in-room onsen-and-sauna suites and a French restaurant, and nobody in the FlyerTalk thread has stayed here. The kitchen holds a Michelin Green Star, and Ikyu guests rate it 4.63 across 89 reviews and describe a strong art-and-dinner stay, though a recurring minority calls the aesthetic self-indulgent, the bathing ordinary and the staff inexperienced. It is a promising design-and-sauna stay, but an unproven one.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is French at the in-house Trésonnier, which holds a Michelin Green Star (L'évo and its chef left in 2020, so older food press describes a kitchen that is no longer here). Guests praise the Toyama ingredients, crab, white shrimp, grass-fed beef and vegetables from the hotel garden, with strong wine pairings. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.59, though a minority find the more experimental courses miss.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The Annex Premier suites have their own hot-spring bath, and two of them pair it with an in-room sauna, while the guest spa adds a dry sauna and a cold plunge. That is an unusually strong sauna offering for a ryokan, and the in-room bath is also the way around the tattoo ban in the public baths. Ikyu guests put the bathing at 4.7.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is understated and hospitable in the guest accounts, and the staff are described as cheerful. After check-in they run a guided art tour of the building and garden that explains the thinking behind the pieces.
