Ikyu guests put service at 4.52, their lowest mark for the inn, and the recurring complaint is inexperienced staff, so a stay that goes right on the design and the dinner can still stumble on the floor.

room.label: Room
room.text: There are roughly 23 rooms, each individually designed, across a forested riverside estate, and the Annex Premier suites with their own onsen run 115 to 150 square metres. Hiroshi Naito's architecture and a museum-grade art collection set the tone, and the rooms look onto the Jinzu River. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.67, among the strongest points here.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The estate sits in the forest on the Jinzu gorge outside Toyama, and the lobby's stacked precast-concrete wall in the azekura style was designed by the architect Hiroshi Naito. Art fills the building and garden (a guided tour after check-in explains the pieces), the garden grows vegetables for the kitchen, and rooms look straight onto the river. It is riverside scenery in the foothills near the city, so snow is lighter than at deep-belt inns.

cities.text: Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Toyama (~23 min), then a ~40-min taxi/inn car to Garaku.
Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' Tokyo→Toyama (~2h06), then a ~40-min taxi/inn car to River Retreat Garaku in the Jinzu gorge (free shuttle from Sasazu Stn, 3 min, if timed).
'Thunderbird' Ltd Exp Kyoto→Tsuruga (~50 min), self-change at Tsuruga onto the Hokuriku Shinkansen→Toyama (~1h), then inn car up to Garaku (~40 min). The Tsuruga change is the one transfer.
Reverse of: Airport bus Toyama Station→Toyama Airport (~25 min), the TOY→Fukuoka hop (~1h40, ~3 daily ANA/IBEX), then the subway 2 stops into Hakata (~5 min). ~3.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: Airport bus Toyama→TOY + TOY→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Nishi-Kyushu relay→Nagasaki via Takeo-Onsen (~2h). ~5.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: Airport bus Toyama→TOY + TOY→Fukuoka (~1h40, ANA/IBEX) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho'→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h17). ~5.25h door-to-door.

inns.name: STAY366
inns.summary: A two-rooms-a-night micro-auberge run by the 98WINEs winery above Katsunuma, Japan's first inn with an in-house winery and craft brewery, pairing soba-kaiseki with the maker's own back vintages. Ikyu guests describe it uniformly enthusiastically, praising the Fuji views, personal hosting from the owner, and inventive food, with roughly 40% returning within a year. It is best slotted as a single wine-centric night for the drinking-and-dining concept, which strong crowd sentiment backs up.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a soba-based kaiseki with a different wine paired to every plate, all from the 98WINEs cellar next door and reaching back into older vintages, and the owner serves it himself. The specialty is grilled eel and black truffle wrapped in a soft galette, and Ikyu guests praise both the inventive cooking and the pairing. Before dinner the house craft beer flows freely until 6pm.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: There is no hot spring here. The private bath looks out over the Katsunuma valley and is filled with heated water. Nobody has written about the bathing itself.

service.label: Service
service.text: The owner serves dinner himself and the conversation runs along with it, and on arrival the winemaker and the brewer each talk you through their own tasting. Ikyu guests describe the staff as warm and smiling and count the talk with them among the pleasures of the stay, and after its first year open the inn was reporting that four in ten guests came back.

room.label: Room
room.text: The rooms are calm and not showy, with the owner's taste visible in the small choices and the fittings and amenities chosen with care down to the smallest item, and there is no TV or clock, in keeping with the inn's idea of a stay as an extra day. Only two rooms are let each night.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn sits above the Katsunuma vineyards in Koshu with a view of Mount Fuji and the mountain ranges below it that Ikyu guests praise again and again, and the winery and craft brewery are on the property, so the afternoon runs from a tasting at 98WINEs (named one of the world's best wineries in 2023) to beer with the brewer in front of the mountains.

cities.text: Ltd Exp 'Kaiji' Shinjuku→Enzan (~1h30), then ~10-min drive — inn pickup from Enzan Station (reserve).
Reverse of: The long way round: Ltd Exp 'Shinano' route west via Kōfu to Nagoya (~2.5h), Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h) — a genuine transit day.

inns.name: Saryo Souen
inns.summary: A tranquil, traditional ryokan near Sendai that KI-NRT names on his Tohoku recommendation list and calls a matter of taste against the larger, homier Daikon no Hana, while flagging it as quite a bit pricier. He stayed, but many years ago, and left little beyond that one impression of the atmosphere. Ikyu guests have more to say, putting it at 4.62 overall with the baths at 4.77, and their reviews return to the garden, the detached rooms and the attentive hospitality.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the food here, and KI-NRT's comparison with Daikon no Hana does not touch it. Dinner is kaiseki, and Ikyu guests give the meals their lowest mark at 4.55, a little under their other marks. The few reservations they voice are about dinner, both the make-up of the courses and the pace at which the meal is served.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Akiu's own sodium-calcium chloride spring feeds gender-split main baths, each with a rock-built open-air bath onto the garden, and the nine detached cottages have private open-air baths. Whether the flow is free-running is not published. KI-NRT's own comparison says nothing about the baths. Ikyu guests make them the best-liked part of the stay (4.77), praising the bathhouse and the cottage rotenburo.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service. Ikyu guests put it at 4.64, in line with their other marks, and describe attentive staff who keep a discreet distance, close at hand when needed and never hovering, and the warmest reviews call the whole stay close to perfect.

room.label: Room
room.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the rooms. On Ikyu the detached rooms are what guests talk about, looking onto the inner garden with their own open-air baths, which reviews repeatedly call spacious. The rooms draw 4.59 from Ikyu guests, a little under their other marks.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: KI-NRT found it more tranquil and traditional than Daikon no Hana, and that is all he has said, from a stay many years ago, so treat the impression as dated. Ikyu guests fill in the picture with a beautiful inner garden that the detached rooms look onto, polished corridors and deep quiet, and there is no guest lounge.

cities.text: Akiu Onsen is roughly 30-40 min by car or shuttle bus from JR Sendai Station.
Tohoku Shinkansen Hayabusa from Tokyo to Sendai is about 1h30, then roughly 40 min by car out to Akiu Onsen.

inns.name: Seiryuso
inns.summary: Seiryuso is a classic garden sukiya inn at the bottom of Izu with a seafood kitchen and a one-of-a-kind spa (own-source onsen plus Japan's oldest Kelo sauna, a Thermarium and an onsen pool). Ikyu guests rate it 4.66 over 75 reviews, with recurring niggles about weak shower pressure and a dated, stairs-heavy building.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Seafood leads the kitchen, with kinme-dai (golden-eye snapper), Ise lobster and abalone, and food is the top mark this inn gets on every platform. Guests call the meals delicious, and the new maisonette rooms come with free drinks through dinner. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.67.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The onsen is the inn's own source, free-flowing in the indoor and open-air baths and even in the garden pool (swimsuits on). The spa adds Japan's oldest Kelo Finnish sauna, with löyly and open-air rest beds, plus a Roman-style Thermarium. The room baths are rock-lined onsen usable at any hour. Weak shower pressure in the main bath is the recurring complaint.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service gets the warmest marks here. The staff are young, and Ikyu reviews repeatedly praise them as kind and good at explaining the ingredients as they serve the courses. Ikyu guests put service at 4.76, their highest mark for the inn.

room.label: Room
room.text: The inn is a classic sukiya building set in 6,600 square metres of garden, and the rooms show their age. Guests describe dated, Showa-retro tatami rooms and a building with many level changes and steps. On the plus side, the in-room open-air baths are huge, with a small private garden in front, and the maisonette rooms added in December 2025 are clean and new. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.64.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Rendaiji Onsen at Shimoda is the far-south tip of Izu, and the inn sits in generous gardens, 6,600 square metres of them, with a calm, old-school atmosphere that flows through the whole place. From the room baths you look onto small private gardens. The one drawback is geography, since Shimoda is a long way down the peninsula and a backtrack to go anywhere else, so it works best as a southern out-and-back.

cities.text: JR Ltd Exp 'Odoriko'/'Saphir Odoriko' Tokyo→Izukyū-Shimoda (~2h45, one seat), then Seiryuso's free shuttle (~10 min, reserve the prior day).
Reverse of: Inn shuttle + Odoriko LEX Izukyū-Shimoda→Atami (~70 min), then 'Hikari' Atami→Kyoto (~2h; 'Nozomi' skips Atami). Far-south Izu — a backtrack to go anywhere.

inns.name: Sekiyo
inns.summary: A quiet nine-room retreat on the wooded slope of Mt. Wakakusa above Yugawara, a former villa dressed with antiques and local artists' work, with wide views to Mt. Iwato and the Jukkoku Pass. Its own free-flowing spring feeds the public baths and the in-room kakenagashi tubs in seven of the nine rooms, and the kaiseki leans on Sagami Bay seafood, with the Manazuru abalone course as the seasonal centrepiece. Ikyu guests rate it 4.77 across 51 stays, the rooms and the cooking their high marks. Nobody in the thread has stayed yet, though KI-NRT counts it with Yui as Yugawara's two top luxury inns.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kaiseki leans on Sagami Bay seafood from Manazuru and local organic vegetables, cooked to bring out the ingredient, and the Manazuru abalone course is the seasonal headline. KI-NRT says it is highly regarded for its food, and Ikyu guests put the meals near 4.82, among their high marks; repeat guests come back for it. Some 2025 and 2026 repeaters found the seasoning heavier.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The inn draws its own 76° sodium-chloride spring and runs it free-flowing through two public bath areas, each with an indoor and an open-air bath, which swap at midnight. Seven of the nine rooms have a private kakenagashi bath, but those are all indoors (Shiroyama and Midori have none), so the only open-air bathing is communal. KI-NRT notes that Yui has an open-air onsen in every room. Ikyu guests put the baths near 4.80 and call the onsen quiet.

service.label: Service
service.text: Sekiyo is a quiet, understated inn where the hospitality is personal, and Ikyu guests put the service near 4.71, singling out the considerate, unobtrusive attention and the spotless upkeep. KI-NRT has heard of incredible hospitality here, but two 2026 Ikyu reviews describe lapses at dinner service, and a FlyerTalk member's two emails went unanswered for two weeks.

room.label: Room
room.text: The nine wooden sukiya rooms sit in a former villa on a wooded slope, spread across a main building and detached annexes, dressed with antiques and local artists' work and open to garden and mountains. Seven have their own indoor onsen bath; Shiroyama and Midori do not, so avoid those two if the in-room bath matters. Ikyu guests give the rooms their highest mark and praise the serene seasonal detailing.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Sekiyo sits on the wooded slope of Mt. Wakakusa above Yugawara Onsen, a former villa woven into the hillside with a tended garden and wide views to Mt. Iwato and the Jukkoku Pass. Plum and cherry bloom in spring and camellias in winter, and it is quiet up here, a short climb from the coast. Yugawara is a tiny onsen town, but KI-NRT says it has more good ryokans than its size suggests.

cities.text: Reverse of: JR Ltd Exp 'Odoriko' Tokyo→Yugawara (~70 min, one seat), then a short taxi up Mt. Wakakusa to the inn.
Reverse of: Tōkaidō line Yugawara→Atami (~7 min, one stop), then 'Hikari' Atami→Kyoto (~1h57; 'Nozomi' skips Atami). ~2h20, one change at Atami.

inns.name: Sengokuhara COCON
inns.summary: Sengokuhara COCON is a five-suite small-luxury auberge opened in February 2024 in the Sengokuhara highlands of Hakone (800 m, on a 1,000-tsubo garden), where each suite has an in-room Owakudani onsen plus its own dry sauna and cold bath, and dinner is a modern French menu poured with free-flow champagne. A rotating 'stay & art' program dresses the rooms and the gallery. Ikyu guests give it 4.87 across some 140 stays, with service their highest mark at 4.94. Nobody in the thread has stayed here yet.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is modern French built on Hakone and Izu produce by chef Yokoyama, poured with free-flow champagne, and the pairings (Meursault and Château Talbot have appeared) recur in the praise. Ikyu guests mark the cooking near 4.86, the softer of the top marks only because every mark here is high, and repeat guests report the cooking holding up visit after visit.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Each of the five suites has its own in-room Owakudani onsen plus a private dry sauna (up to 90°C on request), a cold plunge and a terrace for the air bath, and there is a large public bath too. There is no open-air tub in the rooms and no bath has a view, but the in-suite sauna-and-plunge set is what guests praise, and Ikyu guests mark the bathing near 4.85.

service.label: Service
service.text: COCON is a five-suite house where the staff-to-guest ratio shows, and Ikyu guests mark hospitality 4.94, the highest of every sub-mark, with anticipatory, unhurried care the recurring theme. Repeat guests dominate the reviews, and they describe preferences remembered from earlier visits and every request met gladly.

room.label: Room
room.text: The five rooms are all suites, at 800 m in the Sengokuhara highlands, and each has an in-room onsen, a dry sauna and a cold bath, plus artworks that change under the 'stay & art' program; the room baths are wide and comfortable. Ikyu guests put the rooms among their highest marks, with the space and the design the standout.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: COCON sits on a 1,000-tsubo garden in the Sengokuhara highlands of northern Hakone (800 m), near the Owakudani source and the pampas-grass fields, a quiet upland-resort address opened in February 2024 whose gallery and rotating 'stay & art' installations run through the common spaces. Three goats live on the grounds. Mount Fuji shows from the rooms.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Shiojitei
inns.summary: A Toba seaside ryokan known from a single 2018 member stay, which ruby&carlos recalled as quite nice and definitely in the luxury category, with great views, good food that stopped short of spectacular, and strong value at the price she paid. She posted to ask what the thread's two-to-three-times-pricier inns offer over it, and with no second stay in the thread the impression stays a thin one, comfortable and no more than that.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: ruby&carlos, who stayed in 2018, called the food good though not spectacular, and she came to the thread to ask what the far pricier kitchens deliver that this one does not. Nobody else has described a meal here.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Her 2018 room had no private onsen, and nobody in the thread has written about the baths themselves.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: The only thing said about the rooms is that hers in 2018 had no private onsen, and nobody in the thread has described the rooms themselves.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Great views are the one thing ruby&carlos singled out about this seaside ryokan in Toba, and nobody else in the thread has described the location.

cities.text: Kintetsu LEX Nagoya->Toba ~1h35, then ~5 min shuttle from Toba Stn.
Kintetsu LEX Osaka->Toba ~2h (one transfer at Iseshi/Ujiyamada), then ~5 min shuttle.

inns.name: Shoraiso
inns.summary: A five-room inn re-opened in 2024 a five-minute drive from the Jigokudani snow-monkey park, with large in-room onsen baths (bigger than Takinami's, by KI-NRT's research) and dinner served in-room or in private rooms. Ikyu guests put it at 4.86 over 90 reviews and mostly rave, though a minority found the kaiseki unmemorable and the main bath a walk to the older sister property. It looks promising, and the crowd largely loves it.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a monthly-changing kaiseki built around the head chef's dashi, and guests split on it more than anything else. Ikyu guests put food at 4.83 and repeatedly single out the delicacy of the dashi, and several rank it among the best they have eaten at any ryokan, though a minority find the meal less memorable than the price suggests. A lounge pours free-flow craft beer, local juice and pudding.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own onsen bath, and they are large, bigger than Takinami's by KI-NRT's research. The main bath is the famous Momoyama bath at Yorozuya, the older sister inn across the way, with a small sauna attached, though it means a walk across to the older building. Nobody says whether the water runs free from the source. Ikyu guests put the baths at 4.88.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has stayed here. Ikyu guests give service their highest mark (4.92) and describe well-paced, attentive staff, and the head chef comes to the table himself to finish the meat course, a visit guests divide on, some counting it a highlight and others a performance. Spheres_pnw wondered whether the effusive early reviews are unprompted, since the owner answers almost all of them on Google.

room.label: Room
room.text: Five rooms since the 2024 re-opening, each with its own onsen bath, and KI-NRT, who has not stayed, rates them highly from his research, with larger in-room onsen than at Yamagata The Takinami and the choice of dinner in the room or in a private dining room. Ikyu guests put rooms at 4.83 and like the Nagano-themed amenities, the Japanese-made fixtures and the cleanliness of a new building. The smallest of the five is Shakunage, upstairs.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Shoraiso is in Nagano about a five-minute drive from Jigokudani Monkey Park, which KI-NRT counts as a plus if you are into that sort of thing, and outside snow-monkey season he says there is not enough to do nearby to warrant more than one night unless you have a rental car. The inn is the newer annex of Yorozuya, whose retro main building stands just across the way, and Ikyu guests describe a peaceful, new and spotless place.

cities.text: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' Tokyo→Nagano (~1h20–1h30), change to the Nagaden Ltd Exp 'Snow Monkey'/'Yukemuri'→Yudanaka (~45 min), then ~7 min to the inn — snow-monkey country. ~2h35 door-to-door. ⚠ Nagaden halved ltd-exp service to ~10/day (Sep 2024) — plan the Nagano connection; local fallback ~70–80 min.

Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' Kanazawa→Nagano (~65 min), Nagaden Ltd Exp→Yudanaka (~45 min) + ~7 min (inn pickup 15:00–18:30, or walk). ⚠ Nagaden halved ltd-exp service to ~10/day (Sep 2024) — the Nagano connection is roughly hourly; local fallback ~70–80 min. Nagano is a straight shot on the mainline return.

inns.name: Sosuikyo
inns.summary: Twelve detached villas scattered through trees at the foot of the Suzuka range, opened in July 2020 as the annex of Aqua Ignis. Each villa is built around a single material (earth, stone, wood, lacquer, washi, glass, iron) with the art chosen by the ceramicist Koichi Uchida, every one has a free-flowing open-air onsen off a 43°C spring on its terrace, and two villas have added a hinoki sauna and cold plunge. Dinner comes from the Aqua Ignis restaurants a shuttle away. The Ikyu crowd gives it 4.67 over 85 reviews, with bathing and service high and the meals softer.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Sosuikyo has no kitchen of its own, so dinner is chosen from the Aqua Ignis complex a shuttle away: the Michelin-starred kaiseki counter Roan Yumiji (villa guests only), Okuda Masayuki's Italian Al Checciano, HINOMORI, an eel house and a soba shop. Ikyu guests put meals at 4.48, the inn's weakest mark, for a specific reason: the kaiseki and the kappo draw superlatives, while the Italian and the thin breakfasts collect most of the complaints.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: People come back for the water: an alkaline simple spring at 43°C and 460 litres a minute, unwatered and free-flowing into a private open-air bath at every villa, with the big Kataoka baths at Aqua Ignis a shuttle away. Ikyu guests put bathing at 4.76. Two villas, Kinotoki and Sekiro, now add a hinoki 'kupu' sauna with a hinoki or Komono-stone cold plunge on Suzuka groundwater. In winter the crowd has found the bath temperature running lukewarm.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is the inn's strongest mark, with Ikyu guests putting it at 4.79, and it is of a small, unshowy, adjusting kind. Guests describe their car recognised before they have given a name, luggage carried, shuttles run on demand well before check-in, and again and again a complaint from one stay fixed by the next. A minority found the manner formal and without much warmth.

room.label: Room
room.text: Each of the twelve detached villas runs roughly 90 m² and is built around one of eight materials (earth, stone, plaster, wood, lacquer, washi, glass, iron), with a bedroom, a tatami corner, a mini-kitchen and antiques chosen by the ceramicist Koichi Uchida. No two are alike, and regulars work through them stay by stay. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.69, and the recurring gripes are draughtiness in winter and visible wear in the older villas.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The villas sit on a quiet wooded parcel along a river at the foot of the Suzuka mountains, five minutes' walk from Kintetsu Yunoyama-Onsen and about an hour out of Nagoya, so the valley feels remote even though it is on a commuter line, with Mount Gozaisho above and Ise within a day. The one drawback is that the inn keeps almost no common space of its own, because dining, the large bath and the bakery are all over at Aqua Ignis.

cities.text: Reverse of: Yunoyama Line→Kintetsu-Yokkaichi (~25–30 min), Kintetsu Ltd Exp→Nagoya (~30 min), then the Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Nozomi'/'Hikari' Nagoya→Kyoto (~35 min). Two changes, all high-frequency.

Reverse of: Yunoyama Line→Kintetsu-Yokkaichi (~25–30 min), Kintetsu Ltd Exp→Nagoya (~30 min), then the Tōkaidō Shinkansen 'Nozomi' Nagoya→Tokyo (~1h40). Two changes; Nagoya is the pivot for everything from here.

Reverse of: Kintetsu Yunoyama Line local Yunoyama-Onsen→Kintetsu-Yokkaichi (~25–30 min, ~2/hr), change to a Kintetsu Ltd Exp→Kintetsu-Nagoya (~30 min). One change at Yokkaichi; the inn's free shuttle covers the 5-min walk if you ask.

inns.name: Takaragawa Osenkaku
inns.summary: A rustic bath destination in Minakami and no luxury ryokan, which SeamasterLux, the one member who has stayed, says himself ("not luxurious by any means") while calling it a wonderful experience he would repeat, all for the large riverside mixed-gender rotenburo. The river runs through the middle of the property with the open-air baths along its banks, and the baths are why people come, since nobody has praised the rooms, the food or the polish. The soak in an extraordinary place is the memory he took away, and the inn around it is beside the point.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the food here.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The large mixed-gender open-air onsen is the reason people come, with the river flowing through the middle of the property. SeamasterLux calls the baths beautiful and the stay a wonderful experience ("What an experience!"), and he came back to the thread looking for anything comparable, without much luck. KI-NRT has never stayed, though he confirms Takaragawa Onsen is well regarded for exactly this kind of communal mixed-gender bath.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here.

room.label: Room
room.text: Nobody has described the rooms. SeamasterLux, the one member who has stayed, calls the property "not luxurious by any means", and that is all the thread says about the accommodation.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The river flowing through the middle of the property, with the open-air baths on its banks, is the setting, and SeamasterLux calls it the highlight of the stay. Nothing else about the surroundings has been described in the thread.

cities.text: Joetsu Shinkansen Tokyo->Jomo-Kogen ~1h15, local to Minakami, then ~30 min by car.
Joetsu Shinkansen Niigata->Jomo-Kogen ~40 min, then ~30 min by car via Minakami.

inns.name: Tamakiya
inns.summary: Tamakiya is an eight-room food-and-sake auberge in snowbound Matsunoyama, built on chef Akira Kuriyama's terroir French and the owner-sommelier's sake pairings, with in-room source-fed saline baths, though rooms run small for the price. The restaurant holds a Michelin star from the 2020 Niigata guide. Ikyu guests praise the pairing and the solo-friendly hosting while marking food and rooms softer, and the solo fallback shabu-shabu course divides them. You stay here for the kitchen.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is chef Akira Kuriyama's French cooking from Niigata ingredients, and the restaurant holds a Michelin star from the 2020 Niigata guide. The owner pairs sake to each course, and the pairing is what Ikyu guests praise most, for labels they would never have picked themselves. The French course needs two or more diners, so solo guests get pork shabu-shabu, on which opinion splits. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.58.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The spring is ancient seawater, salty and counted among Japan's three great medicinal waters, and Ikyu guests praise its quality and go back in several times a stay; they put the bath at 4.92. Six of the eight rooms have a private source-fed semi-open-air bath. There is a sauna, and the communal bath bans tattoos, so book a room with its own bath.

service.label: Service
service.text: Ikyu guests put service at 4.92, their highest mark here, and what recurs in the reviews is that solo guests are looked after as attentively as groups and that the inn runs a free lounge with massage chairs, drinks and sweets, remarkable for eight rooms. The owner works the dining room himself, choosing the sake for each course and talking it through at the table, and guests who mention him are as warm about the conversation as about the pour.

room.label: Room
room.text: The eight rooms are clean and easy to use, and six have their own semi-open-air bath fed from the source, so book one of those six, because the water is what guests praise most about the place. The rooms themselves run small for the price, and Ikyu guests put them at 4.54, the lowest mark they give the inn.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Matsunoyama Onsen sits deep in the mountains of Tokamachi in Niigata, one of the snowiest towns in Japan, and the resort itself is a small cluster of inns of the kind the Japanese call a hidden hot spring, buried in snow through the winter.

cities.text: Jōetsu Shinkansen Tokyo→Echigo-Yuzawa (~75 min), JR Jōetsu line→Muikamachi (~22 min), Hokuhoku line→Matsudai (~24 min), then the ~20-min inn shuttle. ⚠ The Hokuhoku locals run ~hourly (all-stops since 2023) — budget 3h if a connection slips.

Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Jōetsumyōkō (~64 min), Hokuhoku line toward Matsudai (~55–65 min, one change, sparse), then the ~20-min inn shuttle. Confirm the day's Jōetsumyōkō→Matsudai connection at booking — frequency is the binding constraint.

inns.name: The Hiramatsu Karuizawa Miyota
inns.summary: The Hiramatsu Karuizawa Miyota is a French auberge that opened in 2021 at the foot of Mt. Asama near Karuizawa, built around the food pedigree of Hiramatsu's Tokyo restaurant and an in-room onsen bath in every room (the water is brought in from Ueda). It holds two Michelin Keys, one of only 20 hotels in Japan with that many. Nobody in the FlyerTalk thread has stayed, but Ikyu guests are vocal at 4.7 over 137 reviews, praising the rooms, the bathing and the staff, while the kitchen, which the property is built around, draws the sharpest complaints.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The place is built around its dinner, a grand French and Italian auberge kitchen on Shinshu produce. Head chef Shigeo Yanagihara trained in the Paul Bocuse lineage and buys from roughly 40 local producers, from orchards to game hunters. Ikyu guests are divided over the result, and while some find the cooking well above what an onsen ryokan serves, dinner draws the most complaints here, and food is the lowest of the Ikyu marks at 4.55.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own semi-open-air hot-spring bath, and the water is real onsen, trucked in daily from Ueda because nothing rises on site, which also makes tattoos a non-issue. Ikyu guests praise the in-room bath and the highland air on the verandah while you soak, and they put the bathing at 4.74.

service.label: Service
service.text: The Hiramatsu group runs the hotel as a French auberge, so the hospitality is a restaurant house's kind, and Ikyu guests describe warm, attentive staff from arrival to send-off, with the dining room's course explanations and the sommelier drawing particular praise. Michelin gave the hotel two Keys in October 2025, one of only 20 hotels in Japan at that level. Service is still marked below the rooms and the bath on Ikyu, at 4.62.

room.label: Room
room.text: There are 37 rooms and villas, all opened in 2021, in a contemporary style with floor-to-ceiling glass and Mt. Asama filling the windows, and each has its own semi-open-air hot-spring bath. Guests praise the size, the cleanliness, the view and the amenities, and even guests who disliked dinner call the rooms spacious. Ikyu guests put rooms and facilities at 4.79, their highest marks here.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The hotel stands at the foot of Mt. Asama in Miyota, one town west of Karuizawa, a highland resort where you can see a long way and the air on the verandah is a pleasure. The snow is light and dry on this Pacific side, which makes it a refined wind-down and no deep-snow finale. In the evening there is the TAKIBI bonfire lounge with marshmallow roasting.

cities.text: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Asama' Tokyo→Karuizawa (~1h06–1h16), then ~15 min by taxi (free hotel pickup) — the easiest access on the whole corridor. For the Hiramatsu (Miyota), ride one stop on to Sakudaira + a ~20-min taxi (~1.9h total).
Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Hakutaka' Kanazawa→Karuizawa direct (~1h50; the faster 'Kagayaki' skips Karuizawa), then ~15 min by taxi. The Hiramatsu adds ~15–20 min to Miyota via Sakudaira (~2.4h).

inns.name: The Hiramatsu Kashikojima
inns.summary: The Hiramatsu group's original auberge (2016) has eight rooms over Ago Bay with in-room onsen and a serious French kitchen, which on food alone would outcook Yusura, the other Ise inn. It has held one Michelin Key for two straight years, 2024 and 2025. Ikyu guests are enthusiastic and specific, 4.77 over 27 reviews, with the food their highest mark; the only recurring gripe is the silent shuttle driver.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The kitchen is French, an auberge menu built on Ise lobster, abalone and Matsusaka beef, and it is what Ikyu guests praise most, at 4.89. Dinner and breakfast both draw praise across the reviews, and the sauces are elaborate, which most guests love and which is the one point where taste divides.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The water is real onsen from the Okushima-Hamashima source, and every room has its own onsen bath, with a private open-air bath you reserve as well. Ikyu guests find both good, though the bath is the lowest of the marks they give here, at 4.63, and the reserved open-air bath, a walk over from the main building, is where the complaints come in.

service.label: Service
service.text: Ikyu guests put service at 4.78 and describe care that starts before arrival, with transfers and special requests arranged in advance, smart service at table and a strong regard for privacy. The recurring complaint is the shuttle driver, who says nothing and does not offer to take the bags.

room.label: Room
room.text: The house was purpose-built in 2016, and all eight rooms look over Ago Bay and have their own onsen bath. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.81 and describe them as beautiful and well designed, a comfortable size with the bay in view.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn sits on Ago Bay in Ise-Shima, and the view from the lounge and the rooms is the pearl-raft water of the bay, which Ikyu guests call spectacular. The quiet recurs in review after review, and it is possible to go a whole stay without seeing other guests.

cities.text: Reverse of: Kintetsu Ltd Exp Iseshi/Ujiyamada→Kyoto (~2h); most change at Yamato-Yagi, a few run direct (2/hr).
Reverse of: Kintetsu Limited Express Ujiyamada/Iseshi→Kintetsu-Nagoya (~80–85 min, direct).

inns.name: The Hiramatsu Sengokuhara
inns.summary: A 20-room Hiramatsu auberge in Sengokuhara where every room has a private Ōwakudani-source onsen bath and dinner is a full Italian course, a Western kitchen that is welcome after a run of kaiseki nights. It holds one Michelin Key, its second straight year with one. Ikyu guests love it overall (4.77 across 98 reviews), with portion size the one complaint that recurs.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a full Italian course, and most Ikyu guests find it superb, with the food at 4.7 across their reviews. The dining room seats families apart from couples. The complaint that recurs in the critical reviews is portion size, with small courses at dinner and a modest breakfast.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own half-open-air bath, and the water is real onsen, kakenagashi from the Ōwakudani source, so hot that guests add cold water before they can get in. There is also a private bath to reserve, booked at check-in, so arrive early for a good slot. Ikyu guests give the bath 4.78, in line with their other marks here.

service.label: Service
service.text: At check-in the dinner and breakfast menus are handed to every guest and gone through ingredient by ingredient, with changes made willingly. Staff keep the right distance, and Ikyu guests give the service 4.79, with the faults in the reviews limited to small things like the fitness room's hours, now 8 to 8.

room.label: Room
room.text: Twenty modern auberge rooms, spacious and clean, with a huge two-person tub built into the room itself so it is easy to slip into, Bulgari toiletries, a well-chosen Gabbeh rug and a free minibar, and Ikyu guests give the rooms their highest mark here at 4.82. The quibbles in the reviews are small ones about the bathroom fittings.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Sengokuhara is the quieter, grassy-highland corner of Hakone, and on clear days Mount Fuji shows from the room. The car park is a wide flat lot at the door.

cities.text: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), Tozan railway→Kōwakudani (~35 min), 5-min inn shuttle (reserve).

Reverse of: Direct Tozan BUS Gōra/Sengokuhara→Odawara (~45 min — one seat; Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen→Kyoto (~1h50 on the ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari'; 'Kodama'+change or ~2h40 all-Kodama otherwise).

Midōsuji hop Umeda→Shin-Osaka, Tōkaidō 'Hikari' Shin-Osaka→Odawara (~2h05 — the same ~2-hourly Odawara-calling 'Hikari' the hakone>kyoto leg uses at ~1h50 to Kyoto, plus the ~15-min Kyoto–Shin-Osaka segment; 'Nozomi' skips Odawara and all-'Kodama' is ~2h40), then the direct Tozan BUS Odawara→Gōra/Sengokuhara (~45 min, one seat; the Tozan rail adds a Hakone-Yumoto change).

inns.name: Tobira Onsen Myojinkan
inns.summary: A single inn standing alone at 1,050 m in the Tobira Onsen canyon above Matsumoto, known for its standing bath over the canyon, with real onsen water in the rooms and a choice of two kitchens that sidesteps kaiseki fatigue. It has been a Relais & Châteaux member since 2008. The crowd adores it (TripAdvisor #1 in Matsumoto, Ikyu 4.56 across 166 reviews), but the reviews are mixed, with the food and the rooms the softest of the Ikyu marks and the service the best. KI-NRT stayed 20-odd years ago and found it pretty good.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: You choose between two kitchens, organic French at SAI and modern Japanese at TOBIRA, both built on Shinshu farm-to-table produce, and Ikyu guests who write about the food mostly call the local cooking delicious. Food is nonetheless the softest of the Ikyu marks at 4.51, and what complaints there are come from the Japanese dining room.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The water is real Tobira Onsen, and there are three baths, the main bath, the lying bath and the famous half-open-air standing bath over the canyon stream, which Ikyu guests single out above the other two. Not all rooms have onsen, as KI-NRT notes. Ikyu guests put the bath at 4.61.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is the best of the Ikyu marks at 4.67, at about the level of an international hotel, with staff who talk with you beyond serving the plates, and a dedicated shuttle from Matsumoto makes the remote spot easy. Myojinkan has been a Relais & Châteaux member since 2008, re-audited by a mystery guest every three years. With 39 rooms and two dining rooms (SAI and TOBIRA) it is a big house, and the weaker Ikyu reviews find the care uneven.

room.label: Room
room.text: Around 40 rooms make this a resort-sized inn (KI-NRT calls the 39-room footprint rather large, though it makes availability easier to find), and not every room has onsen; some have a private open-air hot-spring bath. The rooms are among the softer Ikyu marks at 4.54, and guests describe interiors that show their age in places.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn stands alone at 1,050 m in the Tobira Onsen canyon above Matsumoto, a single house in the mountains that Ikyu guests describe as healing and as a place to reset, with the sound of the stream and birdsong around the bath. If you drive, the last 7 km or so of road are narrow with no room to pass, so leave the large car at home. Matsumoto is close enough for a day at the castle, which KI-NRT calls a must.

cities.text: JR Ltd Exp 'Azusa' Shinjuku→Matsumoto (~2h35), then Myōjinkan's shuttle (~35–45 min, reserve) or a taxi (~30 min). A Chūō-line spur off the north loop.

Reverse of: ~35–45-min inn shuttle to Matsumoto, JR Ltd Exp 'Shinano'→Nagano (~50 min), change to Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki'/'Hakutaka' Nagano→Kanazawa (~65–70 min). One change at Nagano — cleaner than the Shinano→Nagoya→Kanazawa alternative.
Reverse of: Inn shuttle to Matsumoto, JR Ltd Exp 'Shinano' Matsumoto→Nagoya (~2h05, through the Kiso valley), then Tōkaidō Shinkansen Nagoya→Kyoto (~35 min) — the natural pivot west.

inns.name: Tsuruko
inns.summary: Tsuruko is the venerable Kanazawa kaiseki house, reopened in November 2025 as a four-suite auberge in the Takaoka-machi teahouse quarter, where each suite has its own in-room open-air onsen and the restaurant's cooking is served to order in the room, and a detached 'Jihaku' annex adds a private kappo counter. Ikyu guests give it 4.87 across 23 stays, with the meals and the bathing their highest marks, and a Michelin one-star Sushi Jin collaboration runs some nights. Nobody in the thread has stayed yet, though KI-NRT names it with Asadaya as the top ryokan option near the center of Kanazawa.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is the Kaga kaiseki of the old Tsuruko restaurant, cooked to order and served in your suite, and some nights a Michelin one-star Sushi Jin chef takes the counter. KI-NRT has heard the food is incredible, and while crab is a big part of the menu he doubts it is 95% crab like some Hokuriku houses. Ikyu guests mark the cooking their highest mark, near 4.9, and repeat guests single out the meals and the counter breakfast by the open kitchen.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every suite has its own in-room open-air bath drawn from hot spring, which is rare in Kanazawa (KI-NRT says few if any of the city's properties have onsen, and Asadaya's bath is not hot spring), and the Koju suite adds a private sauna. There is no communal bathhouse. Ikyu guests put the bathing near the top of their marks, level with the cooking.

service.label: Service
service.text: Tsuruko is a four-suite house where the owner talks Kanazawa proverbs, local ingredients and sightseeing over breakfast at the counter, and the staff explain each dish and the sake, which Ikyu guests call perfect. They mark hospitality 4.87, and the intimacy and anticipatory care recur across reviews.

room.label: Room
room.text: The four suites run over 90 square metres each, with a bedroom, a living room and a dining area set around a counter that resembles the original Tsuruko restaurant, in Kanazawa's Takaoka-machi teahouse quarter, and a detached 'Jihaku' annex has its own kappo counter; everything was renovated in 2025. Ikyu guests praise the space and calm, and the rooms are among their higher marks at 4.83.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Tsuruko sits in the Takaoka-machi teahouse district of central Kanazawa, an easy walk from Kanazawa Castle, though KI-NRT puts Kenrokuen and the Higashi Chaya geisha quarter at more like a 30-minute brisk walk. It is a machiya-quarter address built around its own kaiseki restaurant, with no hot-spring town around it. Like most Kanazawa ryokans it has no big garden, but Kenrokuen is close and extremely photogenic under January and February snow.

cities.text: Hokuriku Shinkansen 'Kagayaki' direct Tokyo→Kanazawa (~2h28).
Reverse of: Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa→Tsuruga (~50 min), change to Thunderbird Ltd Exp→Kyoto (post-2024 routing). Snow-risk in January.

Ltd Exp 'Thunderbird' Osaka Stn→Tsuruga (~1h20), ~10-min change at Tsuruga, Hokuriku Shinkansen Tsuruga→Kanazawa (~40 min) — ~2h10–2h30 station to station. Departs central Osaka, so there is no Shin-Osaka hop; the Tsuruga change is the one the Mar 2024 extension imposed (the one-seat Thunderbird to Kanazawa is gone). ⚠ January snow on the Hokuriku coast delays this corridor.

Reverse of: West then south by air, no Tokyo backtrack: airport bus Kanazawa Station→Komatsu Airport (~40–50 min), a frequent ANA/Oriental Air Bridge hop KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40, ~4 daily), then the subway 2 stops into Hakata/Tenjin (~5 min). ~3.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: Airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then the Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen relay Hakata→Nagasaki via Takeo-Onsen (~2h). ~5.75h door-to-door.
Reverse of: Fly to Kyushu then south: airport bus Kanazawa→Komatsu + KMQ→Fukuoka (~1h40) into Hakata, then Kyushu Shinkansen 'Mizuho' Hakata→Kagoshima-Chūō (~1h17). ~5.25h door-to-door.

inns.name: Ubuya
inns.summary: Kozantei Ubuya has the best Fuji view of any ryokan on Lake Kawaguchi, at $480–770 a night, a real saving over Fufu, and KI-NRT calls the property itself solid but not on the level of Fufu. Rakuten guests are consistently warm, putting it at 4.36 over 717 reviews with the lake-and-Fuji location their highest mark at 4.79 and the buffet dinner their lowest at 4.0. The view sets it apart, and everything else about the stay is solid without being a showstopper.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: KI-NRT has heard that the food isn't amazing, merely very good, though he has not eaten here himself. Rakuten guests put dinner and breakfast at the bottom of their marks (4.0 and 4.07 out of 5), and while several of them call the meals tasty, the buffet dinner is where the crowd is least impressed, and breakfast comes out only a little better than dinner.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Special Suite #501 has an open-air onsen bath on its own deck, and friends of KI-NRT who stayed there loved it. Several other rooms also have an open-air bath facing Mt. Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi, and Rakuten guests give the bath 4.54 out of 5, several of them singling out those in-room baths with the mountain in front of them.

service.label: Service
service.text: Nobody in the thread has written about the service here. Rakuten guests consistently describe courteous, considerate staff, and the crowd puts service at 4.43 out of 5.

room.label: Room
room.text: Several rooms have their own open-air bath looking over the lake to Mt. Fuji, and KI-NRT's advice is to stretch for one of the Tokubetsu-shitsu (Special) rooms if you can, and still save a pretty penny over Fufu. He has not stayed himself and puts the property below Fufu and the top Hakone ryokans in overall quality. Rakuten guests put the rooms at 4.57 and single out the rooms with a lake-view open-air bath.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Ubuya sits right on Lake Kawaguchi with an unobstructed, picture-perfect view of Mt. Fuji across the water, the best Fuji view of any ryokan in Kawaguchiko, and KI-NRT confirms that the picture on the website really is how the mountain looks on a clear day. Rakuten guests put the location at 4.79, their highest mark, with repeated praise for the lake-view welcome lounge.

cities.text: Reverse of: JR 'Fuji Excursion' Ltd Exp Kawaguchiko→Shinjuku direct (~2h, ~4/day). Miss it → Fujikyu→Ōtsuki + Chūō Ltd Exp = ~2h25, 1 change.

Round the south side of Fuji rather than back through Tokyo: Fujikyu 'Mishima·Kawaguchiko Liner' bus Kawaguchiko→Mishima (~1h30–1h40, roughly hourly, ¥2,700 — japan-guide, Oct 2025), one change at Mishima, then the Tōkaidō Shinkansen Mishima→Kyoto (~1h51 on a Hikari that calls at Mishima, ~2h27 on the all-stations Kodama — ekitan). ~4h15 door-to-door with the inn shuttle and the change. (Via Tokyo — 'Fuji Excursion'→Shinjuku, cross to Tokyo Station, 'Nozomi'→Kyoto — is ~4h30 and two changes, and the Fuji Excursion runs only ~4/day.)

inns.name: Ujo Soan
inns.summary: Ujo Soan is a six-room hideaway at Yuhigaura on Kyoto's Tango coast, with detached rooms that each have a private open-air onsen bath, winter snow-crab on the table and the sunset beach below. Ikyu guests rate it 4.79 across a modest 36 reviews and call the hospitality worth the premium, though softer notes flag a possible chef change and bath water that is trucked in and circulated instead of piped straight from the source. Nobody in the thread has stayed, so you book on the concept and the crowd's warmth.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is built around the Tango coast's winter snow-crab and is served in private dining rooms, which KI-NRT notes as an advantage over Sumihei's semi-private ones. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.75, though the more critical reviews find the meals below the price and mention a chef change.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every room has its own open-air onsen bath, the larger Soke house adds a mist sauna, and there are free-use private baths plus a large communal bath, which KI-NRT notes Sumihei lacks. The water is not piped from the spring. It is trucked in, circulated, heated and sterilized, as at Sumihei. Ikyu guests put the bath at 4.78, in line with their other marks.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is what Ikyu guests praise most, at 4.83, and the warmest reviews single out the room attendants, who notice what a particular guest needs and act on it without being asked, and several reviewers are regulars who come back for exactly that. The critical reviews, a minority, fault lapses in basic follow-through between staff and the manner of newer hires, below what the price promises.

room.label: Room
room.text: The six rooms are five detached villa-style units plus the larger Soke house, each with its own open-air onsen bath, and check-in is 2 PM with check-out at 11 AM, an hour longer at each end than Sumihei, as KI-NRT notes. Guests under 13 are not accepted. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.72, the softest of their marks.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Ujo Soan stands at Yuhigaura Onsen on the Sea of Japan coast of Kyoto's Tango peninsula, the same peninsula as Taiza Onsen Sumihei, and the view is the long sunset beach the resort is known for. The detached rooms are wrapped in bamboo and greenery, and the lounge in the annex building looks out over the coast. January brings heavy snow.

cities.text: Ltd Exp 'Hashidate' Kyoto→Amino direct (~2h30). Snow-risk in January.
Reverse of: Amino→Kyoto (~2h30) + Shinkansen→Tokyo (~2h15) — a full travel day.

inns.name: Wasure no Sato Gajoen
inns.summary: Gajoen is the Myoken Onsen ryokan credited with first putting hot-spring flow-through private open-air baths into guest rooms, opening in 1970 in a Kagoshima gorge where hot springs steam from the rocks. The thread knows it almost entirely by reputation, since the one member who stayed, about nine years ago, found it amazing but cautions it may have changed since. Ikyu guests give it 4.67 across 31 reviews, praising the local cooking and the warm staff, though the weakest reviews flag steep stairs.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: The cooking is local. Repeat visitors on Ikyu praise dishes built on local vegetables and local seasoning, beautiful to look at and gentle on the body, and small onigiri are handed over for the train home. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.71, though the two weakest reviews both fault the breakfast.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Gajoen is credited as the first ryokan to put hot-spring flow-through open-air baths into its guest rooms, and it opened in 1970 in Myoken Onsen, where hot springs gush from the riverside rock. The room baths are source-fed, and there are private baths too, including the Takeyu and a cool carbonated 'ramune' bath, though the weakest Ikyu reviews flag steep, narrow stairs on the way to them. Ikyu guests put the baths at 4.68.

service.label: Service
service.text: Warm staff are what repeat visitors single out, and the warmest reviews come from guests on their second or third stay who say they want to come back every year; departing guests get a small bouquet to take home. Ikyu guests give service their highest mark, 4.84, well ahead of the rooms and facilities. The two weakest reviews both warn that the many steps and steep, narrow stairs make it hard going for anyone with weak knees.

room.label: Room
room.text: The guest buildings have thatched roofs and earthen walls that merge with the greenery, and the Kaze room has a fully open, sudare-screened terrace that fills the room with the green outside. Rooms are split between the older-style buildings and the newer Sora building, and they have an open-air bath and a daybed. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.55, their lowest mark.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The ryokan sits on the Amori River in Myoken Onsen, Kagoshima, in a gorge where hot springs gush from hollow orange rock, and KI-NRT has seen it from the footbath at Myoken Ishiharaso directly across the river; he suggests pairing the two, and says Sakurajima is worth visiting on a clear day. Repeat visitors on Ikyu give the sound of the river and the surrounding nature as reasons they keep coming back.

cities.text: Shinkansen Hakata to Kagoshima-Chuo, then ~15 min car from Kagoshima Airport area to the inn.
~15 min by car from Kagoshima Airport to the inn.

inns.name: Yagyu no Sho
inns.summary: A 15-room sukiya-zukuri classic in Shuzenji, a few lanes from Asaba, grown from a 1959 Kyoto-kaiseki ryotei. Every room has its own free-flowing onsen, open-air in six of them, which is the strongest in-room bathing in Shuzenji. Thread glimpses are warm (one member, back for a second stay, still calls it an excellent pick), and Ikyu guests give it 4.72 over 34 reviews but split sharply: the regulars rank it with the best in Japan, while others found the service rigid for the price.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: Dinner is a Kyoto-style kaiseki served in your room (the house grew out of a 1959 Kyoto ryotei), and KI-NRT calls the cuisine sublime; at Ufufu down the road, by contrast, meals are counter dining. Head chef Kanda's menu follows the seasons, and a salon serves brandy and grappa after dinner. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.85, repeat guests say the kaiseki is what brings them back, and praise for the kitchen runs through otherwise divided reviews.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: Every one of the 15 rooms has its own free-flowing onsen, and in four rooms and the two detached villas the bath is open-air; KI-NRT names in-room onsen in every room as one of the things it shares with Ufufu down the road. Ikyu guests put the bath at 4.91, the highest mark they give the inn.

service.label: Service
service.text: EK017, back for a second stay in 2025, had an attendant who was very warm, friendly and helpful and took care of everything, and the Ikyu regulars call the service first-class. Ikyu guests put service at 4.68, but two 2025 reviews go the other way and find it rigid and just ordinary for a top-class price.

room.label: Room
room.text: The 15 rooms are sukiya-style, and KI-NRT calls it a very traditional ryokan, for better or for worse. Ikyu guests put the rooms at 4.53, one of their lower marks for the inn, though the regulars admire the traditional craftsmanship of the rooms. EK017's room Meigetsu had a dining table and real chairs instead of floor cushions.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: Yagyu no Sho stands in the Shuzenji onsen village a few lanes from Asaba, wrapped in the bamboo garden it is named for. It is quiet, with little contact with other guests. EK017 enjoyed the gift shop, full of local paper crafts (the area is well known for its paper), and the inn features in an English coffee-table book of renowned ryokans that KI-NRT praises.

cities.text: 'Kodama'/'Hikari' Tokyo→Mishima (~45-55 min, every ~30 min), then the flat-rate cab into the Shuzenji valley (~40-50 min, book with the room). No self-handled change. Rail alt: Izuhakone Sunzu line→Shuzenji (~35 min) + short taxi, +1 change.

Reverse of: The inn-bookable flat-rate cab Shuzenji valley→Mishima (~40-50 min; Asaba ¥12-15k, book with the room — Asaba runs NO shuttle), then the direct Mishima-calling 'Hikari'→Kyoto (1h50, ~2-hourly, dep Mishima :58 — reserve; hourly 'Kodama'+change fallback). No self-handled change. Rail alt: Sunzu line→Mishima (~35 min), +1 change.

inns.name: Zagyosoh (ABBA Resorts Izu)
inns.summary: A 50-year Ryokan Collection resort in Izukōgen forest whose three kitchens (kaiseki, a French restaurant and a teppanyaki counter) let you vary dinner without leaving the grounds, which directly answers kaiseki fatigue. Ikyu guests give it 4.55 overall and praise the villas, the six bath types and the French cooking, but service is the recurring weak point, with disorganized arrivals and check-ins. Book a villa over a main-building room, and expect some friction.

cuisine.label: Food
cuisine.text: There are three kitchens, kaiseki, a French restaurant and a teppanyaki counter, so you can eat differently each night without leaving the grounds. Ikyu guests put the food at 4.7 and praise the French menu most, with the washoku close behind. Room drinks are all-inclusive and the Häagen-Dazs is free.

onsen.label: Bath
onsen.text: The water comes from the Ukiyama spring source and there are six kinds of bath, from in-room onsen in the villas (the dog-friendly villa has a spacious open-air bath beside a reflecting pool) to two garden open-air baths and rental baths. The inn lists two large baths, each with a sauna, but the main bath is gone for now, and the garden rotenburo Aoi has no roof.

service.label: Service
service.text: Service is the weak point in the Ikyu reviews, at 4.33 against 4.77 for the rooms. The recurring complaints are disorganized arrivals and check-ins, staff who wait to be asked, and a level of care that the unhappy guests measure against the bill and find wanting.

room.label: Room
room.text: The modern villas are the rooms to book, and Ikyu guests give them the highest marks of anything here. The dog-friendly villa has its own spacious open-air bath and a reflecting pool lit at night. The main-building rooms are Shōwa-era and dated beside the villas. The top maisonette pool villa has a pool that takes hours to heat.

setting.label: Place
setting.text: The inn sits on 6,000 tsubo of national-park forest at Izukōgen, a large wooded resort compound. On a clear morning a short walk from the grounds gives views out to Izu Ōshima and Toshima.

cities.text: JR Ltd Exp 'Odoriko' Tokyo→Izu-Kōgen (~2h, one seat) — or Shinkansen Tokyo→Atami (~40 min) + Izukyū Line — then the inn's free shuttle (~6–15 min, reserve).
Reverse of: Izukyū Izu-Kōgen→Atami (~50 min), then 'Hikari' Atami→Kyoto (~2h; 'Nozomi' skips Atami).
